that order with **nothing extra alive** -- so any construct that buys the
order by keeping a value live is the wrong shape however close it gets, and
what you are looking for is a spelling that reorders the first references
without adding a live range.

## A `u16` subscript's `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0xf` is a MERGED insn, and the base `ldr` lands relative to it by statement (wave 48, W48-I)

Reading a `u16` local and using it to subscript a `u16` array produces three
shifts — `lsl #16`, `lsr #16` (the truncation) and `lsl #1` (the scale) — which
combine merges into `lsl #16; lsr #15`. **The merged insn takes the position of
the LATER of the two it consumed**, so which statement holds the `* 2` decides
where the array's base `ldr` sits. All four measured on `sub_08049F24`
(140 B, MATCHED), which needs the base `ldr` AFTER both shifts:

| spelling | base `ldr` lands |
| --- | --- |
| `u16 t; t = …;` then `&arr[t]` | BETWEEN the two shifts (96.4%) |
| `u32 t; t = …;` then `&arr[(u16)t]` | BEFORE both shifts (95.0%) |
| whole chain inline in the call | base hoisted to a callee-saved reg ahead of the calls |
| `off = t * 2;` its own statement, base added as `u8 *` | AFTER both — the ROM |

`arr + t` and `t + arr` are byte-identical to `&arr[t]`: **reversing the
pointer and integer operands of a pointer addition changes nothing**, so do not
spend an attempt on it.

## NOT binding a VALUE to a local is a lever, and it is the exact inverse of "binding locals are punctuation" (wave 49, W49-A)

The wave-17 rule says a value assigned in N consecutive statements is ONE pseudo
whose live range spans all N, so splitting one local into N frees a register.
The mirror image is just as usable and came up three times in one batch: **a
value the original left as a repeated INLINE EXPRESSION becomes one long-lived
pseudo the moment you name it, and that single change moves registers, spills
and instruction counts.** Write the expression out at each use and agbcc's CSE
folds the reads that are cheap to fold and re-emits the ones that are not —
which is what the ROM does.

Three distinct diffs in `sub_0805A388`, each fixed by deleting a local:

- **A named local suppresses a reload the ROM has.** `n = *cell;` then using
  `n` three times keeps the byte in one pseudo. Writing `*cell` three times
  lets CSE fold the first two (same block) and RELOAD the third after the
  register is needed for a pool address — the ROM's second `ldrb`. Naming it is
  2 bytes short and no allocation lever recovers them.
- **A named local dies at its last use, so agbcc masks IN PLACE.** `terrain`
  as a local gives `ands r2,r0` (2-operand, dest = the dying local). Written
  inline it stays a CSE temp that must survive, so each mask goes to a fresh
  register: `ands r0,r2`. Same length, different bytes.
- **Both together are what set the FRAME SIZE.** Keeping the two values inline
  raised pressure enough to spill `flag` to the stack (frame 0xc, not 0x8) and
  to push the out-pointer behind the cell pointer in the register order. With
  either one bound the function is size-exact with r5/r6 swapped throughout.

**The converse still holds and must not be over-applied: a base-plus-constant
POINTER must be bound.** `q + 0x12 + off` as one expression reassociates to
`(off + 0x12) + q`; `props = q + 0x12; props[off]` does not. Same for
`rows = q + 0x417a` and `cells = q + 0x1432`. And binding an array base
early is still the way to order its pool word (`tbl = gUnknown_0857685A;`
ahead of the 0x1432 constant). **So the rule is by KIND: bind addresses, do not
bind values.**

One more, from `sub_0805A0EC`: **an intermediate that the ROM RECOMPUTES from a
kept pointer must stay inline at the recompute site even when it is bound
elsewhere.** There `off` is bound (that is what orders the 0x1432 load after
the `ldrh`), but the late use is written longhand as `props[*(u16 *)rowp + x]`,
and agbcc rebuilds it from the `ip`-resident row pointer exactly as the ROM
does. Binding it at both sites keeps it live and deletes the recompute.

## Two disjoint counters in one function are usually ONE local, and it is worth a register (wave 49, W49-K)

A function with a setup loop, a nested map walk and a wrap-up loop reads as
three counters, and declaring three is the obvious thing. It is wrong twice in
one batch, and both times the whole residual was the same shape: the counter and
some other pseudo swap hard registers, costing 2--4 bytes in `mov rLO, ip` /
`mov ip, rLO` copies while every instruction stays otherwise identical.

- `sub_08021810`: declared `u8 i, x, y` with `i` running the 6-byte clear loop
  and the 5-element max loop and `x` the inner map loop. +4 bytes: the ROM keeps
  `x` in `r3` and the `y * 2` temp in `r4`, the candidate had them swapped, and
  the pool address needed an extra `mov r0, ip` to be loaded through. Deleting
  `i` and running all three loops on `x` matched byte-for-byte.
- `sub_080219AC`: declared `int i, n, x, y` with `i` running the 5-army reset
  loop. +4 bytes: `x` landed in `ip` and `&gUnknown_08499590`'s pool address in
  `r6`, the ROM has them the other way round. Same fix, same result.

The mechanism is the tie-break the register chapter already describes. Locals
get their pseudos at `expand_decl` time in DECLARATION order, so every local
outranks every later temporary; between two locals the priority is roughly
frequency over live length. Folding the setup loop's counter into the map
loop's variable does not lengthen its live range (the ranges are disjoint) but
it does add the setup loop's references to the same allocno, and that is enough
to move it ahead of the address constant it was tying with.

Read backwards this is a cheap diagnostic. **If your only residual is one pseudo
in `ip` where the ROM has it in a low register (or the reverse), and the
function has more counted loops than it has counters in the ROM's register file,
merge the counters before you touch anything else.** It is the exact inverse of
the wave-17 "binding locals are punctuation, one per statement" rule, which
splits a local into N: that rule is about a value recomputed inside each
statement, this one about a counter whose loops never overlap.

## A wrap-around `(x + n - 1) % n` must BIND its delta, and the two `movs rD,#0` before a loop guard read out the comma init (wave 49, W49-L)

Two independent readouts off one function, `sub_080660BC` — a cursor that steps
`gUnknown_08580934->unk11[]` up or down with the usual no-negative-modulo idiom.

**1. `fold` reassociates the delta out of existence, so the CSE never forms.**
The ROM is `subs rD, rN, #1` (the delta, computed once) then
`adds r0, rOLD, rD`, and it keeps that delta live across a whole loop to reuse
it in a second modulo. Every inline spelling loses it:

```c
(x + (n - 1)) % n      ->  subs rX,#1 ; adds rX,rX,rN     /* (x - 1) + n */
(x + n - 1) % n        ->  same -- the parse differs, fold does not
```

`fold`'s `split_tree`/`associate_trees` pulls the constant out of the inner
`MINUS_EXPR` and re-attaches it to the *other* operand, so what reaches RTL is
`(x + (-1)) + n` and there is no `n - 1` value for CSE to share with the second
site. Binding it — `step = n - 1;` as its own statement, then `(x + step) % n`
at both sites — restores the ROM's shape exactly, and is worth 1 instruction
plus the register assignment of `n` itself (`n` moved from `r5` to the ROM's
`r6` the moment the binding appeared). This is the general `fold` reassociation
rule already in this file, but the *symptom* is unusual and worth naming: a
delta that the ROM computes once and you compute twice, in a function where
your instruction count is otherwise exact.

**2. Two `movs rD, #0` immediately before a loop guard are the loop counter and
an accumulator, and their ORDER is the comma init.** The ROM:

```
movs r2, #0          @ i
movs r3, #0          @ same
cmp  r3, r6          @ guard 0 < n, reusing the accumulator's zero
bge  .Lafter
```

Counter first, accumulator second. `acc = 0;` written as its own statement
before `for (i = 0; ...)` emits them the other way round — accumulator, then
counter — because gcc emits in source order and the `for` init comes last.
`for (i = 0, acc = 0; i < n; i++)` reverses it and matches. Both spellings are
size-identical and semantically identical, so this only shows up as a byte
diff; it is the cheapest possible readout of a comma init and it is the first
place to look when a loop preamble is two instructions out of order.

Note the guard itself is not a third statement: agbcc CSEs the accumulator's
freshly-stored zero and compares *that* register against the bound, which is
why the guard reads `cmp acc, n` rather than `cmp i, n`. Do not read the
register in the guard as the loop variable.

## `ldrsb` vs `ldrb; lsl #24; asr #24` is about the ADDRESS, not the signedness (wave 49, W49-A)

Wave 37 settled the halfword case: `sign_extend (mem:HI)` always folds to
`ldrsh`, so `ldrh; lsls; asrs` is never an `(s16)` cast. **The byte case is
different and the discriminator is the addressing mode, because THUMB `ldrsb`
has only a register-offset form.**

The same global, `gUnknown_03003340`, produces both spellings:

- `c_0805AD90.c` reads `(s8)gUnknown_03003340[y][x]` where the address is built
  and dies at the load — agbcc emits `ldrb r0,[r0]; lsls #24; asrs #24`,
  because using `ldrsb` would cost a materialised zero register it cannot
  amortise.
- `c_0805A744.c` binds the address (`cell = gUnknown_03003340[y] + x;`) and
  reads `*(s8 *)cell` twice — agbcc emits `movs r0,#0; ldrsb r0,[cell,r0]`,
  materialising the zero once and reusing the live pointer.

**Do not read an `ldrsb` as evidence that the array is signed.** In
`sub_0805A744` the `ldrsb` sits two instructions from a plain `ldrb` of the
SAME address supplying the stored value; the array is `u8` and the source has
an explicit `(s8 *)` cast on a bound pointer. ~~If you meet `ldrsb` where a
sibling function has `ldrb; lsl; asr`, the sibling did not bind the address —
that is the whole difference.~~

**CORRECTED, wave 53 (W53-E): that last sentence is WRONG, and binding is not
the discriminator for the byte case either. What decides it is whether a
scratch register is free to hold the zero index.** Two measurements, both from
matched functions:

- `sub_080591E4` and `sub_08059464` contain the SAME statement, character for
  character — `best = (s8)map->unk2D5A[map->unk417A[unk03] + unk02];`, no bound
  pointer in either — and it compiles to `movs r0,#0; ldrsb r0,[r2,r0]` in the
  first and `ldrb r0,[r0]; lsls #0x18; asrs #0x18` in the second. Both matched
  the ROM. In `sub_080591E4` the address landed in r2 and left r0 free for the
  invented zero; in `sub_08059464` the address landed in r0 and there was
  nothing spare to amortise.
- `sub_0805F7B8` gets `ldrsb` from an UNBOUND `(s8)gUnknown_03003340[y][x]`,
  the same expression `c_0805AD90.c` gets `ldrb; lsl; asr` from.

So the extension form carries **no source information at all** for bytes — not
about signedness, not about binding. Do not spend a round chasing it, and do
not add an `(s8 *)` cast to a candidate just because the ROM shows `ldrsb`;
fix whatever is contending for the register instead. (Binding the address is
still a real lever for something else — in `sub_0805F7B8` it is what splits the
address and the value into separate pseudos, which is a different fact and is
what makes the ROM's `adds r3,r0,#0` copy appear.)

**CORRECTED, wave 51 (W51-P): the halfword half of the opening sentence is
WRONG, and it is wrong for the same address-form reason the byte case is.**
`sub_08084700` reads `((s16)proc->unk4a >> 2) & 0xf` at three sites and agbcc
emits `ldrh r0,[r0]; lsls r0,#0x10; asrs r0,#0x12` at every one of them — the
cast IS in the source, and that spelling matched the ROM. THUMB `ldrsh`, like
`ldrsb`, has only a register-offset encoding, so once the member address has
been folded to a single register (`adds r0, #0x4a`, forced because 0x4a is past
the 5-bit scaled `ldrh` displacement) combine cannot match the `ldrsh` pattern
and leaves the shift pair behind.

The discriminator is WHICH PASS builds the load, and the same function shows
both halves:

- `proc->unk64` and `proc->unk6a` are DECLARED `s16`. The load is HImode-signed
  from the start, so the *expander* builds it and is free to invent the zero
  index register: `movs r1,#0; ldrsh r0,[r0,r1]`.
- `proc->unk4a` is declared `u16` and cast at the use. The load is built as
  HImode-unsigned and *combine* has to promote it, which it can only do if the
  address already has a register-offset form. It does not, so the shifts stay.

So: `ldrh; lsls #16; asrs #16` (or a merged `asrs #16+k`) IS reachable from an
`(s16)` cast on a `u16` member, and it does not tell you the member is signed.
Read the ADDRESS, not the extension — for halfwords exactly as for bytes.

## agbcc keeps a QImode/HImode LOCAL unextended and extends at the USE — so where the shifts land tells you the variable's TYPE (wave 51, W51-P)

`sub_080590DC` holds a best-so-far value in a register, initialised `0x78`,
compared against an `ldrsb` result and assigned from a `u8` array element. Two
spellings, and they put the SAME two shifts in opposite places:

- `s8 best;` — the store is bare (`ldrb r0,[r0]; mov r8,r0`) and the compare
  carries the extension (`mov r7,r8; lsls r0,r7,#24; asrs r0,r0,#24; cmp r1,r0`).
  agbcc's PROMOTE_MODE does NOT keep a QImode pseudo sign-extended; it truncates
  for free at the definition and pays at every read.
- `int best;` with an `s8` temporary in between (`t = arr[i][j]; best = t;`) —
  the extension moves to the definition (`ldrb r0,[r0]; lsls r0,#24;
  asrs r0,#24; mov r8,r0`) and the compare is a bare `cmp r0, r8`.

The ROM has the second shape. The measurement was 46.2% for the first spelling
and 56.1% for the second with no other change, and the same pairing decided
`sub_0805E2AC` (there the variable is `u16`, so the definition's shifts are
`lsls #16; lsrs #16` and the read carries an explicit `(s16)` cast's
`lsls #16; asrs #16`).

**Read it as a diagnostic:** shifts at the STORE and a bare compare means an
`int`/wider variable fed by a narrow temporary; a bare store and shifts at every
READ means the variable itself is `s8`/`s16`. Do not try to reach the first
shape by re-typing the variable — the temporary is what produces it, and it is
also what stops CSE folding the store's `ldrb` into the guard's `ldrsb`.

## OPERAND ORDER inside a commutative `|` decides which side is HOISTED and which register it gets — and it is NOT readable off the `orrs` (wave 51, W51-P)

Two functions in one batch turned on this, and in both the emitted `orrs` looks
the same whichever way the source is written, so the diff gives you no hint that
the order is the lever.

- `sub_080590DC` stores a packed pair inside a nested loop.
  `(u16)j | (i << 16)` leaves `i << 16` at the store site, recomputed every
  inner iteration (56.1%). `(i << 16) | (u16)j` gets `lsls r2, r2, #0x10`
  hoisted into the INNER preheader beside the loop's other two invariants
  (92.4%). Both spellings emit `orrs r0, r2` with `(u16)j` as the destination.
- `sub_08087A10` builds `0x400 | (i * 0xc + 0xb4) | ((i + 0xa) << 12)` and both
  non-constant terms are givs of the same loop. Written in that order the two
  givs land in sl and sb the wrong way round; written
  `0x400 | ((i + 0xa) << 12) | (i * 0xc + 0xb4)` they land the ROM's way and the
  function matched. The `mov r0, sl; orrs r2, r0; mov r1, sb; orrs r2, r1`
  sequence is byte-identical either way — only the constants in the preheader
  and in the increments move, four instructions apart from the `orrs`.

**So when a diff shows a preheader constant or a giv init on the wrong side, and
the arithmetic that consumes it is byte-identical, try transposing the operands
of the commutative operator that joins them before touching anything else.**
Corollary: a hoisted-vs-inline invariant inside a `|` is a two-line experiment,
not an allocation problem.

## A `/ 8` with NO round-toward-zero bias is still SIGNED — `lsrs` is the only unsigned tell (wave 49, W49-J)

`x / 8` on a signed `int` is normally three instructions, the wave-31 reading
c_080468D4.c records: `cmp #0; bge; adds #7` to bias the dividend, then one
shift. The standing shortcut has been "no bias, therefore unsigned". **It is
wrong**, and it cost an attempt on sub_08046778.

Controlled probe, one function, one operand changed:

```c
sub_08014B0C((a + gUnknown_084C211C[n * 2] * 8) / 8, ...)   /* a, table: u8 */
```

agbcc emits `adds r0, r3, r0` then **`asrs r0, r0, #3`** — the bias is gone but
the shift is arithmetic. Both operands are `u8`, so combine's `nonzero_bits`
proves the sum non-negative and `expand_divmod` drops the correction; it does
NOT change the expression's type, so the shift stays signed. The ROM has
`lsrs r0, r0, #3`, and only `(u32)(a + gUnknown_084C211C[n * 2] * 8) / 8`
produces it.

So there are THREE distinguishable spellings, not two:

| emitted | source |
| --- | --- |
| `cmp #0; bge; adds #7; asrs #3` | signed `/ 8`, range unknown (a plain `int` parameter) |
| `asrs #3` alone | signed `/ 8` on a provably non-negative expression |
| `lsrs #3` alone | the expression is UNSIGNED |

Read the SHIFT, not the bias. The bias only tells you whether combine had range
information, which is a property of how the operands were declared, not of the
divide. The same three-way split applies to the fused forms: sub_08046914's
`lsls #0xd; asrs #0x10` is `(s16)(v / 8)` and c_080468D4's `lsls #0xd;
lsrs #0x10` is `v / 8` truncated to u16 — the second shift carries the sign of
the *cast*, the first carries the divide.

## Two identical `i * K` in one call's arguments: agbcc CSEs them, the ROM often does not (wave 48, W48-I)

`sub_0801BD00(0x60, i * 16 + 16, blob, i * 16 | flag << 12)` compiles to ONE
`lsls rN, r4, #4` kept in a scratch plus a copy (`adds r1, r0, #0`); the ROM
emits `lsls r1, r4, #4; adds r1, #0x10` — modifying r1 in place, which destroys
the value — and then a SECOND `lsls r3, r4, #4`. Same instruction count, so the
size matches and only the registers differ, which reads like pure allocation and
is not.

Any spelling that makes the two multiplies different expressions restores it.
decomp-permuter's answer was a differently-typed copy of the counter
(`s16 j = i;` used in argument 2 only), which is byte-correct and almost
certainly not the original text but identifies the fact. `(i + 1) * 16` also
breaks the CSE, but agbcc then shares the `i + 1` with the loop's own increment
and the tail loses 2 bytes — the c_08048850.c `i * 2 + 2` finding seen from the
other side. **The two effects are in tension: the ROM can want the un-CSEd form
for the argument and the un-shared form for the increment at the same time.**

Related: a 0/1 flag folded into arithmetic must be its own local.
`((i == g) + 2) << 12` written inline lets agbcc fold both arms to constants
(`movs rD,#0xc0; lsls #6` / `movs rD,#0x80; lsls #6`) across an unconditional
`b`, +8 bytes. `sel = 0; if (i == g) sel = 1;` then `(sel + 2) << 12` gives the
ROM's arithmetic form. `(sel + 2) * 0x1000` and swapping the `|` operands are
both byte-identical to it.

## loop.c CAN hoist a global pointer's LOAD into the preheader — write the assignment INSIDE the loop body (wave 50, W50-L)

Both `sub_080378A8` and `sub_08037A78` want a global pointer read once per
outer iteration and held in a register across the inner loop, with the load
placed **after** the inner loop's entry guard, in the LICM preheader:

```
	movs r4, #0            @ x = 0
	cmp r4, r6
	bhs  ...               @ inner guard
	ldr r2, =gUnknown_03003F68
	ldr r5, [r2]           @ <-- the load, in the preheader
```

Writing `buf = gUnknown_03003F68;` in the OUTER loop's body (before the inner
`for`) puts the load before the guard, which is wrong by three instructions.
Writing it as the **first statement of the INNER loop body** is what matches:
loop.c hoists it into the preheader, which is after the guard by construction.
This is the placement half of "anything after a hoisted invariant was written
by the loop optimiser" — the *load itself* is source, its *position* is not.

**But it does not always hoist, and the reason is not yet known.** The
identical construction on `sub_08037A78` — same block, same wave, same
`ldr rN,=sym; ldr rM,[rN]` shape, a global declared `u8 *` instead of
`void *` — leaves the load inside the inner loop, reloaded every iteration.
The two functions differ in that `sub_080378A8` takes a `void *` parameter and
`sub_08037A78` an `int` it casts to `u16 *`, and in the store count (4 `strh`
plus a `strb` to a fixed symbol, against 8 `strh`). If you meet this, **probe
both spellings — inside the inner loop and in the outer body — before
assuming either**; each is one free `compile_probe` and they are 16 bytes apart.

**Wave 55 (W55-F) found the boundary of this rule: it does NOT transfer from a
pointer global's LOAD to a bare ADDRESS CONSTANT.** `sub_0805FC1C`'s ROM hoists
`ldr r0,=gUnknown_085D5AD0 ; mov sl, r0` into the preheader — after the entry
guard, before the giv init, so an LICM hoist by position — and reaches the table
with `add r0, sl`. The candidate rematerialises it, which costs the loop counter
its low register (`movs r1,#1 ; add ip,r1` for the increment) and desynchronises
two `return` blocks so cross-jumping merges only their tail: +8 bytes from one
missing hoist. Three levers were measured and all three did nothing:

- Writing the bind as the **first statement of the loop body** — the W50-L
  recipe — `cls = (u8 *)gUnknown_085D5ABC + 0x14;` then
  `tbl = *(u8 **)(cls + rec->unk00 * 0x5c)` compiles **byte-for-byte identically
  to not writing it at all.** CSE const-propagates the bind away before loop.c
  ever sees a movable. A *load* survives CSE and can be hoisted; a *constant*
  does not.
- Declaring the interior address as its own symbol (a 0x5c-stride struct with
  the pointer at offset 0, so no displacement is needed) also produced a
  byte-identical stream — **symbol spelling has no effect on LICM.** It only
  moves which name the pool word relocates against, and both resolve to the same
  address, so it buys nothing and costs a false object in the header.
- decomp-permuter, 300 s: no improvement on 69.2%.

The corollary for reading a diff: **a preheader `ldr =const ; mov rHI, r0` that
your candidate lacks is not a data-spelling problem and not a statement-order
problem.** Do not spend attempts respelling the reference; the pool order simply
reports the hoist happened (the hoisted word lands ahead of a word referenced by
the body's very first statement, which no in-body position can achieve).

## `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` on the STORES does not buy you aliasing disambiguation (wave 50, W50-L)

gcc 2.x `alias.c` has `fixed_scalar_and_varying_struct_p`: a MEM at a *fixed*
address that is *not* in a struct is supposed not to conflict with a MEM at a
*varying* address that *is*. That predicts you can free a scalar global's load
from a loop by making the loop's stores COMPONENT_REFs.

**Probed on `sub_08037A78` and it is false.** Rewriting

```c
dst[0] &= mask[0];  dst[2] &= mask[1];  ...      /* u16 *dst */
```

as

```c
dst[0].unk00 &= mask[0];  dst[1].unk00 &= mask[1];  ...   /* struct Cell *dst */
```

produced **byte-identical** assembly — same instructions, same registers, same
literal pool. The disambiguation is either absent from agbcc or does not reach
`invariant_p`. Do not spend an attempt on it.

**Replicated independently in wave 51 (W51-C)** on `sub_0805A008`, in both
directions: putting `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` on the STORES (a `struct Cell *`
out-pointer against flat `out[0]` / `*(s16 *)(out + 2)` derefs) and putting it
on the LOAD instead (reading the global through
`((struct MapRef *)&gUnknown_08499590)->p`) each produced byte-identical
assembly. Neither side of `fixed_scalar_and_varying_struct_p` is reachable.

## What DOES decide whether a global's load is loop-invariant is the STORE'S BASE (wave 51, W51-C)

This is a partial answer to the open question the W50-L chapter above leaves —
"it does not always hoist, and the reason is not yet known".

Measured on `sub_0805A008`, a nested cell sweep whose only stores are three
`strb`/`strh` through a pointer, against a `*(u8 **)&gUnknown_08499590` read at
the inner loop's entry guard. **Six spellings of the store all produce
byte-identical output and all hoist the load:**

* through a `struct Cell *` copied from a `void *` parameter;
* through a `u8 *` copied from a `u8 *` parameter, flat derefs;
* the same made `volatile`;
* the load made a COMPONENT_REF instead;
* the pointer PARAMETER mutated in place, with no copy local;
* the pointer arriving as an `int` and cast (this is the shape W50-L reports as
  the one that did NOT hoist there, so that reading does not generalise).

**One spelling kills the hoist:** storing to a **variably indexed global**,
`gUnknown_03004730[n] = x;`. The map pointer is then reloaded at every site, the
freed high register takes `y * 2`, and the stack spill disappears.

Two consequences worth carrying:

* **A store through a parameter-derived pointer does not block LICM of a
  global's load, whatever its type.** If your candidate hoists a load the ROM
  reloads, the answer is not in the out-pointer's declaration and no amount of
  retyping it will help. Wave 48 spent a park on that lead and wave 51 closed
  six spellings of it.
* **A `volatile` STORE does not block LICM of another MEM.** `aliases_everything_p`
  tests for an `AND` address, not for `MEM_VOLATILE_P`, so volatility on the
  store side never reaches `invariant_p`. Volatile is a tell about a *broken
  address chain* (see the main brief) and about *its own* reads — it is not a
  general "stop the optimiser" lever.

Read the two chapters together as: `symbol` vs `symbol` and `symbol` vs
parameter-pointer are both disambiguated; `symbol` vs `symbol[variable]` is not.

## Reading a four-way `switch`: case ORDER is visible, and the switch value's signedness is visible (wave 50, W50-L)

From `sub_080378A8`, cases 6 / 0xa / 0xb / 0xe:

- **`bhi` in the decision tree means the switch value is UNSIGNED**; `bgt`
  means signed. `switch (b & 0x1f)` with `b` declared `u8` gives `bgt` (the
  `&` promotes to `int`); with `b` declared `unsigned` it gives `bhi`. That one
  keyword is the whole difference and it is invisible anywhere else in the
  function, because every other use of `b` is a `>>` or an index.
- **The case body that is emitted INLINE in the decision tree, reached by a
  `bne` to the default rather than a `beq` to a label, is the FIRST case in
  source order.** agbcc emits the bodies in source order and the tree's last
  test falls straight into the first of them. Here the ROM inlines the 0xe
  body and jumps to 6 / 0xa / 0xb, so the source order is 0xe, 6, 0xa, 0xb —
  *not* ascending, and writing them ascending costs one instruction and moves
  four labels.

## The BLANK arm of an `if` emitted FIRST means the source tests the NEGATED condition (wave 50, W50-L)

`sub_080378A8`'s inner body is

```
	ldrb r7, [r5]
	cmp r4, r7
	bhs  L_blank           @ falls THROUGH to L_blank
	ldrb r0, [r5, #1]
	cmp ip, r0
	blo  L_big             @ jumps FORWARD to the big arm
L_blank:
	ldr r2, =gUnknown_0849D434
	b    L_join
L_big:
	...
```

agbcc always lays the *then* arm inline and the *else* arm after it. So a ROM
that puts the short arm inline was written `if (!cond) short; else long;`, here
`if (x >= buf[0] || y >= buf[1]) src = blank; else { ... }`. Written the
positive way round (`if (x < buf[0] && y < buf[1])`) both branches become
`bhs L_else` and the `.4byte` for the blank table moves out of the first
literal pool — a diff that looks like a pool-ordering problem and is actually
an if/else layout problem. **Read the pool order backwards to find it.**

## An explicit narrowing cast survives a SPILL and folds away in a register (wave 50, W50-L)

`sub_080378A8` clamps two values written the same way in the source:

```c
if (w > 0x20) w = 0x20;          /* cmp r6, #0x20; bls          */
if ((u8)h > 0x20) h = 0x20;      /* lsls #24; lsrs #24; cmp; bls */
```

Both are `unsigned` locals loaded by `ldrb`. `w` stays in r6, so combine sees
the `zero_extend` at the def and deletes the cast; `h` is spilled to `[sp,#4]`
between the def and the use, the chain breaks, and the `lsls #24; lsrs #24`
pair survives. **So an apparently asymmetric pair of casts in the ROM can be a
symmetric pair in the source** — do not invent two different types for the two
variables, and do not delete the cast from the one that shows it. The tell that
the type is `unsigned` and not `u8` is elsewhere: `(buf[0] - w) >> 1` is a
`lsrs`, and `w++` is a bare `adds` with no re-truncation (a `u8` or `u16` local
truncates at the assignment — compare `x` in the same function, which is `u16`
and gets `lsls #16; lsrs #16` at every increment).

## A 32-bit MASK on a `u16` destination needs an intermediate 32-bit local — otherwise combine narrows it and deletes the truncation (wave 50, W50-K)

`sub_0801C090` builds OAM words as "keep the high bits, replace the low field":

```
	mov r0, sb
	orrs r0, r2                       @ a2 | attr0
	ldr r1, _0801C140 @ =0xFFFFFF00
	ands r0, r1
	...
	orrs r0, r1
	lsls r0, r0, #0x10
	lsrs r7, r0, #0x10                @ store into a u16 local
```

The obvious spelling does **not** produce this:

```c
u16 attr0;
attr0 = ((a2 | src[0]) & 0xffffff00) | ((src[0] + a2) & 0xff);
```

agbcc emits `mov r0,#0xff; lsl r0,r0,#8; and ...` and **no** `lsl #16; lsr #16`.
The store into the `u16` pseudo is `(set x (zero_extend:SI (subreg:HI t)))`;
combine merges that with the `ior` and the `and` (3 insns, within its limit) and
`force_to_mode` rewrites the mask to `0xFF00`, after which the value provably
fits 16 bits and the truncation is dead. So a 1-instruction pool `ldr` plus a
2-instruction truncation becomes a 2-instruction `mov`/`lsl` and nothing else.

**Route the value through a 32-bit local first and both come back:**

```c
u32 t;
t = ((a2 | src[0]) & 0xffffff00) | ((src[0] + a2) & 0xff);
attr0 = t;
```

Binding only the masked half works too (`u32 hi = (a2|src[0]) & 0xffffff00;
attr0 = hi | (...);`). Four spellings that do NOT work, all measured on the same
expression — every one narrows the mask and drops the truncation:

- `u16 a = <expr>;`
- `a |= 0xffffff00;` on a `u16`
- `a = (u16)(<expr>);`
- `u32 a = (u16)(<expr>);`

Writing the constant as `~0xff` (int) instead of `0xffffff00` (unsigned int)
changes nothing. A `?:` also keeps the pool word and the truncation, but pays a
`b` and a copy at the merge, so it is not the same code.

**The inverse case is not the same lever.** A *redundant* mask —
`u8_array[i] & 0xff` — is deleted by `nonzero_bits` on the QImode load, and an
intermediate `u32` local does NOT save it; on `sub_0801B2FC`'s tail loop it also
flipped the loop into a `check_dbra_loop` countdown. Wave 65 measured that
candidate at exact total size (444/444) and 84.01%, but the AND was still gone:
the regained bytes were the changed loop form and pool/alignment, not the
desired `movs #0xff; adds; ands`. That one is still open; it needs a load whose
TREE mode is not known-byte while instruction selection still chooses `ldrb`.

The same wave tested the direct liveness hypothesis on `sub_0801C090`: binding
`src[1]` and `src[0]` to `u16` locals in each arm moved the candidate from -16
to -12 bytes, but did not spill the loop count and scored only 22.22%, below the
45.83% permuter best. A pair of source-halfword bindings is therefore not the
missing register-pressure lever.

**A third variant: the destination is a STRUCT MEMBER STORE, and the cause can
be a change in a CALLEE'S RETURN TYPE (wave 60, W60-D).** Same mechanism, new
shape. `sub_08029948` writes a `u16` struct member:

```c
gUnknown_03001470[id].unk22 = (u16)a;      /* narrowing DELETED */
```

The cast feeds nothing but a `strh`, which truncates anyway, so combine removes
it and the function comes out 4 bytes short — the ROM materialises the
narrowing before the call (`adds r4,r0,#0 ; lsls r4,#0x10 ; lsrs r4,#0x10`).
Binding the value to a `u16` LOCAL restores it:

```c
u16 v;
v = a;
gUnknown_03001470[id].unk22 = v;
```

because a promoted HImode pseudo must actually hold a zero-extended value, and
that is part of its representation rather than an optimisable expression.

Note the direction is the OPPOSITE of the wave-50 case above and the fix is the
mirror image: there a `u16` local destination killed the truncation and a `u32`
intermediate saved it; here a cast into a `strh` kills it and a `u16` local
saves it. **What the two share is the rule, not the type: the value must pass
through a pseudo whose declared representation forces the conversion, and
whichever spelling makes the conversion merely "an expression combine can
prove redundant" loses it.**

**And a cause worth knowing, because it strikes drafts nobody has touched.**
This draft had been correct once. `sub_080152C0`'s return type was later
corrected to `s8` in `include/unknown-functions.h` for an unrelated function's
sake; that made the `(u16)` cast provably dead where it had not been before,
and the draft silently lost 4 bytes. See the chapter on parks going stale. Do
not re-measure the six spellings in the wave-50 table above — they are settled;
`work/sub_0801C090/NOTES.md` carries the four that fail and the two that work.

## `nonzero_bits` is tracked only for a SINGLE-SET pseudo — masking a parameter IN PLACE keeps a later truncation alive (wave 57, W57-A)

This closes the "still open" inverse case at the end of the chapter above, and
the lever is neither an intermediate local nor a cast: it is the number of times
the pseudo is **set**.

`sub_08002298` masks its second parameter to 8 bits and later hands it to
`sub_0802BD54`'s `u16` parameter. The ROM keeps the truncation:

```
	adds r7, r1, #0
	movs r0, #0xff
	ands r7, r0            @ the mask
	...
	lsls r1, r7, #0x10
	lsrs r1, r1, #0x10     @ a (u16) conversion on a value that provably fits in 8
```

Spelled the way the promoted `sub_08002510` next door spells the same head, that
pair is **deleted** and the function comes out 4 bytes short:

```c
int v;
v = a2 & 0xFF;               /* ONE set of v -> nonzero_bits(v) = 0xFF */
sub_0802BD54(..., v, ...);   /* emits `adds r1, r7, #0` */
```

Masking the parameter in place restores it exactly:

```c
a2 &= 0xFF;                  /* TWO sets of a2 -> nonzero_bits unknown */
sub_0802BD54(..., a2, ...);  /* emits `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` */
```

`combine` drops a zero-extension when `nonzero_bits` proves the value already
fits, and for a REG it consults `reg_stat[].nonzero_bits`, which
`set_nonzero_bits_and_sign_copies` fills in **only for pseudos with
`REG_N_SETS == 1`**. A separate `v = a2 & 0xFF` is a one-set pseudo, so 0xFF is
known and the 16-bit truncation is provably dead. `a2 &= 0xFF` gives the
parameter's pseudo two sets — the prologue's copy out of the argument register,
and the AND — so nothing is known and the truncation survives.

**Consequences, all of which cut against the obvious reading:**

- **An explicit `(u16)v` cast does NOT restore it.** Measured. The implicit
  conversion to a prototype's narrow parameter and an explicit cast build the
  same tree, and both fold on a one-set pseudo. That is a real limit on the
  wave-15 note that a probe cannot tell `u16 v` from `int v` with a cast: the
  discriminator here is the SET COUNT, not the cast and not the declaration.
- **Both spellings produce the same two head instructions**, so the head is not
  where this is visible — only the distant use is.
- **Read it backwards.** A redundant-looking `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` (or the
  `#0x18` pair) on a value the ROM has *already* masked narrower is neither a
  type tell nor an artefact. It says the original's value lives in a pseudo with
  more than one assignment, and the commonest source of that is a parameter
  modified in place — which is exactly what a decompiler never writes.
- Worth 4 bytes across two call sites, and the only difference between a
  632-byte match and a 628-byte miss.

## `arr[base - 1 + i]` cannot be spelled in ONE expression — it needs a TEMPORARY (wave 51, W51-I)

`sub_080040C8` tests the four map neighbours of `(x, y)`. The ROM's left one is

```
ldrh r0, [r0]        @ MAP->rowOffset[y]
subs r0, #1
adds r0, r0, r4      @ + x
```

i.e. `(rowOffset[y] - 1) + x`, with the constant applied to the ROW value
BEFORE the column is added. **No single-expression spelling produces that.**
All three were compiled and measured against the same 980-byte body:

| source | agbcc emits | result |
|---|---|---|
| `MAP->cell[MAP->rowOffset[y] + x - 1]` | `adds r0,r0,r4; subs r0,#1` | order reversed, 8 B off |
| `MAP->cell[MAP->rowOffset[y] - 1 + x]` | `subs r2,r4,#1; adds r0,r0,r2` | fold reassociates, then CSE shares `x - 1` with the `sub_0800BA9C(x - 1, y)` argument — 10 B off |
| `MAP->cell[MAP->rowOffset[y] + (x - 1)]` | same as above | same |

`fold` moves the constant out of the inner sum whichever way you group it, and
once `x - 1` exists as a value, cse hands the subscript the shared copy. The
spelling that matches is a **statement boundary**:

```c
r = MAP->rowOffset[y] - 1;
if (MAP->cell[r + x] == 7)
    sub_0800BA9C(x - 1, y);
```

That closed the last 8 bytes of a 99.2% candidate, and the same shape with
`+ 1` closed the right-hand neighbour. The temporary dies inside the statement,
so it costs no register — the ROM keeps the whole chain in `r0`. This is the
"statement boundary is a fold barrier" lever (wave 46, W46-C) applied to a
SUBSCRIPT rather than to a pointer, and it is the only lever that works here:
15 minutes of decomp-permuter over ~17,500 iterations from the 99.2% base found
nothing, because the fix is a fold barrier, not an allocation.

## A DEAD-looking `mov rHI, r0; mov rLO, rHI` after a `bl` means the variable is read LATER (wave 51, W51-I)

`sub_080040C8` opens four of its loops with

```
bl sub_08003B6C
mov r8, r0        @ n = <call>
mov r7, r8        @ i = n
cmp r7, #0
```

and in two of those four, `r8` is never read again before being overwritten —
it looks like a dead store the compiler forgot. It is not. agbcc coalesces
`n = f(); i = n;` into a single `adds r7, r0, #0` **whenever `n` is dead after
the copy**; the copy survives only while `n` is still live. So a redundant
`mov` pair after a call is a positive statement that *the same variable is read
somewhere later in the function*, even if this block never touches it again.

Here the later read was in the final nested loop's initialiser
(`for (x = n = 1; ...)`), 400 bytes further on. Reading the pair as
"allocation noise" cost this function 8 bytes across two blocks and was the
whole residual until it was read as liveness.

**Corollary for the preheader-order rule.** The same function opens with
`movs r0, #7; mov ip, r0` BEFORE the fill loop's `movs r6, #0` (the source's
`y = 0`). Anything sitting *after* the loop init is a LICM hoist and must not
be authored — but this one sits *before* it, so it is SOURCE: a local assigned
`7` and stored inside the loop. Writing the literal `7` at the store instead
left agbcc rematerialising it and cost 4 bytes. The rule reads both ways.

## `X + (off + C)` survives only when X is the POINTER side of the sum (wave 50, W50-K)

`sub_0801C53C` computes a VRAM destination as

```
	lsls r1, r1, #5                   @ X = (a1->unk22 & 0x3ff) << 5
	ldr r3, [sp]                      @ off
	ldr r4, _0801C63C @ =0x06010000
	adds r2, r3, r4                   @ off + C   <- grouped
	adds r1, r1, r2
```

Every ordinary spelling of the three-term sum reassociates the constant onto the
complex term instead, emitting the pool `ldr` BEFORE the `ldr [sp]`:

- `(u8 *)0x06010000 + off + X`
- `(u8 *)(0x06010000 + off) + X`
- `X + (u8 *)(0x06010000 + off)`
- `(u8 *)(X + (off + 0x06010000))`

All four fold to `(X + C) + off`. What reproduces the ROM is casting **X** — the
complex term — to the pointer and leaving `off + C` as an int sum:

```c
    (u8 *)((a1->unk22 & 0x3ff) << 5) + (off + 0x06010000)
```

`ptr + int` is not reassociated across the pointer conversion, so the int sum
stays a unit. Read the rule as: whichever operand carries the pointer type is
the one the constant will NOT be folded into.

## `A * (B << k)` and `A * (B * 2^k)` are different code (wave 50, W50-K)

In the same function, `sub_08011E54`'s size argument is

```
	ldrb r4, [r2]                     @ w
	adds r3, #1
	add r3, r8
	ldrb r2, [r3]                     @ h
	lsls r2, r2, #5
	muls r2, r4, r2                   @ w * (h << 5)
```

Written `w * (h * 0x20)` fold reassociates the constant onto the FIRST operand
and emits `lsl` on `w` instead (`lsl r4,r4,#5; mul r2,r2,r4`), and `w * h * 0x20`
gives `mul` then `lsl`. Only the explicit shift `w * (h << 5)` leaves the scale
on the second operand, because fold does not reassociate `MULT_EXPR` with
`LSHIFT_EXPR`. This is the same family as the existing "`g * 0x100` is not
`g << 8`" rule and points the opposite way, so check which side the ROM scales.

## `while (n-- > 0)` and `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)` are DIFFERENT dbra forms (wave 50, W50-K)

Both become countdowns, and the two are distinguishable at both ends:

```
	adds r2, r6, #0                   @ copy n for the guard
	subs r6, #1                       @ first decrement, in the preheader
	cmp r2, #0
	ble  out                          @ SIGNED guard
	...
	adds r0, r6, #0                   @ test the PRE-decrement value
	subs r6, #1
	cmp r0, #0
	bgt  loop
```

is `while (n-- > 0)`. The `for` loop over the same range gives an UNSIGNED guard
(`cmp n,#0; beq out`, because gcc knows a `u16`-derived bound is non-negative)
and a 3-instruction bottom (`sub #1; cmp #0; bne`). The tells are the `ble`/`beq`
guard and the extra register copy before the decrement.

## `(i + 1) * K` in a loop body kills EVERY giv in that loop (wave 55, W55-B)

The single highest-value readout of the wave, and it looks nothing like a loop
bug. `sub_0807C034` iterates `for (i = 0; i < proc->unk4c; i++)` and the ROM
carries **five** induction variables — `i*10`, `i*10+10`, `i*8+0x80`,
`gUnknown_0202FF78 + i`, and `i` itself. The first draft, written with

```c
if (v >= i * 10 && v < (i + 1) * 10) { ... }
else if (v >= (i + 1) * 10)          { ... }
```

produced **zero** of them: every quantity was recomputed from `i` inside the
body with a `lsls`/`adds`/`lsls` multiply-by-ten synthesis. Changing nothing but
the two `(i + 1) * 10` into `i * 10 + 10` matched the function outright.

The mechanism: `(i + 1)` is materialised as its own pseudo, and CSE then notices
the loop's own increment computes the same value and rewrites `i = i + 1` into a
plain register COPY of it. `basic_induction_var` only recognises
`SET (reg) (PLUS (reg) (const_int))`, so after that rewrite **`i` is no longer a
biv at all** — and with no biv, `strength_reduce` has nothing to hang a giv on
and the whole loop loses strength reduction.

**The tell is in the loop bottom, not in the body.** Look for the increment:

- `adds r4, #1` — `i` is a biv, givs are possible.
- `adds r4, r7, #0` where `r7` was computed earlier in the body as `i + 1` —
  the biv is gone, and *every* missing giv in that loop has this one cause.

So `i + 1` is safe to write anywhere it is not multiplied or otherwise reused;
what breaks is spelling a giv's expression *through* it. Distribute the constant
by hand: `i * K + K`, `(i + 1) * K` never.

## A giv of the form `C + i*K` CANNOT be spelled inside a larger expression — it needs its own local (wave 55, W55-B)

Companion to the rule above, and the one that cost `sub_080791B0` three
attempts. The ROM's block is

```
movs r5, #0x80
lsls r5, r5, #2        @ r5 = 0x200, the giv, stepping #0x20
movs r4, #7
_080791FE:
ldrh  r0, [r7]
lsls  r0, r0, #3       @ *q * 8
adds  r0, r0, r5       @ + the giv
lsls  r0, r0, #5
```

i.e. `0x200 + i*0x20` is one register. Three source spellings were probed and
**all three compile identically, and all three are wrong**:

```c
(*q * 8 + i * 0x20 + 0x200) * 0x20     /* constant last  */
(i * 0x20 + 0x200 + *q * 8) * 0x20     /* constant first */
(*q * 8 + (i * 0x20 + 0x200)) * 0x20   /* parenthesised  */
```

Every one emits `lsls rT, rI, #5` for `i*0x20` and materialises `0x200`
separately, because **fold canonicalises an integer constant toward the front of
a sum regardless of how the source parenthesises it** — you cannot keep `C` and
`i*K` adjacent inside a bigger expression. And a lone `i*K` is not worth a giv
to gcc: replacing one `lsls` with one `adds` is zero benefit, so it declines.
`C + i*K` costs three or four instructions and is very much worth one, which is
why the ROM has it and your candidate does not.

**Binding it to a local is the only spelling that works**, and it reproduces the
ROM exactly:

```c
for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)
{
    t = i * 0x20 + 0x200;          /* one insn -> one giv */
    CpuFastSet(base + (*q * 8 + t) * 0x20, dst, 0x40);
}
```

An explicit second counter (`t = 0x200;` before the loop, `t += 0x20;` at the
bottom) also produces the giv, but it puts the update where the source puts it,
which was one instruction out of place; the `t = i * K + C` form lets
`strength_reduce` schedule the update itself and that is what the ROM has.

**A second, free tell confirms the diagnosis before you rewrite anything: the
loop DIRECTION.** `check_dbra_loop` can only reverse a counted loop into
`subs; cmp #0; bge` when the biv has no remaining non-giv use. So:

- ROM counts DOWN, candidate counts UP (`adds rI,#1; cmp rI,#N; ble`) → `i` is
  still being read for something the ROM turned into a giv. Ascending-vs-
  descending is a *symptom of a missing giv*, never a sign that you got the
  source loop's direction wrong.

## `sym + C + i*K` folds the symbol into the pool word; put `C` inside the index to keep it bare (wave 55, W55-B)

`sub_080791B0` copies twenty-odd runs out of `gUnknown_0200FC50`. For each, the
ROM builds the giv's initial value at RUNTIME off the bare symbol:

```
ldr  r0, _080793F0     @ =gUnknown_0200FC50
movs r1, #0x80
lsls r1, r1, #6        @ 0x2000
adds r5, r0, r1
```

Written as `gUnknown_0200FC50 + 0x2000 + i * 0x40`, agbcc instead folds
`sym + 0x2000` into a single relocated pool word and the giv init becomes one
`ldr` — byte-identical in *count* only by accident, and it also changes the
pool's contents, so the `.rodata` comparison fails even where the instructions
line up. Writing the constant as part of the SUBSCRIPT keeps the symbol bare:

```c
gUnknown_0200FC50 + (0x100 + i * 2) * 0x20     /* matches */
gUnknown_0200FC50 + 0x2000 + i * 0x40          /* folds to sym+0x2000 */
```

**The diagnostic is the pool, not the instruction stream:** a `.word` carrying a
non-zero addend against your symbol (`.word 0x00002000` + `R_ARM_ABS32
gUnknown_0200FC50`) where the ROM has a bare relocation is this rule, every
time. Note the exception in the same function: where the offset is a
*pure constant* with no loop index (`CpuFastSet(gUnknown_0200FC50 + 0x3B00, …)`),
the fold is CORRECT — that is exactly the force-addr address constant the ROM
carries, and the splitter has simply invented a `gUnknown_02013750` name for it.
`trymatch` reports that as "different symbols that resolve to the same address",
which is a match.

## Reading a binding local in a LATER loop blocks its in-place coalescing (wave 55, W55-B)

A sharpening of "binding locals are punctuation". `sub_080791B0` opens with the
`c_08079024.c` idiom

```c
q = &proc->unk52;
*q = 5 - n;
if (*q > 3)
    *q = 3;
```

and the ROM computes `q` **in place on the parameter's register** (`adds r4,
#82`, destroying `proc`), then copies it into `r7` for the loop that follows.
Reading `*q` inside that loop instead gives `adds r7, r4, #0; adds r7, #82` —
the same two instructions, in the wrong order, with `proc` still live.

The lever is which expression the LOOP reads:

- loop reads `*q`   → `q` is one long-lived pseudo, allocated up front, `proc`
  survives, no in-place add.
- loop reads `proc->unk52` → `q`'s live range ends at the second `strh`, so it
  coalesces with `proc`; CSE then recognises `&proc->unk52` in the loop as the
  same address and emits the copy. This is the ROM.

So a value used by a few statements and then again after a control-flow join is
**two pseudos in the original, not one**, and the second reference is written as
the full member access rather than through the binding. Read backwards: an
in-place `adds rP, #K` on a parameter register followed later by a copy of that
same register is the signature of exactly this split.

## `x + K` on a binding local FOLDS back through the local's own definition, and that keeps the base alive (wave 55, W55-H)

Given `x = i * 16 + 0x38;` and three uses `x`, `x + 8`, `x += 4`, agbcc does NOT
emit a chain off `x`. cse.c rebuilds `x + 8` as `i * 16 + 0x40` — the same
instruction count at that site, but it gives `i * 16` a second use, so `i * 16`
gets its own register and `x` becomes a copy:

```
    ROM         lsls r4, r0, #4 ; adds r4, #56          i*16 dies INTO x
                adds r2, r4, #0 ; adds r2, #8           +8 off x
    candidate   lsls r4, r1, #4 ; adds r5, r4, #0 ; adds r5, #56
                adds r2, r4, #0 ; adds r2, #64          +64 off i*16
```

Two instructions per site, and the extra live value cascades: it pushes another
local into a high register and can add a spill slot, so the frame grows too.

**What DOES work, measured:** `x += 4` instead of `x + 4` for the LAST use.
The mutation makes the ROM's destructive `adds rN, #4` come out exactly, because
after it the `x == i * 16 + 0x38` equivalence is dead. **What does NOT work:**
`x += 8` for a middle use — the ROM's middle use is a non-destructive
`adds r2, rX, #0; adds r2, #8`, which proves `x` is still live there, and every
spelling of a live-through `+8` (`x + 8`, a second local `x2 = x + 8`, or the
independent `i * 16 + 0x40`) reduces to the same rtx and folds.

So: **a binding local only blocks the fold for uses AFTER it is mutated.** If
the ROM shows a non-destructive `adds rD, rBASE, #0; adds rD, #k` where your
candidate shows `adds rD, rBASE, #0; adds rD, #(k + C)`, the difference is not
the offset — it is that the ROM's base pseudo has one use and yours has two.
This is the same phenomenon as "Two identical `i * K` in one call's arguments"
above, seen from the other side, and it is currently UNSOLVED for the
live-through case. `sub_080482D8` is parked on exactly this.

## `sym + i*A + j*B` in a loop forces a `.rodata` address constant; `&sym[i*A + j*B]` does not (wave 56, W56-C)

Same array, same arithmetic, two spellings, and only one of them strength-reduces.

```c
/* A */ CpuFastSet(gUnknown_0200FC50 + i * 0x100 + j * 0x400,  dst, 0x40);
/* B */ CpuFastSet(&gUnknown_0200FC50[i * 0x100 + j * 0x400], dst, 0x40);
```

**A** makes agbcc park the array's ADDRESS in a `.rodata` address constant and
reload it through a DOUBLE load *inside the inner loop*:

```
    ldr  r4, [pc, #164]     @ .word .rodata     <- address OF the address
    ...
    mov  r2, r9
    ldr  r1, [r2, #0]       @ the actual gUnknown_0200FC50, reloaded every iteration
    lsls r0, r4, #10
    adds r0, r0, r1
```

Because the base arrives from MEMORY it is not loop-invariant as far as
`strength_reduce` is concerned, so the source pointer never becomes a giv: the
`j * 0x400` is recomputed with an `lsls` in the body and the loop's ascending
counter survives instead of being turned into a `dbra` countdown.

**B** emits the plain pool word (`ldr r4, [pc]; .word gUnknown_0200FC50`), keeps
the base in a callee-saved register across the whole nest, and both pointers
become givs with the ROM's `subs rCNT,#1; cmp rCNT,#0; bge` bottom.

This is NOT the ordinary `-fforce-addr` blob described in the chapter below —
there is no such blob in the ROM for this function, and nothing needs carving at
promotion. It is a defect that YOUR spelling introduces, and the size delta does
not warn you about it: both spellings were `size: match`. **The tell is the
double load in the loop body, not the `size:` line.** Diagnose it ROM-side: if
`asm/` reaches the array with one `ldr rN,=sym`, spell it `&sym[...]`.

## A loop's giv INIT order and its giv INCREMENT order are always the SAME — if the ROM shows them different, one of the two pointers is source-level (wave 56, W56-C)

Measured on `sub_0807E980`'s tail, a `CpuFastSet` double loop over two pointers
advancing at different strides. Writing both as pure induction expressions gives,
in every spelling tried:

| spelling | preheader init order | body increment order |
|---|---|---|
| both inline in the call | dst, src | dst, src |
| dst hoisted to its own statement | src, dst | src, dst |
| src as a source-level `u8 *`, `src += K` in the body | src, dst | src, dst |
| dst as a source-level `u8 *`, `dst += K` in the body | dst, src | dst, src |

**The two orders never disagree, and `check_dbra_loop`'s counter init is always
emitted LAST, after every giv init.** So a ROM that shows

```
    <src init>            <- inits are src, dst
    movs rCNT, #7         <- counter init BETWEEN them
    <dst init>
  body: call; dst += 0x100; src += 0x400   <- increments are dst, src
```

is telling you three things at once: the counter is a **source-level descending
`for (j = 7; j >= 0; j--)`** (not an ascending loop converted by
`check_dbra_loop`, which would put the init last), both pointers are
**source-level locals** incremented in the body, and the one whose init sits
after the counter was written **inside the `for`'s init clause**:

```c
src = &gUnknown_0200FC50[i * 0x100];
for (j = 7, dst = (u8 *)(0x06015000 + i * 0x800); j >= 0; j--)
{
    CpuFastSet(src, dst, 0x40);
    dst += 0x100;
    src += 0x400;
}
```

That reproduces the ROM's instruction order in the loop **instruction for
instruction**. The catch, and the reason `sub_0807E980` is parked at 99.0%
rather than matched: two source-level pointer locals cost a register. The ROM
lets the outer counter `i` and `dst` share one register (it stashes `i + 1` at
the TOP of the outer body and then overwrites `i`'s register with `dst`), and
gcc only does that when it is tight. With the explicit locals it is not tight,
so it keeps `i` separate, evicts `proc` from r7, and stops holding the array
base in `sl` — **+12 bytes spread over the rest of the function, none of it in
the loop you fixed.** Binding the base to its own local to buy `sl` back made it
worse again.

**So this pair of facts is a diagnostic, not yet a lever.** Read the disagreement
between init order and increment order to learn the loop's source shape; then be
aware that spelling it out may cost more elsewhere than the order is worth. And
do NOT try `(7 - j)` to keep a descending counter with ascending offsets —
`strength_reduce` does not handle it at all, and recomputes `movs r0,#7; subs
r0,r0,rJ` plus both shifts in the body.

**One thing the permuter IS good for here:** 12,480 iterations from the 98.65%
draft found the "hoist the dst into its own statement" mutation, which is what
flipped the src/dst REGISTER assignment to the ROM's (98.65% -> 99.0%). It found
nothing for the ordering, which is consistent with the table above — the
ordering is not reachable by any mutation of a two-giv loop.

## A `[2]` read on a `-fforce-addr` row hoists the `+4` onto the BASE unless the row is bound (wave 55, W55-H)

`gUnknown_085D6A48[gUnknown_03004580[side][1]][2]`, written inline, compiles to
`adds rBASE, #4` on the pool-word base and then the index add, losing the
`ldrh rD, [rN, #4]` displacement:

```
    ROM         adds r0, r0, r2 ; ldrh r0, [r0, #4]
    inline      adds r2, #4 ; adds r0, r0, r2 ; ldrh r0, [r0, #0]
```

Binding the row to a `u16 *` local first restores the displacement. This is the
same lever c_0804B744.c documents for `e0[4]`, and it applies to ANY non-zero
member index on a force-addr-backed row, not just to rows read more than once.

**And use ONE LOCAL PER TEST SITE.** `sub_0804C0FC` reads the row twice, in two
`if`s separated by calls. Reusing a single `row` local for both leaves 3 bytes
differing: the first site's address lands in a callee-saved-shaped register
because the pseudo is shared, where the ROM lets it die in `r0`. Two separate
locals, `row0` and `row`, took it to MATCHED. That is the "binding locals are
punctuation" rule with the count read off the ROM's register choice.

## Five readouts from the 0x08037 map block (wave 43, W43-D)

Five of six matched; each of these was the whole difference on at least one.

**A clamped local's DECLARED TYPE is readable from the branch, and `u8` is not
`int`.** `if (w > 0x20) w = 0x20;` then `(w + 1) >> 1`, with `w` loaded by
`ldrb`, gives three different outputs and the ROM picks the third:

| declaration | compare | shift |
|---|---|---|
| `int w`  | `ble` | `asrs` |
| `u32 w`  | `bls` | `lsrs` |
| `u8 w`   | `bls` | `asrs` |

Only `u8` pairs an UNSIGNED compare with an ARITHMETIC shift: it promotes to
`int` for the shift, but agbcc knows the zero-extended value is non-negative at
the compare and picks the unsigned condition. So `bls` + `asrs` together are a
positive readout of a narrow local, not a contradiction to explain away. Storing
the same `ldrb` into an `int` first loses it — the type is the whole signal.

**agbcc's `fold` merges a constant only with an ADJACENT one.** `j + 1 + i +
0x1000` keeps the `1` and the `0x1000` apart, so the loop hoists 0x1000 into a
register (two instructions, no pool word) and leaves `adds #1` inline.
Reorder it to `j + i + 1 + 0x1000` and the two constants become adjacent, fold
makes 0x1001, and it needs a pool word. `fold` only handles `(A + C1) + C2`,
where the inner tree's own second operand is already a constant — a variable
between them blocks it. Reading this backwards: **two separately-materialised
constants in one expression tell you a non-constant term sits between them in
the source.**

**A loop counter that steps 16 with a bound of `N * 16` is what the SOURCE
wrote.** Both `sub_08037A20` and `sub_08037B90` count in pixels, not tiles. A
tile counter (`for (i = 0; i < n; i++)`) with `i * 32` inside emits `lsl #5` and
`lsl #6` per iteration and steps by 1; the ROM steps by 16 and scales down
(`dst[y * 2 + x]`). Do not read the 16 as strength reduction and try to write
the tile form — a u16-truncated counter blocks giv reduction anyway, so a
counter that steps 16 AND is truncated `lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10` cannot be a
compiler-invented biv.

**Comparing a `u16` struct member against a `u8` PARAMETER produces a hoisted
`lsls #0x10` and an in-loop `lsrs #0x10`.** agbcc narrows the comparison to the
member's HImode and re-extends the u8 side; LICM hoists the invariant half into
the preheader. This looks exactly like a missing `(u16)` cast, and the instinct
to add one — or to introduce a `u16` local holding the parameter — is wrong and
costs both shifts plus a second pseudo, because a u16 local assigned from a u8
is a free copy. Write the bare `g[i].member == a1`.

**`switch` arm BODIES are emitted in source order**, so their layout reads the
original `case` order straight off. `sub_08037C34`'s ROM emits the `case 0xe`
body first and `case 0xb` last, and the source lists them 0xe, 6, 0xa, 0xb —
which is also the order of four unrelated zero-stores earlier in the same
function, a free consistency check. Ordering them by ascending case value
reverses all four bodies and flips the last test from `bne` to `beq`+`b`. The
dispatch TREE is still built by value and does not move.

## A GOTO LOOP IS INVISIBLE TO loop.c — no LICM, no giv, no `check_dbra_loop` (wave 46, W46-B)

gcc 2.9 finds loops from `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG`/`END`, which the front end emits
only for `for`, `while` and `do`/`while`. **A loop built from a label and a
conditional `goto` gets no notes, so `loop.c` never runs on it at all.** All
three of its passes disappear together, and that is what makes the tell
readable:

- no LICM, so loop-invariant constants are **rebuilt every iteration**;
- no `strength_reduce`, so there is **no giv** — any stride has to be an
  explicit source variable;
- no `check_dbra_loop`, so an **ascending counter stays ascending**.

`sub_08060170` adds the useful combined readout (wave 63, W63-D): a label/goto
loop can carry **two explicit walking pointers and an explicit ascending
counter at once**.  The equivalent `for`/`do` spellings either left one address
as `base + i`, or strength-reduced both addresses and let `check_dbra_loop`
reverse the now-exit-only counter.  Writing the byte copy as a label/goto loop
emitted `ldrb; strb; inc source; inc destination; inc counter; cmp; ble`
exactly, because none of those three source variables passed through loop.c.

**Read the loop body for rebuilt constants first.** One constant materialised
inside a loop is an allocation accident; *several* is this. `sub_08063698`'s
loop rebuilds `0x1FFE0`, `0x06000000` (`movs r0,#0xc0; lsls r0,#0x13`) and its
`0x100` stride on every pass — three hoistable invariants left in place. Wave 44
read the first of those as a single stray LICM hoist and spent the wave trying
to spell the mask so `combine` would build it after loop-opt; the mask was never
the axis. Rewriting the `for` as a goto loop removed the hoist, the extra
preheader `ldr`, the `r7` push/pop pair and the +2 bytes in one edit and took
the function from parked to size-exact.

`sub_08063528` is the same tell in a function that has BOTH kinds. Its default
arm is a real `do`/`while`: the constant `1` is hoisted into `r6` and
`SIOMULTI[i]` is strength-reduced to a pointer walking down by 2 from
`0x04000126`. Its `0xE7`/`0xE8` arm runs the same source expression as a goto
loop and gets neither — `movs r1, #1` inside the body and the address rebuilt
as `0x04000120 + i * 2` every pass. Two loops over the same registers in one
function, optimised and not, is decisive.

**The converse is the cost, and it is why this is not a free lever.** A goto
loop that needs a giv cannot have one. `sub_0806412C`'s ROM has an ascending
counter *and* a 0x18 giv in the same loop; written as a `for` the counter gets
reversed by `check_dbra_loop`, and written as a goto loop the stride has to
become a source variable whose increment agbcc then schedules above the inner
loop instead of at the bottom. Nothing gives both, and it is parked on exactly
that.

**Do not reach for this on a plain counter-direction mismatch.** `subs; cmp #0;
bge` on its own still proves nothing (see the `check_dbra_loop` rule below) —
the discriminator is the rebuilt constants, not the branch.

### A goto loop also decides whether the `-fforce-addr` `.rodata` WORD SURVIVES (wave 49, W49-B)

A third consequence, and the one that is hardest to attribute because the
symptom appears in the literal pool rather than in the loop. **Writing the loop
as `while (1)` can delete an `-fforce-addr` `.rodata` address constant that the
ROM has.** Two passes acting in series do it:

1. LICM hoists the pool load `(set r (mem (symbol .LC0)))` into the preheader,
   because it is loop-invariant and `RTX_UNCHANGING_P`;
2. CSE-after-loop then sees a hoisted load from a constant-pool entry whose
   contents it knows, and const-propagates it back into a bare `symbol_ref`.

The `.LC0` entry is left unreferenced and never emitted, so the honest
`gUnknown_X->member` spelling — the one the `-fforce-addr` chapter tells you to
write — silently produces a **two-deep** `ldr; ldr` where the ROM has a
**three-deep** `ldr; ldr; ldr`. Nothing about the diff points at the loop.

`sub_080309AC` and `sub_08030B00` are the measurement. As `while (1)` they lose
the word and hoist `0x1AAE`, `&gUnknown_0202575C` and the constant `0` into
callee-saved registers; as goto loops both match byte-for-byte with the pool
word intact and nothing hoisted. The confirming read is the one this chapter
already prescribes — **the ROM re-materialises `0x1AAE` at THREE separate
sites**, which no LICM would ever leave.

**So the `-fforce-addr` chapter's "write the honest spelling and let the build
place the word" needs a rider: if the honest spelling does not produce the word
at all, suspect the LOOP FORM before you suspect the spelling.** Diagnose it by
probing a known-matched neighbour — `c_08030930.c`'s promoted body emits the
`.rodata` word under `compile_probe`, which proves the flag is on and moves the
question back into your own C in one free call.

### The goto loop's hidden SECOND cost: in-loop refs stop being weighted (wave 48, W48-K)

The chapter above prices a goto loop in codegen (no LICM, no giv, no dbra).
There is a second bill and it lands in the REGISTER ALLOCATOR, which is a
different pass and a different symptom, so it does not look related.

`flow.c` bumps `REG_N_REFS` by the enclosing `loop_depth`, and `loop_depth` is
tracked from `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG`. A goto loop has no note, so **every
reference inside it counts exactly ONE**, the same as straight-line code, and
`global.c`'s `allocno_compare` priority (`floor_log2(n_refs) * n_refs /
live_length`) is computed on those flat counts. A value read three times per
iteration and a value read once therefore tie, and the tie goes to whichever
has the SHORTER live range.

`sub_08071B9C` is the clean measurement. It is a palette-fade proc whose loop
reads `proc->unk2c` three times per pass (once per `Interpolate` call) and its
`data` local once:

- Written as a `for`, the loop notes exist, `proc`'s three in-loop refs are
  weighted up, and it wins `r7` with `data` in `sl` — **the ROM's assignment**.
  But strength reduction then turns all three array walks into givs and
  `check_dbra_loop` reverses the counter, so the BODY is wrong.
- Written as a goto loop the body is byte-exact — ascending counter, one shared
  `lsls rN, rI, #1` index, one source-level `*dst++` — but `data` (7 flat refs,
  dead one instruction earlier) outranks `proc` (7 flat refs, live to the tail)
  and takes `r7`. That costs one `mov rX, sl` at each of the four `proc` uses,
  +8 bytes, and it also flips which operand of a two-address `ands` is the
  destination, because the mask constants stop being consumed by the AND and
  stay live to be shared.

So **the two spellings are not "same code, one detail different" — they trade
the loop body against the register file, and on a loop that reads one pointer
much more often than another you may be able to get only one of them.** Read
the trade before spending attempts: if the ROM has an ascending counter AND a
giv you are in `sub_0806412C`'s park; if it has an ascending counter and NO giv
but the register assignment is call-frequency-shaped, you are in this one.

The lever, if you need it, is `n_refs` and not spelling: `floor_log2` steps at
8, so a spelling that gives the parameter an eighth reference — or drops the
local to six — is worth more than any amount of statement reordering. Nothing
tested moved it on `sub_08071B9C`; declaration order fixes the STACK SLOT order
(spill slots are assigned in declaration order — getting `i` declared before the
two pointers put them at `[sp,#4]/[sp,#8]/[sp,#0xc]` as the ROM has them) and
does not touch the register choice.

### A shared constant's def can be emitted at the previous loop's EXIT, and it costs a callee-saved register (wave 48, W48-K)

`sub_08073A00` is size-exact at 232 bytes with one instruction in the wrong
place. Eight `u8` globals are stored in a row, six of them zero; agbcc CSEs the
zero into one pseudo, and the ROM defines it at the FIRST of those stores
(`ldr r0, =g; movs r1, #0; strb r1, [r0]`). Written the obvious way the def
instead appears at the exit of the *preceding* `for` loop, several statements
early, where it overlaps the incoming parameter — so three values need registers
across the loops instead of two, and the function pushes `{r4, r5, lr}` where
the ROM pushes `{r4, lr}`.

**A stray `movs rN, #0` sitting between a loop's backward branch and the next
statement's first instruction is this, and it is a register-pressure fact, not a
statement-order one.** Do not go looking for a missing statement.

Two loops sharing one counter variable and two loops with separate counters are
BOTH wrong here and wrong in different directions, which is the useful half:

- shared `i`: both loops get identical register assignments (walker `r0`,
  counter `r1`, value `r2`) matching the ROM, and the stray zero appears;
- separate `i`/`j`: the stray zero disappears — agbcc reuses the second loop's
  exhausted down-counter, which is already 0 — but that pins the counter in a
  callee-saved register for the whole loop and re-shuffles both loops' registers.

So the counter-sharing question is decided by the LOOP BODIES' register
assignment, and the constant's placement is a separate problem that the counter
choice cannot fix.

## CSE beats CROSS-JUMPING to it: a known-zero register kills a shared `movs rD,#0` (wave 49, W49-B)

Two arms of a select that both assign the same constant normally end up sharing
one block — `jump.c`'s cross-jumping merges identical tails. **But CSE runs
first, and if one of those arms sits on a path where some variable is provably
equal to that constant, CSE rewrites the arm to copy the register instead.** The
two blocks are then no longer identical and the merge never happens.

`sub_08030234`'s three-way select is the measurement. The ROM has one
`movs r0,#0` reached from both arms:

```
    mov r1, sl ; cmp r1, #0 ; bne  L_else     @ nBad
    mov r2, r8 ; cmp r2, #0 ; bne  L_zero     @ nSplit  -> the SHARED zero
    <value>    ; b L_store
L_else:  mov r0, r8 ; cmp r0, #0 ; beq L_other
L_zero:  movs r0, #0
         b L_store
```

Written as two ordinary `buf[i] = 0;` statements, `record_jump_equiv` records
`nBad == 0` on the fall-through of the `bne`, and CSE emits `mov r0, rNBAD` for
that arm — same size, same cost, and fatal. The fix is to give the zero block
**two predecessors in the SOURCE**, with a `goto` into it, so it is already
shared before CSE gets there.

**The second-order symptom is what makes this expensive to diagnose: the extra
reference to `nBad` changes its `REG_N_REFS`, which flips which callee-saved
register it wins.** The diff therefore shows a whole-function `sl`/`sb` swap
alongside the two-instruction block difference, and reads like two independent
problems. It is one. **A register-assignment swap that appears together with a
duplicated constant is a consequence, not a second bug — fix the block and
re-measure before touching the allocation.**

The same reasoning says a `?:` will not help: it expands to the same
preset-then-conditionally-overwrite shape (`mov r0,#0; cmp; bne; ldrh r0,…`),
measured, and that is a *third* spelling that cannot cross-jump either.

## `while (c) B` and `if (c) do B while (c)` are BYTE-IDENTICAL — loop rotation is NOT source-reachable (wave 59, W59-G)

Two shapes appear in the ROM for a top-tested loop:

- **jump-to-test** — `b .Lbottom`, body, `.Lbottom:` test, `bne .Ltop`. Two bytes
  of entry cost, one copy of the test.
- **rotated** — the test duplicated inline at entry as a guard (`ldrb; cmp; beq
  end`), body, then the test again at the bottom. Six bytes of entry cost.

It is tempting to read the rotated form as a source-level `if (c) do { } while
(c);` and the other as a plain `while`. **It is not.** Measured on
`sub_0807B7BC`, whose ROM rotates its outer loop and whose draft does not:

```c
while (*str != 0) { ... str++; }                        /* 144 bytes, 9.0% */
if (*str != 0) { do { ... str++; } while (*str != 0); } /* 144 bytes, 9.0% */
```

**Byte-for-byte identical output** — same size, same registers, same spill
slots, same rotation choice, same 130 differing bytes. The front end folds the
source guard away and a later pass re-decides the rotation on its own, so the
source cannot express which form you get.

**The readout that IS available.** `sub_0807B7BC` has two nested loops and
**exactly one of them is rotated in each version — and it is the other one.**
The ROM rotates the outer loop and leaves the inner one jump-to-test; the draft
rotates the inner and leaves the outer jump-to-test. So the choice is made
once per function and is a consequence of something else (here, of the register
allocation: the two versions use a different number of call-saved registers).
**Do not spend an attempt spelling a loop guard.** If the rotation is wrong,
look for the allocation difference that moved it, and if the allocation is the
residual, park it.

## Control flow

**Branch polarity.** For `if (C) return A; return B;` agbcc branches to the A
block and falls through into B. Read it backwards: the fallthrough value is the
*second* return in the source. Writing the logically equivalent inverse gives a
~90% near-miss with the branches swapped — a one-attempt fix, always try it
first.

**But first settle whether the source branched at all. `if (C) return A;
return B;`, `return C ? A : B;` and `return C;` are three different shapes, and
the paragraph above only describes the first.** All three are the obvious way
to write a two-valued function and the choice is not cosmetic. One probe, two
globals, measured on the four functions this came from:

| source | codegen | length |
|---|---|---|
| `if (c) return 2; return 1;` | `cmp; bne L; mov r0,#1; b E;` **pool**; `L: mov r0,#2; E: bx lr` | 24 |
| `return c ? 2 : 1;` | `mov r1,#1; cmp; beq L; mov r1,#2; L: add r0,r1,#0; bx lr;` **pool** | 24 |
| `if (c) return 1; return 0;` | `cmp; bne L; mov r0,#0; b E;` **pool**; `L: mov r0,#1; E: bx lr` | 20 |
| `return c;` (0/1 result) | `cmp; beq L; mov r0,#1; L: bx lr;` **pool** | 16 |

Two things fall out. **The ternary is the same length as the `if`/`return`
pair** — no size signal at all, same failure class as the `|=` operand swap —
and the tells are that the ternary computes into **r1** and ends with a
redundant `adds r0, r1, #0`, and that its literal pool lands **after** the
`bx lr` instead of in the middle of the function. Read a pool sitting between
the two return blocks as the `if`/`return` form. **The boolean form, by
contrast, does have a 4-byte signal**, because it keeps the true-value block as
a fallthrough and never materialises the zero: a function that visibly stores
both constants did not write `return c;`.

`sub_0803BB44`/`sub_0803BB5C`/`sub_0803BB74` are the first row and
`sub_0803BB90` is the third — so even a leaf returning a plain 0/1 can want the
long spelling.

**This paragraph used to end "reaching for `return x != 0;` because it is the
natural C costs four bytes". That is wrong, and wave 10 measured it.** `!= 0` is
not a fourth spelling with a cost of its own; it is a synonym for row 4. Four
spellings over one `Proc_Find` call, one probe, agbcc -O2:

| source | codegen |
|---|---|
| `return f() != 0;` | `cmp; beq L; mov r0,#1; L: pop; bx` — **24 bytes** |
| `return f() ? 1 : 0;` | byte-identical to the above |
| `return !!f();` | byte-identical to the above |
| `if (f()) return 1; return 0;` | `cmp; bne L; mov r0,#0; b E;` **pool**; `L: mov r0,#1; E:` — **28 bytes** |

So the real fork is **explicit `if`/`return` pair versus everything else**, not
the presence of `!= 0`. Any expression that has to normalise a non-0/1 value to
a boolean collapses to the short fallthrough form, and the three short spellings
are indistinguishable in the output — pick whichever reads best. Note the
ternary does NOT get the r1-and-`adds r0, r1, #0` treatment described above when
its arms are literally 1 and 0; that tell belongs to a ternary over two *other*
constants.

Corollary, and the reason this matters: when the callee returns a pointer, `!= 0`
is the only one of the four that is also correct C. The 13-member
`Proc_Find` existence-predicate family at 0x08078150-0x0808AA88 is all short
form, and `src/decomp/c_080457A4.c` already recorded this correctly.

**Both of those tables are the `bl f; cmp; beq; mov #1` shape. There is a
THIRD, BRANCHLESS shape for a returned `!=`, and it is not a different source
spelling — the same `return x != K;` produces one or the other depending on `x`
and `K`.** It is `(t | -t) >> 31` with `t = x ^ K`, i.e.

```
mvn r0, r0 ; neg r1, r0 ; orr r1, r1, r0 ; lsr r1, r1, #0x1f   <- x != -1
mov r1,#5 ; eor r0,r0,r1 ; neg r1,r0 ; orr r1,r1,r0 ; lsr #0x1f <- x != 5
lsl r1,#0x18 ; lsr r1,#0x18 ; neg r0,r1 ; orr r0,r0,r1 ; lsr #0x1f  <- (u8)x != 0
```

Two independent triggers, one probe, fourteen spellings, agbcc `-O2`:

| `return … ;` | shape |
|---|---|
| `x != 0`, `x` a plain `int` — parameter, local, or a `bl` result | **branching** |
| `!!x`, `x ? 1 : 0` on the same `int` | branching — identical to the row above |
| `(x & 0xff) != 0`, `(x ^ y) != 0`, `(x - 1) != 0`, `(x >> 3) != 0` | branching — *computing* the operand is NOT the trigger |
| `x != -1`, `x != 1`, `x != 5` — any **non-zero** constant | **branchless** |
| `(u8)x != 0`, `(s8)x != 0`, or `x != 0` on a `u8` **parameter** | **branchless** |
| `x == 0`, `x == -1` — `==` in any form | branching, and it costs an extra `mov rD, #0` |
| `x < 0` | neither: a lone `lsr r0, r0, #0x1f` |

So the triggers are **a non-zero compare constant** or **a narrowing conversion
on the operand** — and an explicit mask that computes the same value as the cast
is *not* one of them, which is the counter-intuitive half. `mvn` rather than
`eor` is just `x ^ -1` peepholed, so **`mvns` followed by `neg`/`orr`/`lsr #31`
reads directly as `!= -1`.**

Family F020 (seven 32-byte leaves: `sub_08019850`, `sub_0803ACD0`,
`sub_0803B16C`, `sub_0803C2FC`, `sub_0804B160`, `sub_080670D8`, `sub_0806E198`)
is the whole shape in one line — `return <lookup>(script) != -1;` — with the
`lsls #N; asrs #N` in front of the `mvns` being the callee's signed return width
re-extended at the call site (`#0x18` for an `s8`-returning callee, `#0x10` for
an `s16` one). Probed and byte-identical there, so none of them is evidence:
`bool8` vs `int` return, and binding the call result to an `s8`/`s16` local
before the compare. The explicit `if (…) return TRUE; return FALSE;` spelling is
*not* — it emits the branching four-block form from the table above and is four
bytes longer.

**"Branching" in that table does NOT mean "both arms and an unconditional
