## `member * 0x100` and `member << 8` into a NARROW destination differ by `ldrsh` vs `ldrh` — and it was worth 74 percentage points (wave 54, W54-D)

The existing rule in this doc says "`g * 0x100` is not `g << 8` for a narrow
global — `shorten_binary_op` applies to `MULT_EXPR` and not to shifts." This is
the same mechanism on a narrow struct MEMBER with a narrow DESTINATION, and the
symptom is different enough to be worth its own heading, because it does not
look like a shorten_binary_op problem at all — it looks like the member has the
wrong signedness.

`sub_080860DC` stores into a `volatile u16` global:

```
ROM     bl sub_08087298 ; movs r2,#0 ; ldrsh r1,[r7,r2] ; lsls r1,#8
                        ; adds r0,r0,r1 ; strh r0,[r4]
```

`p->unk4e` is `s16`, so `ldrsh` is what its type says. Written honestly as
`gUnknown_03002F18 = sub_08087298() + (p->unk4e << 8);` agbcc emits **`ldrh`**:
the destination is 16 bits wide, so combine's `force_to_mode` runs with a
0xFFFF mask over `(ashift (sign_extend (mem:HI)) 8)`, only the low 8 bits of the
memory operand can survive the shift, and a `zero_extend` is then good enough.
The declared signedness of the member is simply discarded.

**Spelling it as a multiply gets the sign back.** `shorten_binary_op` fires on
`MULT_EXPR`, does the arithmetic in the operand's own HImode, and keeps its
signedness, so `sub_08087298() + p->unk4e * 0x100` emits `ldrsh` and then the
same `lsls #8`. On this function that ONE edit took the candidate from -20
bytes / 24.6% to size-exact / 98.2%, because the two `ldrh`/`ldrsh` sites are in
the two arms that dominate the layout.

A third spelling was measured and is the WRONG fix even though it also restores
the `ldrsh`: routing the sum through an `int` local and storing that. It adds an
`lsls #16; lsrs #16` truncation at the store and sinks the destination's address
`ldr` below the `bl` (c_080867BC.c's rule, in reverse). +8 bytes.

**Read backwards: an `ldrh` in your candidate where the ROM has `ldrsh`, on a
member you have already typed signed, is not a type error — it is a shift that
should have been a multiply.**

---

## A shared tail after an if/else-if chain must be WRITTEN OUT in each arm, not left as one trailing statement (wave 54, W54-D)

Two functions this wave (`sub_08084C14`, `sub_080860DC`) have an if/else-if
chain where several arms end with the same two or three calls and the ROM has
exactly one copy of them. The tempting spelling is

```c
if (a) { ...; }
else if (b) { ...; }
else if (c) { ...; return; }
else return;
shared_tail();          /* one copy */
```

and it is wrong twice over. The single copy lands **after every arm in the
chain**, where the ROM has it immediately after the last arm that reaches it;
and giving the final arm an `else return;` turns its fallthrough into a jump,
which lets the post-reload cross-jump pass merge that arm's tail with an earlier
one — the ROM does not merge them, because the last arm falls THROUGH to the
epilogue and `cross_jump` has no jump insn to pair it with.

**Write the tail out at the end of each arm that needs it and let cross-jumping
merge them.** It places the merge point correctly and it leaves the last arm's
fallthrough alone. On `sub_080860DC` this was worth 20 bytes and moved the whole
back half of the function into place.

## A WRAPPER STRUCT with a leading filler is the only spelling that hoists a column offset onto the BASE when the column is VARIABLE (wave 54, W54-G)

The `gUnknown_085D6A48` column-offset problem has been worked three times
(W33-F, W34-A, W37-J3) and every one of those rounds had a CONSTANT inner
subscript. `sub_080553C8` is the first with a VARIABLE one, and the answer is a
different spelling from all five in the W37-J3 table.

The ROM reads `gUnknown_085D6A48[row][col + 5]` twice in adjacent statements and
computes the address as

    ldrh col ; lsls #1 ; ldrh row ; lsls/adds/lsls #3 ; adds ; adds r3,#0xa ; adds

i.e. `col * 2` first, then `row * 24`, then **`base + 10` as its own CSE'd
pseudo shared by both statements**. Four spellings measured with `compile_probe`
against that, same declaration (`u16 [][12]`, left unchanged):

| spelling | index order | where the +10 lands |
|---|---|---|
| `g[row][col + 5]` | correct (col, row, base) | `adds rC, #5` on the COLUMN, **per statement** |
| `((struct Row *)g)[row].unk0a[col]` | wrong (row, base, col) | `adds #0xa`, per statement |
| `(rows = (struct Row *)g, rows)[row].unk0a[col]` | wrong (row, base, col) | `adds #0xa`, per statement |
| `*(g[row] + col + 5)` | wrong (row, col, base) | folded into the POOL WORD, `g+0xa` |
| **`((struct Tbl *)g)->cells[row][col]`**, `struct Tbl { u8 filler_00[0xa]; u16 cells[8][12]; }` | **correct** | **`adds rB, #0xa` on the BASE, CSE'd across both statements** |

**The lever is `->` on a wrapper struct, not `[]` on a row struct.** The row
struct (W37-J3's spelling) makes the record a subscripted ARRAY element, so the
outer index expands before the base and the whole index order inverts. The
wrapper keeps a single `COMPONENT_REF` at the top and leaves the two subscripts
underneath it untouched, so the array machinery still expands inner-then-outer
while the member's byte offset is applied to the base pointer — where `fold`
then reassociates it out of the address PLUS and CSE picks it up.

This is the wave-35 W35-I wrapper-struct rule ("a WRAPPER STRUCT reaches the
hoisted member offset on a PLAIN ARRAY GLOBAL") extended to the case W35-I did
not cover: a *variable* subscript below the member. `sub_080553C8` matched on
the attempt that used it. `gUnknown_085D6A48` still does not need retyping.

## `(s16)` on a `u16` STRUCT MEMBER does compile to `ldrsh` — the wave-30 "s16-OBJECT tell" does not hold for a member feeding a float conversion (wave 54, W54-G)

Two chapters disagree and the disagreement is now resolved by probe.

- Wave 37 (W37-A): "`sign_extend (mem:HI)` always folds to `ldrsh`, so the
  declared signedness of the member is irrelevant."
- Wave 30 (W30-A) and the `union Unk802C57CBuf` note in
  `include/unknown-globals.h`: "`movs rI,#0 / ldrsh rD,[rB,rI]` is the
  s16-OBJECT tell ... an (s16) cast on a u16 member would emit
  `ldrh; lsls #16; asrs #16` instead."

**Wave 37 is right and the "s16-OBJECT tell" is not a tell.** Probed on
`gUnknown_0200F720[a5].unk04`, declared `u16`:

    (float)(s16)g[a5].unk04   ->  movs r1,#4 ; ldrsh r0,[r0,r1] ; bl __floatsisf
    (float)g[a5].unk04        ->  movs r1,#4 ; ldrsh r4,[r0,r1] ; bl __floatsisf
                                  cmp r4,#0 ; bge .L ; ldr r1,=6.5536e4 ; bl __addsf3

Both give `ldrsh` with the register-offset form, which THUMB has no immediate
form of, so the `movs rI,#k` is forced addressing and carries no type
information at all. What DOES discriminate is the other direction: the
**uncast** `u16` read adds an unsigned-correction branch (`+ 65536.0f` when the
sign bit is set) before the float is used. So on a member feeding a float
conversion, the absence of that correction proves an `(s16)` cast or an `s16`
member, and its presence proves an unsigned one — but the `ldrsh` itself proves
neither. Found while deriving `sub_0801E508`, which meant `struct Unk0200F720`
did NOT have to be retyped to settle it.

## A three-term address sum puts the BASE LAST only when there is NO pointer local (wave 54, W54-H)

`sub_08054598` reads `gUnknown_02029A10[side].entries[slot]` five times. The ROM
builds the address as

```
ldr  r2, =gUnknown_02029A10      @ base loaded FIRST
lsls r1, r0, #3; add r1, r8; lsls r1, r1, #2   @ slot * 36
movs r0, #0xb4; muls r0, r7, r0                @ side * 180
adds r1, r1, r0                  @ the two INDEX terms summed
adds r1, r1, r2                  @ ... and only then the base
```

i.e. `(slot*36 + side*180) + base`. Six spellings were probed against that:

| spelling | tree |
|---|---|
| `e = &g[a].entries[b];` | `a*180 + (b*36 + base)` |
| `e = g[a].entries + b;` | same |
| `e = &g->entries[a*5 + b];` | one combined `*36` |
| `e = (T *)((u8 *)g + a*sizeof(Group)) + b;` | same as the first |
| `g2 = &g[a]; e = &g2->entries[b];` | `(base + a*180) + b*36` |
| **no local — the full expression at every use** | **`(b*36 + a*180) + base`** |

Only the last one is the ROM, and it is the ROM at every one of the five sites.
`fold` reassociates the ARRAY_REF chain so that the ADDR_EXPR pairs with the
INNER index; binding the result to a pointer local freezes that pairing, and
writing the expression out lets CSE build the offset first and add the base
once at the end. **A pointer local is not free even when it is dead after one
statement** — this is the "binding locals are punctuation" rule showing up as an
address-tree shape rather than as a register.

Corollary for the `2 * (i + K)` case, which came up twice this wave: agbcc 2.9
does **not** distribute the element scale over an added constant. `g[side][i+9]`
emits `(i + 9) * 2`, four instructions, and keeps the bare symbol in the pool;
the ROM's single folded pool word at `&g + 18` can only come from a **row
symbol** declared at that address and subscripted `[i]`. Two symbols were
carved this wave on exactly that evidence: `gUnknown_020296CE`
(== `gUnknown_020296BC` + 0x12) and `gUnknown_085D6A52` (== `gUnknown_085D6A48`
+ 0xa, i.e. column 5 of its 24-byte rows).

## `x = <rhs>;` as its OWN statement swaps the source and the destination address (wave 54, W54-H)

`expand_assignment` expands the destination MEM before `store_expr` evaluates
the value, so `dest = src;` always emits the destination's address arithmetic
first. When the ROM shows the **source** first, the original bound it:

```
                         ROM (sub_08055A38, the row[2] == 1 arm)
lsls r0, r6, #2 ; adds r0, r0, r2 ; add r0, r8 ; ldrh r1, [r0]   @ source
lsls r0, r3, #1 ; adds r0, r0, r4 ; add r0, ip ; strh r1, [r0]   @ dest
```

`x = gUnknown_085521B4[side][i][0]; gUnknown_020298E0[side].unk1a[out] = x;`
reproduces it; folding the subscript into the store does not. **The two are the
same SIZE and the same instruction multiset** — this is the wave-54 brief's
"instruction ORDER around a pool load" failure mode, and a size match is not
evidence the statement split is right. It was worth 85.7% -> the whole tail on
`sub_08055A38` and it is the difference between a wrong and a byte-exact tail on
`sub_08054C5C`.

**But a NESTED CALL is the wrong way to spell the same thing.** For a chained
`u16` result the ROM has `adds r3, r0, #0; lsls r3,#0x10; lsrs r3,#0x10` — copy
into the argument register, then narrow in place, which is a temporary with no
home of its own. Three spellings, measured on `sub_08054C5C`'s tail:

- reusing the running local `t`: narrows into `t`'s register (r7) and then
  copies to r3 — same count, wrong bytes;
- `g(1, a[1], b[1], f(0, a[0], b[0], 0))`: agbcc loads `a[1]` and `b[1]` into
  callee-saved registers **before** the inner `bl`, which the ROM does after;
- **a second short-lived local** (`u = f(...); g(..., u);`): exact.

## OPEN: which of two equal pool words loop.c hoists is not reachable from source (wave 54, W54-H)

Two functions in the 0x08054-0x08055 run are size-wrong by 8 bytes each, with
every statement settled, and both residuals are the same thing: the ROM and the
candidate hoist a **different one** of two address constants that are symmetric
under every input `move_movables` can see (one use apiece, lifetime 1 apiece,
same loop, same pre-hoist insn count).

**The readout is the pool slot order**, which is pseudo-creation order: a word
hoisted into the preheader sorts before every word left in the loop body.

- `sub_08054C5C` (568/560, 87.5%): ROM hoists `gUnknown_085D6A48`, candidate
  hoists `gUnknown_085D6A52`.
- `sub_08055768` (464/472, 30.1% — positional, the shortfall moves every later
  byte): ROM hoists five invariants and leaves BOTH `gUnknown_08552150` and
  `gUnknown_02029A10` in the loop; the candidate hoists one of them, which frees
  r2 as a long-lived register and removes the `mov r2, ip` the ROM pays to read
  a high register. Inlining the value read flips WHICH of the two is hoisted but
  never gets to neither.

Both are **stable fixpoints**: hoisting one fewer word raises the body's scratch
demand, which is what makes the ROM's allocation the worse of the two, so no
allocation lever can walk from one to the other. decomp-permuter found nothing
in 300 s on either. Levers refuted: the wave-17 struct-row spelling (hoists
neither), inlining a one-use local, and reordering the addends. Recorded so the
next agent does not re-derive the decompositions, which are correct.

**Wave 63 correction: the first `sub_08055768` fixpoint is reachable with the
wave-59 opaque-store LICM barrier.** Adding the zero-code
`gUnknown_08551E64[0][0] += 0` inside each scan loop takes the draft from
464/472 to 468/472 and makes loop 1 instruction-for-instruction exact: both
address constants remain in its body, and the ROM's pool order and register
allocation follow. It does not close loop 2: that loop still cross-jumps a
two-instruction shared tail the ROM keeps separate. Moving the barrier within
the loop or spelling the opaque address through `x`, `out`, or `side` is
byte-identical; a zero-trip `do/while` around the conditional and block-scoping
`x` both regress allocation. Thus "not reachable from source" was too broad:
the first LICM decision is reachable, while the second allocation/cross-jump
decision remains open.

## `p + K` as a value: the bound-pointer spelling (wave 55, W55-C)

`ldrb rD, [rB]` where the address was built as `adds rA, rB, #K` / `adds rA, rA, rI`
is NOT the same source as `ldrb rD, [rB, #K]` after `adds rA, rI, rB`, even
though both are `p[K + i]` semantically. For K that fits an `ldrb` displacement
(0..31) agbcc will fold it into the load, so the ROM building the address in full
means the source bound `p + K` to its own pointer variable.

Measured with `compile_probe`, four spellings of `p[1 + *q]`:

    p[1 + *q]          -> ldrb r1,[r1]; add r1,r1,r0; ldrb r0,[r1,#1]
    *(p + 1 + *q)      -> IDENTICAL to the above -- fold reassociates
                          `(p + 1) + x` into `(p + x) + 1`
    r = p + 1; r[*q]   -> add r0,r0,#1; ldrb r1,[r1]; add r0,r0,r1; ldrb r0,[r0]
    i = *q; r = p + 1; r[i]  -> same as the third

So the parenthesised inline form does not work; only a **separate assignment to a
pointer local** keeps `p + K` out of fold's reach, because fold never sees the
two operands in one tree. This closed the whole address-arithmetic half of
sub_0805FC1C and recurs three more times in the 0x0805Dxxx-0x0805Fxxx block
(sub_0805EB58's +0x12 plane, sub_0805DCD4's +0x12 plane in both of its scans).

The corollary is the diagnostic: **a struct member array at offset <= 31 read
with a variable index produces the folded `[rB, #K]` form**, so a ROM that
materialises the base is telling you the source did not spell it as a member.
Above 31 the constant has to be materialised anyway and the ordinary member
spelling is correct -- sub_0805FC1C and sub_0805EB58 both mix the two in one
statement (+0x12 bound, +0x1432 as a member).

Read it in expression order too: the ROM emits `adds rA, rB, #K` at the point of
the ASSIGNMENT, so where that add sits relative to the index computation tells
you whether the binding statement comes before or after the index's.

## `if (c) X else Y`: which arm the ROM inlines (wave 55, W55-C)

agbcc emits `if (c) X else Y` as *jump-if-false to Y*, with **X inline** and Y
placed after it. So when the ROM reaches a block by a jump-if-TRUE and has the
other arm inline, the source condition is the OTHER one and the arms are
swapped from the way you first wrote them.

sub_0805F914 has `cmp r0,#0x10; beq <block placed after the literal pool>` with
the scoring arm inline. Written the natural way round --
`if (unk00 != 0 && tbl->unk1a == 0x10) v = 0; else v = <score>;` -- agbcc emits
`bne <else>` with `v = 0` inline, which is a whole-block mismatch. Inverting it
to `if (unk00 == 0 || tbl->unk1a != 0x10) v = <score>; else v = 0;` reproduces
the ROM exactly. This is cheap to check and is not visible in a byte percentage:
both spellings are the same length.

## `(s8)g[y][x]` versus `((s8 *)g[y])[x]` are different code (wave 55, W55-C)

`gUnknown_03003340` is declared `u8 *[]` and its readers need signed cells. The
two spellings are NOT interchangeable and the ROM uses both, sometimes in one
function:

    (s8)g[y][x]        -> ldr; adds; ldrb; lsls #24; asrs #24   (4 insns)
    ((s8 *)g[y])[x]    -> ldr; adds; movs rZ,#0; ldrsb rD,[rA,rZ]  (4 insns)

combine folds `sign_extend (mem:QI)` into `ldrsb` -- inventing the zero index
register that THUMB's register-offset-only `ldrsb` needs -- but it does NOT fold
`(ashiftrt (ashift (zero_extend (mem:QI)) 24) 24)` back into a sign_extend, so
the value cast survives as the shift pair. Contrast the wave-37 finding for
HImode, where `ldrh; lsls; asrs` is NEVER an `(s16)` cast because
`sign_extend (mem:HI)` always folds; the QImode case is the opposite and the
shift pair IS the cast. sub_0805EB58 uses `(s8)g[y][x]` for its `< 0` guard and
for the `best` store but `((s8 *)g[y])[x]` for the compare against `best`;
sub_0805F914 uses the pointer cast in its first scan and the value cast in its
second.

## `(u8)(x - 0x80)` in one expression emits `add #0x80`; the ROM's `subs #0x80` needs the subtraction as its OWN statement (wave 55, W55-A)

`sub_08073E0C` reads a signed-offset PCM sample as `sample - 0x80` truncated to
eight bits. The ROM is

    ldrb r1, [r0]
    subs r1, #0x80
    lsls r1, r1, #0x18
    lsrs r3, r1, #0x18

and the obvious spelling does not produce it. Eight variants were probed
(`compile_probe`, `u8 *p`):

| source | opcode |
|---|---|
| `(u8)(p[0] - 0x80)` | `add r0, r0, #0x80` |
| `(u8)(p[0] + 0x80)` | `add` |
| `(u8)(p[0] - 0x80U)` | `add` |
| `(u8)(p[0] - 0x7F - 1)` | `add` |
| `u8 v; v = p[0]; v -= 0x80;` | `add` |
| `(p[0] - 0x80) & 0xFF` | `sub`, but `mov r1,#0xff; and` instead of the shift pair |
| **`int t = p[0]; t -= 0x80; (u8)t`** | **`sub` + `lsl #0x18` + `lsr #0x18`** |

The rule: once the QImode truncation is part of the SAME expression as the
addition, fold normalises the constant modulo 256, and -0x80 and +0x80 are the
same residue, so agbcc always prints `add`. Splitting the subtraction into its
own statement on an `int` puts the `minus` in SImode where the constant cannot
be renormalised; the `(u8)` at the later use then emits the shift pair on its
own. The same split is why `combine` can serve `(u8)t >> 1` out of the SImode
`lsl #0x18` result with a single `lsrs #0x19` rather than a second shift pair.

This is the byte-width twin of the wave-16 "count `lsls #a`/`lsrs #b` as
`x << a >> b`" rule: read the shift pair as the truncation and then ask which
STATEMENT the arithmetic belongs to, not just what the arithmetic is.

## `cmp rX, #lo; blt default; cmp rX, #hi; bgt default` on an UNSIGNED value is a `switch`, never an `if` (wave 55, W55-A)

`sub_08074038` tests a `u16` parameter twice:

    cmp r7, #0        @ r7 is the zero-extended u16 parameter
    blt _default
    cmp r7, #5
    bgt _default

An `if (a3 >= 0 && a3 <= 5)` cannot produce it — with a `u16` operand agbcc
folds `>= 0` away and warns `comparison is always true due to limited range of
data type`, which is fatal under `-Werror`. Making the parameter `s16` produces
the two compares but then sign-extends the parameter (`lsl #0x10; asr #0x10`) at
EVERY other use, which the ROM does not do. `if (n <= 5)` on the `u16` emits a
single unsigned `cmp #5; bhi`.

What does produce it, exactly, is

    switch (n)
    {
    case 0:            ...  break;
    case 1: case 2: case 3: case 4: case 5:
                       ...  break;
    default:           ...  break;
    }

`expand_end_case` emits `cmp n, #0; bne` for the case-0 node and then bounds the
1..5 group with the SIGNED pair above, using the enclosing node's low bound
(0, not 1). Probed directly: a three-way `if` chain and the `switch` differ by
exactly these two instructions.

**So a signed two-sided range test on a value that provably cannot be negative
is a case-node bound.** It is also the cheapest switch tell there is, because a
five-case group with one body emits no jump table.

## Address arithmetic: `sym + const` as an ADDRESS CONSTANT defeats strength reduction; a bare biv subscript does not (wave 55, W55-A)

Two functions in this batch turned on the same distinction.

**`sub_08075AC4`.** The ROM keeps the palette base in the literal pool and adds a
byte-offset giv:

    ldr r2, =gPal
    add r2, sb          @ sb = 0x1F2, decremented by 2 each iteration
    strh r0, [r2]

Writing the subscript as `gPal[0xF0 + i]` (equivalently `gPal[15 * 16 + i]`)
makes the address `gPal + 480 + 2*i`. The `gPal + 480` part is an address
CONSTANT with a non-zero addend, `-fforce-addr` parks it in this unit's
`.rodata` and reloads it through two instructions every iteration, and no giv is
formed for the index at all — 8 bytes and a completely different loop. Writing
`gPal[n]` where `n` is a bare induction variable keeps `gPal` a plain relocated
pool word and lets `strength_reduce` build the `n * 2` byte offset as a giv.
Same story for `gUnknown_0200B614[n * 3]` beside it, and because both givs are
initialised from the same `n`, agbcc CSEs their inits into the ROM's
`movs r1, #0xf9; lsls r1, r1, #1; adds r1, #0xf9` chain (`n*2` then `n*3`)
instead of pooling `0x2EB` as a literal.

**`sub_08073E0C`.** The mirror case. `gUnknown_03004790.pcmBuffer[1][i]` folds to
the address constant `gUnknown_03004790+0x980` and emits it as a single pool
word; the ROM instead loads a pointer and adds 0x350 and 0x630 at RUNTIME
(`movs #0xd4; lsls #2` / `movs #0xc6; lsls #3`). Under `-fforce-addr` agbcc
builds the `.rodata` indirection word only for a STORE destination — a plain
LOAD of a global takes the direct literal-pool path, and both paths are visible
for `gUnknown_0202FDE4` inside that one function. So runtime-added member
offsets on a load mean the source named a POINTER, not the object.

**Diagnostic, both directions:** a `movs`/`lsls` pair materialising a struct
member offset says the base is a runtime value. An offset that never appears as
an instruction says it was folded into an address constant, and then
`-fforce-addr` — not your subscript — decides how the base is reached.

## `a - (i + K)` is reassociated to `(a - K) - i` and then hoisted — bind `i + K` to its own local, and use a SEPARATE local per site (wave 55, W55-A)

`sub_08074038` computes `a4 - (i + 3)` and `a4 - (i + 1)` after a loop that
varies `i`. Written that way, fold turns each into `(a4 - K) - i`, the loop pass
then hoists `a4 - 3` and `a4 - 1` into the preheader as loop invariants, and
both need stack slots — `sub sp, #0x20` where the ROM has `#0x1c`. The ROM's

    adds r0, r6, #3
    mov  r1, r8
    subs r0, r1, r0

only comes back if `i + K` is bound to a local first (`k = i + 3;` then
`a4 - k`), because fold cannot associate through a VAR_DECL.

**And the local must not be shared with a different site.** The same function
needs a second temp inside a loop, where `j = i + 1; call(); i = j;` is what
splits the `adds` before the `bl` from the `lsls`/`lsrs` after it (a plain
`for (i = 0; ...; i++)` emits all three together at the loop bottom). Reusing
ONE local `j` for both the loop and the straight-line block unions their live
ranges: the union crosses a call, the pseudo takes a callee-saved register, `i`
and the `u16` bound get pushed up, the bound lands in a HIGH register where every
`cmp rX, #imm` then needs a `mov` first, and a parameter is spilled. Two
separate `int` locals — one live across the call, one dying immediately — match
byte-for-byte. **A binding local is punctuation (wave 17), and punctuation that
serves two sentences is a different mark from punctuation that serves one.**

## `check_dbra_loop` does NOT renumber a descending counted loop whose bound is non-zero (wave 55, W55-A)

`for (i = 0xF9; i >= 0xF0; i--)` keeps its own numbering: `movs r0, #0xf9` and
`cmp r1, #0xEF; ble`. It is NOT rewritten to count 9..0 even when every use of
`i` has been strength-reduced into givs — the standing intuition that gcc
normalises such a loop to a count-down-to-zero is wrong here.

`sub_08075AC4`'s ROM counts `movs r0, #9 ... cmp r1, #0; blt`, so the original
source has TWO variables: a counter `for (i = 9; i >= 0; i--)` and a separate
index `n = 0xF9; ... n--;` used for both subscripts. `n` is a biv whose only uses
are givs and is eliminated; `i` survives as the counter. The pair costs nothing
because `n` never occupies a register.

This is the wave-49 "two disjoint counters are usually ONE local" rule read in
reverse: two SIMULTANEOUS counters over the same loop really are two locals, and
the tell is a loop trip count that matches the counter's range while the address
givs are initialised from a different constant.

## Literal pool ORDER reads out source evaluation order (wave 55, W55-C)

Pool words are emitted in order of **first reference** in the insn stream. That
makes the pool a direct readout of the order in which the source evaluates its
subexpressions -- and because a byte-identity score is positional, one word out
of place shifts every later `ldr rN, [pc, #X]` immediate and reports near-total
mismatch on a function whose code is already right.

`sub_0805F914` sat at **13.7% identical and matched in one attempt** once the
operands of a single `&` were swapped. The ROM's pool opens
085D5ABC / 030040D8 / 08499590; the draft's opened 08499590 / 030040D8 /
085D5ABC, because the guard had been written

    (map->unk3262[...] & gUnknown_085D5ABC[p->unk00].unk1d) == 0

and the ROM's source is the other way round. `expand_expr` for a binary op
evaluates operand 0 then operand 1 with no interleaving, so for any commutative
operator over two *globals* the pool tells you which side the original wrote
first. Check this before touching a statement.

**Do NOT try to read operand order off the destination register.** The ROM's
instruction is `ands r0, r1` with the result in the CELL's register even though
the cell is operand 1 -- `expand_binop` commutes freely to pick a target. The
same reasoning applied to `sub_0805EB58`'s `(u16)x | (y << 16)` predicted a swap
would help; the swap was tried and measured *worse* (97.9% -> 97.1%). Pool order
is the reliable signal; target register is not.

The complementary case, also wave 55: a `.rodata` relocation in the candidate
where the ROM names a `gUnknown_0816Dxxx`-style symbol is usually NOT a defect --
that is the -fforce-addr address word, and `trymatch` reports `relocs: name
different symbols that resolve to the same address` and accepts it (sub_0805FFA0
and sub_0805F914 both matched that way). What matters is whether the words are
in the same POSITIONS, not what they are called.

## A `.rodata` reloc against a `-fforce-addr` word is the HONEST spelling, not a defect (wave 55, W55-E)

Wave 55 established mid-wave that a file-local literal written where the ROM
names a global in one of agbcc's address-constant blobs is a top cause of
misses. That is real, but the screen it proposed — "original says
`R_ARM_ABS32 gUnknown_081CCxxx`, yours says `R_ARM_ABS32 .rodata`, therefore you
invented a literal" — **produces false positives, and it produced one on
`sub_08073E0C` in the same wave.** That draft already named `gUnknown_0202FDE4`
directly; 0x081CC034 is the unit's own `-fforce-addr` copy of its address, and
`.rodata` is precisely what the honest spelling emits. There was no symbol to
declare and nothing to respell.

**The discriminator is the pool word LIST plus the SIZE, never a single reloc
line:**

- **Lists identical in symbol, order and count, differing only in the first
  entry's spelling, and the candidate is size-SHORT** → honest `-fforce-addr`
  word. The pool is a symptom. `promote.py` will carry it and
  `tools/split_rodata.py` will carve it. Go and find the missing CODE.
- **The list gained a word, lost a word, or reordered** → genuine local-literal
  defect. Name the global.

A one-for-one substitution of a pool word cannot change the function's size, so
**a size delta proves the defect is in the instruction stream** however loudly
the reloc lines disagree. Confirm it with `first difference at +N`: if N is the
offset of the first `ldr rN,[pc,#X]`, every later "difference" is the positional
shadow of the shift and the byte-identity percentage is meaningless.

## agbcc MIN/MAX: `a >= b ? a : b` compares the TARGET COPY, and you cannot move that (wave 55, W55-E)

`fold` rewrites `a >= b ? a : b` to `MAX_EXPR<a,b>` (and `a <= b ? a : b` to
`MIN_EXPR`). With no `smaxsi3`/`sminsi3` pattern on THUMB, `expand_expr` emits

```
    mov T, a          /* target := op0                          */
    cmp T, b          /* compare_from_rtx (TARGET, op1) — NOT a  */
    b<ge|le> L
    mov T, b
L:  mov acc, T
```

— five instructions, and **the comparison is always against the target copy,
never against the value's own register.** CSE then substitutes the value's home
register into the first compare of a pair (they are equivalent and the home is
canonical) but not into the second, because the conditional's join label ends
the extended basic block and clears the table. So the signature output of a
`max` / `min` pair on one value is **ten instructions, first compare on the
home register, second on its own preset** — and that is invariant.

Nine spellings were measured against a ROM shape that has **eleven**: two
presets plus a *third* register holding the value, shared by both compares
(`sub_08073E0C`). None reproduces it:

- `int` values with `(u32)` casts on the condition only — 10, and the second
  group loses its preset entirely.
- `u8` values — the right instruction COUNT, but the extra copy lands at the
  DEFINITION, not in the min/max block, and it costs a fourth high register.
- Nested `?:` (`(va > maxa) ? va : (maxa >= va) ? maxa : va`) — 6 per group.
- `(va < maxa) ? maxa : va` and `((ca = va) < maxa) ? maxa : va` — fold
  canonicalises both back to the identical MAX_EXPR output.
- **A separate condition variable (`ca = va; maxa = (ca >= maxa) ? va : maxa;`)
  is the trap.** It defeats `fold`'s MIN/MAX recognition, so expansion drops to
  the COND_EXPR path — which presets the **accumulator** and conditionally
  stores the value, the mirror image of what you wanted, in 4 instructions per
  group. Copy propagation then folds `ca` back to `va` anyway, so the local buys
  nothing at all.

**Practical consequence:** if the ROM shows a min/max pair whose two compares
share a register that is neither preset, do not spend attempts on ternary
spellings — the shape does not come from the ternary. Note also that
`>`/`<` gives `bhi`/`blo` where `>=`/`<=` gives `bhs`/`bls`, which settles the
operator from the branch with no probing.

## Association and operand order — five wave-55 rules, each worth a function

These are all cases where the C is semantically identical and the bytes are not.
None of them is visible in a probe of the expression alone; all five were
measured against a real target.

- **When one block of a repeated series is spelled in different UNITS from its
  siblings, respell it in the siblings' units before touching anything else.**
  `sub_080791B0` sat at 99.0% for a wave with seven bytes differing: the two
  source givs of one copy block got r5 and r6 the other way round. Same
  instructions, same order, same pool words. The block was written
  `gUnknown_0200FC50 + 0x3000 + i * 0x80` while its four neighbours were written
  `gUnknown_0200FC50 + (0x180 + i * 4) * 0x20` — the same address, since
  `0x3000 == 0x180 * 0x20`. Respelling it in the neighbours' units changed the
  order the two givs enter the RTL, which changed the allocno numbers, which
  broke the r5/r6 priority tie the other way, and it matched. **A diagnosis of
  "two pointer locals are in the wrong order" can be right about the mechanism
  and unusable as an instruction: there were no pointer locals in that
  function, only givs, and no declaration order exists to swap.**

- **`v + C + j` and `j + C + v` produce OPPOSITE code, and the one that matches
  reads backwards.** agbcc reassociates `A + C + B` into `(B + C) + A`, so to
  get the ROM's `adds r2, v, #0; adds r2, #41; adds r2, j, r2` the source must
  name the LOOP COUNTER FIRST: `j + 0x29 + v`. Four copies of one loop in
  `sub_080872D0` were fixed by that single flip. Do not reason forwards from
  the emitted order to the source order for a three-term add.

- **An arithmetic insn that lands in the MIDDLE of a loop preheader was not
  authored — write the expression inline at its uses instead.** The preheader
  is source statements, then LICM hoists, then `strength_reduce`'s inits, so a
  source statement can never appear between two hoists. `sub_080872D0`'s
  `subs r6, #8` sits between the two halves of one hoisted address-load chain.
  Written as the statement `w -= 8;` it comes out first, ten bytes wrong in
  both branches; written inline as `w - 8` at the two places the following loop
  needs it (the bound and the `j + 1 == w - 8` last-iteration test) gcse places
  the single copy in the dominating block, which is exactly that slot. **Read
  backwards this is a cheap diagnostic for the whole class.**

- **`cond ? A : B` takes its branch polarity from the condition AS WRITTEN.**
  `i == 0 ? 0x6088 : 0x6089` emits `cmp; bne` to the 0x6089 arm; the ROM's
  `cmp; beq` to the 0x6088 arm needs `i != 0 ? 0x6089 : 0x6088`. Same C,
  different bytes, and the literal-pool word order follows the arm order.

- **A `?:` selecting an ARRAY BASE must be its own statement.** Written inline,
  `t = (f(x) ? A : B)[i];` makes agbcc evaluate the SUBSCRIPT first and hoist
  `i * 2` into a callee-saved register ahead of the `bl`. The ROM evaluates the
  call and the `?:` first and computes the index afterwards, which is what
  splitting it into `p = f(x) ? A : B; t = p[i];` produces. That one split took
  `sub_08085708` from 91.9% at exact size to a match, and the register swap
  three instructions downstream fixed itself — it was a consequence, not a
  second defect.

### Two folds that no spelling defeats (negative results, wave 55)

Both measured with `compile_probe` over four spellings each. Recording them so
nobody spends another round: the lever is not in the expression.

- **`C1 - (x - C2) * C3` always folds.** agbcc distributes the multiply over the
  subtraction, combines the constants, and — when the result exceeds 255 —
  emits a literal-pool word, which costs 4 bytes against a ROM that kept
  `adds #C1` and `subs #C2` separate. `(x - C2) << k` folds identically, so this
  is NOT the `g * 0x100` / `g << 8` lever; that rule is about
  `shorten_binary_op` on a narrow operand and does not reach a fold over a
  subtraction. Same for `A - (B - 1)`, which agbcc turns into `(A + 1) - B`
  under every cast placement tried, including `(int)(B - 1)` and `(int)(A - (B - 1))`.

- **In `shift | (tile | C)` the constant always attaches to the SHIFT term**,
  whichever way round the two operands are written and whether the constant
  leads or trails. The ROM's grouping — shift computed first, tile second,
  `tile |= C`, then combine — is reproduced EXACTLY, in the ROM's order, by
  using `+` for the outer combine (`shift + (tile | C)`), which then misses by
  the single final opcode (`add` where the ROM has `orr`). That near-miss is the
  useful part of the result: the evaluation order is reachable, only the
  operator is not, so the original almost certainly wrote this through a macro
  whose operands are typed differently.

## BOTH OF THE TWO RESULTS ABOVE WERE REFUTED IN WAVE 55 BY THE SAME ONE LEVER

`sub_080875A4` MATCHED with both of them broken, and `sub_080872D0`'s `A - (B - 1)`
went from unreachable to instruction-exact the same way. The lever is one line:

> **BIND THE SUBEXPRESSION TO A LOCAL. `fold` runs on ONE expression tree, and a
> local assignment is a separate statement, so there is no tree left for
> `associate` to restructure.**

This is not a trick — it is almost certainly what the original source did, and it
generalises to *every* "agbcc always folds X" result in this document. Before
recording a fold as unbeatable, try a local. The three worked cases:

- `C1 - (x - C2) * C3`: `m = x - C2;` then `C1 - m * C3` keeps `subs #C2` and
  `lsls #5` separate and emits NO pool word. Six in-expression spellings had been
  measured as folding.
- `A - (B - 1)`: `k = B - 1;` then `A - k` emits the ROM's `subs r0,#1;
  subs r1,r1,r0` instead of `(A + 1) - B`.
- `shift | (tile | C)`: bind BOTH terms — `u = shift; t = tile | C;` then `u | t`
  — and the constant stays on the tile term, the evaluation order is the ROM's,
  and the outer operator really is `orr`. No macro is needed; the previous
  entry's "must have been a macro" conclusion was wrong.

**TWO COROLLARIES, and skipping either is what costs the extra attempts:**

1. **A local fixes the ASSOCIATION but also pins the ORDER, so bind in the
   ROM's evaluation order.** Statements are emitted in source order, so binding
   only the second operand puts its computation FIRST and the diff moves rather
   than shrinking. In `sub_080872D0` the guard needed `unk37` bound before
   `g - 1` purely for this reason.

2. **Bind SINGLE-ASSIGNMENT. Re-assigning the same local (`x = ...; x = f(x);`)
   costs a `mov`** — gcc gives the incoming value and the local separate
   pseudos and copies between them (`adds r2,r0,#0` ahead of the `adds #216`
   that the ROM does in place). Use a fresh name for the result.
   `sub_080875A4`'s last four bytes were exactly this.

**AND THE COST: each local is a pseudo, and on a register-tight function that
moves the allocation.** `sub_080872D0` is parked at six bytes for this reason —
the fold is beaten and the instruction stream is exact, but whichever local
holds the value inherits a callee-saved register where the ROM used a scratch.
So: use a local to settle the SHAPE first, then count pseudos. See
`work/sub_080872D0/sub_080872D0.c`, which brackets the two spellings.

## Switch statements: block order and cross-jumping (wave 55, sub_08014084)

- **Case bodies are emitted in SOURCE order, not in case-label order, and the
  jump table does not constrain them.** So the ROM's block order IS the order
  the original wrote its cases in, and you can recover it for free: read the
  jump table's targets and sort them by ADDRESS. Do that before writing any
  case. Writing `sub_08014084`'s cases in numeric order put every one of nine
  blocks in the wrong place.

- **Two identical `if`/`else` arms get CROSS-JUMPED, and where the shared tail
  sits in the SOURCE decides whether they do.** With the common tail written
  after the `if`, gcc merges the arms and one copy disappears. With each arm
  carrying its own copy of the tail, gcc keeps both arms in full — while still
  merging the final two-instruction tail into the shared exit. **So a duplicated
  block in the ROM is not evidence of a macro or of hand-written assembly; it is
  evidence about where the `return` was.**

- **`if (x >= C1 && x <= C2)` gets RANGE-FOLDED** into one truncation and one
  unsigned compare against `C2 - C1`. The ROM's two separate signed compares
  need two separate `if` statements with their own early `return`; fold does not
  reach across statements — the same principle as the local-binding lever above.

## A ROM record whose size is not a multiple of 4 cannot be a struct

agbcc inherits the old ARM APCS `STRUCTURE_SIZE_BOUNDARY` of 32 bits, so
`struct { u16 a; u16 b[2]; }` has **sizeof 8, not 6**, and `p++` steps
`adds r0,#8` where the ROM steps `adds r0,#6`. Measured in wave 55 on
`gUnknown_0808FC8C`. Reach such a table as a flat array with a manual stride
(`u16 *p; p += 3;`) and declare it flat in `include/unknown-globals.h`.

## Reading branch polarity: which arm FALLS THROUGH is the tell

gcc emits the test with the branch to the ELSE label and falls through into the
THEN arm. So in a chain of range tests, the arm the ROM falls through to is the
`if` body and the arm it branches to is the `else` — writing
`if (c > K) { deeper } else { shallow }` where the ROM falls through to
`shallow` produces `bls` and the opposite block layout, and inverting all of it
to `if (c <= K) { shallow } else { deeper }` produces the ROM's `bhi`.
Wave 55, `sub_08013D7C`: three nested tests, all three inverted, ~30 bytes.

## `a | b` evaluates the LEFT operand first, and that is visible

`c = s[1] | (s[0] << 8)` and `c = (s[0] << 8) | s[1]` are different code: the
ROM's `ldrb [r6,#1]` before `ldrb [r6,#0]` fixes the narrow term as the LEFT
operand even though the shifted term is what you would naturally write first.
Wave 55, `sub_08013D7C`.

## `arr[i]` and `arr[i + k]` do not share the ROM's address CSE

Written that way agbcc computes the second as `(i + k) * 2 + arr`. The ROM adds
`k * 2` to the already-computed `&arr[i]`. Bind `q = i + arr` and write `q[0]`
and `q[k]`. Wave 55, `sub_08013D7C`.

## A POINTER walk and an ARRAY-GLOBAL subscript are DIFFERENT CODE when the loop reads two bitfields of the same word (wave 55, W55-I)

Two spellings of the same loop that every style guide would call equivalent
produce a 32-byte difference, and the lever is CSE availability, not addressing.

`struct Unk0200C078Rec` is one word split 8/12/12. `sub_08017720` searches a
5-element array of them, reading field 2 (bits 20..31) in the loop guard, again
in an `== ` test, and again in the back-edge test, plus field 1 (bits 8..19)
once. Written against the global array:

```c
for (k = 0; k < 5 && g[b].unk00[k].unk00_14 >= c; k++)
    if (g[b].unk00[k].unk00_14 == c && g[b].unk00[k].unk00_08 > d) break;
```

each field 2 read is `ldrh r0,[r1,#2]; lsrs r0,#4` and each field 1 read is
`ldr r0,[r1]; lsls #0xc; lsrs #0x14` -- three separate, redundant field-2
loads, which is exactly what the ROM has. Bind the base to a pointer first,
either as `e->unk00_14` or as `e[k].unk00_14`, and ALL of it collapses to one
`ldr r0,[r1]; lsrs r1,r0,#20` shared across the whole iteration.

The reason is that a pointer makes one address expression serve both fields.
`get_best_mode` still picks HImode for a 12-bit field at bit 20, but once the
SImode load that field 1 needs is available at the same address, CSE rewrites
the HImode load as an extract from the word already in hand and then deletes
the redundant reloads. With the array-global spelling every read recomputes its
own address, nothing is available, and the redundancy survives.

Read it in both directions:

- **A loop that reads two bitfields of the SAME word and reloads one of them is
  telling you the source did NOT bind a pointer.** Reproduce it with the full
  `g[i].member[k].field` expression.
- **Conversely, one word load feeding several field extracts is the pointer
  spelling.** If your candidate has three loads where the ROM has one, bind the
  base.

The two are not interchangeable in cost either, and neither direction is
"tighter": on this function the pointer form came out 8 bytes SHORT of the ROM
and the array form 24 bytes long, because the array form also loses the single
pointer giv -- agbcc keeps base, `i * stride` and the `k` giv in three separate
registers instead of one walking pointer, which costs two instructions per
iteration and one extra callee-saved register. Getting both at once is still
open; see `work/sub_08017720/sub_08017720.c`.

## A REDUNDANT `if (x == 0)` TEST THAT SURVIVES IN ONE ARM OF AN `else if` CHAIN IS SOURCE, NOT NOISE (wave 56, W56-A)

`sub_0807CE5C` (2,468 B) opens with a seven-arm `else if` chain whose first four
arms all begin `p->unk40 == 0 &&`. In the ROM that test appears **twice**: once
at the top, and once again in front of the FOURTH arm — and nowhere else. The
temptation is to read the surviving copy as a compiler artefact and hoist the
condition into an enclosing `if`. That loses the match: hoisting deletes the
fourth test entirely and the function comes out two bytes short.

The mechanism, and it reads cleanly off the control flow:

- The **first** test's false branch does not fall into arm 2 — it jumps all the
  way past arm 4, to the fifth arm's test. That is `thread_jumps` chaining
  through arms 2, 3 and 4 because each one opens with the same comparison and
  the outcome is known.
- Arms 2 and 3 lose their copy of the test to **CSE**. After threading, each
  one's test has exactly ONE predecessor (the previous arm's *second*
  conjunct failing), so it sits in the same extended basic block as the test
  that already established `p->unk40 == 0`, and `cse_main` folds it away.
- Arm 4 keeps its copy because arm 3's condition is a three-term `&&`, so arm
  4's test is a **join point with three predecessors**. CSE will not fold
  across a join, and the comparison is emitted.

**The read-out rule: count the predecessors of the surviving test.** One
predecessor ⇒ it would have been folded, so it is not in the source there. Two
or more ⇒ write the conjunct out in that arm. This also explains the register:
the value stays live in `sl` for the whole chain, and gcc then **reuses that
register as the constant 0** at later `str`/`strh` sites inside the arms
(`mov r0, sl; str r0, [r7, #0x58]` is `p->unk58 = 0`), which is the same
cse-recorded `reg == const0` equivalence. If your candidate emits `movs rN, #0`
where the ROM does `mov rN, sl`, the missing thing is the equivalence, i.e. the
enclosing comparison, not an allocation lever.

### The same function, three cheaper read-outs worth keeping

- **A duplicated loop BODY means the step is written twice in the source; a
  duplicated loop TEST does not.** Two loops in this function have the shape
  `STEP; while (cond) { STEP; }`. gcc's rotation emits the exit test twice
  (once before, once at the bottom) but the body once. So: body once + test
  twice = `while` with a hand-written pre-step. Body twice would have been a
  different source. Writing either of these as `do { STEP } while (cond);`
  gives one body and one test and cannot match.
- **`cmp rN, #K; bgt` fixes the source condition as `<= K`, and the arms are not
  interchangeable.** Three sites here (`> 3`, `> 7`, `> 0xb`) were drafted with
  the arms the intuitive way round and every one of them inverted the branch to
  `ble` and swapped the two blocks. The then-arm is always emitted inline first,
  so read the inline block as the THEN and let the conditional branch be the
  inverted one. It costs nothing to check and it was the whole residual on two
  of the three.
- **`ldrsh` on a field you only ever increment still pins it signed.** `unk66`
  was drafted `u16` because its only writes are `p->unk66++` / `--`, which emit
  `ldrh` either way. One *test* of it against zero at the top of the function
  emits `movs r2, #0; ldrsh r1, [r0, r2]` — three halfwords instead of the
  `ldrh r1, [r0]` a `u16` gives — and that single site is the discriminator.
  Sweep the ZERO TESTS of a field, not its updates, when picking its signedness.

### The brief's `-fforce-addr` pool guidance held exactly (wave 56, W56-A)

All six words at `0x081D934C`–`0x081D9360` are `-fforce-addr` copies of globals
the function *also* names directly. Referencing the real globals normally
(`gUnknown_030058E0`, `gUnknown_03005948`, `gUnknown_03005910`,
`gUnknown_03005950`, `gUnknown_03005958`, and `gpKeySt` for `0x03002EE0`)
reproduced all thirteen double loads with no spelling trick, and `trymatch`
printed the `rodata` list itself. Note `0x081D934C` holds `0x03002EE0`, which is
`gpKeySt` from `include/hardware.h` and NOT a declarable `gUnknown_` — the note
at `include/unknown-globals.h:6815` already covers this and it is still right.

## fold() ALWAYS merges literal constants across a +/- chain — a separated constant is a STATEMENT BOUNDARY (wave 56, W56-B)

`sub_0807DA98` (3,816 B) matched, and four of its five defects were one root
cause. The ROM repeatedly computes `A - (B - K)` as `B; B -= K; A - B`, keeping
the literal attached to `B`. **No single C expression can produce that.**

Measured with `compile_probe`, all against agbcc -O2:

| source | emitted |
|---|---|
| `a - (b - 3)` | `a + 3; - b` |
| `a - b + 3` | `a - b; + 3` |
| `(m + 0x25) - x*3`, `m - (x*3 - 0x25)`, `m - x*3 + 0x25` | all identical: `(m + 0x25) - x*3` |

The mechanism is fold's `associate` block: `split_tree` decomposes both operands
into {var, constant} and rebuilds, and it fires whenever **more than two**
objects are found. `{a, b, K}` is three, so it always fires. `{a, b}` is two, so
`a - b` is left alone.

**Consequence: if the ROM shows a literal bound to the INNER operand, the
original source had a statement boundary there.** A local assigned in a
preceding statement is a separate tree and fold never sees the pair.

Two corollaries that each cost an attempt:

- **The local also fixes the LOAD ORDER, and the order tells you how many
  locals.** `b = p->unk4e - 3; ... p->unk52 - b` emits `ldrsh; subs #3; ldrh;
  subs` — the `b` statement drags its load to the front. The ROM had `ldrh`
  first, which needs BOTH operands bound: `a = p->unk52; b = p->unk4e - 3;`.
  Read the load order off the ROM before choosing.
- **Strength reduction absorbs the merged constant into the giv's INIT, which
  looks like an unrelated bug.** `(p->unk38 + 0x43 - j * 0x18)` folds to
  `unk38 - (j*0x18 - 0x43)`, and LSR then emits `movs r5,#0x2b; negs r5,r5`
  where the ROM has `movs r5,#0x18`. **A giv whose init is not a clean multiple
  of its step is the tell for a folded constant upstream — do not go looking at
  the loop.** Binding the constant into a local restored `movs r5,#0x18` and
  `movs r4,#0x48` exactly.

### The same rule decides WHERE a bound local is evaluated

Splitting an argument into a local moves its whole computation to the statement
position. `sub_0801F34C(i, (m - x) & 0x1ff, (y - n) | 0x400, ...)` with both `x`
and `y` bound before the call emits `y`'s `adds r2,#0x43` BEFORE the `ands` of
argument 2; the ROM has it after. The fix is to bind only as far as fold
requires and let the rest stay in the argument list — here, three statements
(`x = p->unk38*3 - 0x25; x = j*0x48 - x; x &= 0x1ff;`) then `y` — so that
argument 2 is fully retired before `y` is touched. **Arguments are evaluated
left to right and a bound local is evaluated at its statement; those two clocks
are what you are lining up.**

### Operand order of two subtrahends is EMITTED IN REVERSE of the source

`((0x43 - p->unk30 - j*0x18) & 0xff)` emits `0x43 - j*0x18` first, then
`- p->unk30`. Writing `(0x43 - j*0x18 - p->unk30)` emits `0x43 - p->unk30`
first, then `- j*0x18`, which is what the ROM has. Probe it rather than
reasoning about it; the swap is systematic for `K - var - giv`.

### A dead load that survives -O2 is a `volatile` member plus a bare statement

`sub_0807DA98` contains `mov r3,sb; ldr r0,[r3,#0x60]` whose result is
overwritten two instructions later. Flow deletes a dead non-volatile MEM read,
so this cannot be an ordinary discarded expression. `volatile int unk60;` in the
parameter struct plus the expression statement `p->unk60;` reproduces it
exactly, and costs nothing at the field's two real uses (each is a single read
feeding a `cmp`, which volatile does not change). Recorded as the spelling that
matches; the original's reason for the read is unknown.

### One function can reach the SAME global both through its -fforce-addr word and by a plain pool word

Confirmed for a third time (after W48-J and W51-I). `sub_0807DA98` reads
`gSinLut` nine times: the FIRST read in each of its three affine blocks goes
through `ldr rN,=gUnknown_081D9364; ldr rN,[rN]`, every later read in the same
block is a plain `ldr rN,=gSinLut`. **Spelling `gSinLut` honestly reproduces
both forms with no intervention** — do not try to author the double load, and do
not read the mixed forms as two different symbols.

**AND: `gUnknown_0808F100` IS `gSinLut`, NOT AN UNDECLARED GLOBAL.**
`[0x081D9364] = 0x0808F100 = &gSinLut`, decoded from `baserom.gba`; the same
value sits at `0x081D946C`, which `include/unknown-globals.h` already documents.
The wave-56 brief told W56-B and W56-D that `gUnknown_0808F100` was a real,
undeclared global to be typed and added to `unknown-globals.h`. **That is wrong
and declaring it would have been a duplicate of `gSinLut`.**

**The cheapest way to resolve one of these is `aw2bhr.map`, not `baserom.gba`.**
W56-B dereferenced the pool word in the ROM and then matched the address against
the headers by hand; W56-D got the same answer in one step from
`aw2bhr.map:6945` (`0x0808f100  gSinLut`), confirmed by
`data/rodata-0808F098.s:44` (`gSinLut: @ 0x0808F100`). Two independent methods,
same result. **Grep the map for the resolved address FIRST -- it names the
symbol outright, where the ROM only gives you a number you still have to
recognise.** Fall back to reading `baserom.gba` only when the address is not in
the map.

The same wave-56 brief made this error twice: it also listed
`[0x0808D7DC] = 0x03002EE0 -> gUnknown_03002EE0 (already declared)`. There is no
`gUnknown_03002EE0` either -- **0x03002EE0 is `gpKeySt`** (`unknown-globals.h`
lines 6815 and 10675; `aw2bhr.lds` binds the address to it, and the wave-54
W54-D pool dump at line 6911 independently records `93F4 -> 0x03002EE0
(&gpKeySt)`). Write `gpKeySt->...`. Two of the brief's decoded pool slots named
non-existent globals, so **treat every `-> gUnknown_XXXXXXXX (already declared)`
line in a brief as a claim to check in the map, not a finding.**

### proto_check.py is NOT a gate against the cross-agent signature hazard (wave 56, W56-B)

Measured, not assumed: `tools/proto_check.py` has exactly one subprocess call,
`git diff include/`. **It never invokes agbcc and compiles nothing.** A draft in
`work/` is in no population it examines, so it never reads your draft.

**AND ITS DEFAULT MODE IS DIFF-DERIVED, WHICH MAKES A GREEN RUN ON A CLEAN TREE
VACUOUS.** `collect_prototypes(scan_all)` has two modes. `--all` globs
`include/*.h` and reads them as files -- 2443 prototypes in wave 56. The
DEFAULT path instead parses `git diff include/` and keeps only ADDED (`+`)
lines matching the prototype regex. So the count is a function of how dirty
`include/` currently is, not of the tree: wave 56 saw it report 279, then 280,
then 281 as agents edited headers, and it drifts with nothing but the diff.

**Once a wave's header edits are committed, `git diff include/` is empty, the
default run checks ZERO prototypes, and it still exits 0.** Do not quote a bare
`proto_check` exit 0 as a prototype gate -- say which mode you ran.

`--all` is the real gate, with one caveat: **its current baseline is exit 1**,
on a mismatch that predates wave 56 --

    MISMATCH sub_0801E338 (parameters)
      header:  int sub_0801E338(int, int, int, int, long long, int)
      c_0801E338.c:  ... long long a5, volatile int a6

`norm_type` does not strip `volatile`, so the sixth parameter compares unequal.
The header line is byte-identical to HEAD and `c_0801E338.c` is unmodified, so
this is not a regression -- but anyone adopting `--all` must know exit 1 is the
existing floor or they will read it as their own wave's breakage.

This came up live. W56-B added `void sub_0807DA98(struct Unk7DA98 *);` to
`include/unknown-functions.h` while W56-A held a conflicting local declaration
of the same function in `work/sub_0807CE5C/`. That TU stopped compiling
(`conflicting types for 'sub_0807DA98'`), and **proto_check stayed green
throughout** -- it reported 279 then 280 prototypes, 0 mismatches, before and
after. W56-A read the green result as "the conflicting TU never compiled, so
nothing was checked". That is backwards: the break is invisible to proto_check
by construction, not skipped.

The wave brief's "python tools/proto_check.py catches this" is true only for the
case it describes -- declaring a function that already has a promoted body, a
prototype-vs-definition disagreement. It does NOT cover a CALLER whose local
declaration conflicts with a newly added header prototype. **The only thing that
catches that is compiling the caller**, i.e. `trymatch` on every draft that
calls the newly declared function.

So when you add a prototype to a shared header mid-wave: message the callers,
and do not read a green proto_check as evidence that their drafts still build.

## `tools/proto_check.py` DEFAULTS TO A DIFF-SCOPED CHECK, SO A GREEN RUN CAN BE VACUOUS (wave 56, W56-A/W56-B)

Two agents in wave 56 read this tool's output as evidence it does not provide.
The wave brief says "`python tools/proto_check.py` catches this" about the
cross-agent signature hazard. That is true for ONE of the two shapes and false
for the other, and the reason is in `collect_prototypes()` at line 82.

**It compiles nothing.** Its only subprocess call is `git diff include/`. It
parses `include/` prototypes against `src/decomp/` definitions. **A draft in
`work/` is in neither population**, so a `work/` caller whose local declaration
conflicts with a newly added header prototype is invisible to it. W56-A hit
exactly that break and proto_check stayed green through it; the only thing that
caught it was compiling the caller, i.e. `trymatch`.

**And the default mode is DIFF-SCOPED.** `scan_all` is set only by `--all`.
Without it the tool keeps only the added (`+`) lines of `git diff include/` that
match the prototype regex — it never reads the headers as files. So:

- The `checked N prototype(s)` count measures **how dirty `include/` is**, not
  the health of the tree. W56-A saw it go 0 → 280 across two runs and wrongly
  inferred that the earlier run had been passing because nothing compiled. It
  had been passing because the dirty region contained no prototype-shaped added
  lines. **Do not read that count as a coverage number.**
- **Once a wave's header edits are COMMITTED, the diff is empty, the default run
  checks ZERO prototypes, and it still exits 0.** A green default run on a clean
  tree is vacuous. Section 6 should use `--all`.

**`--all` currently exits 1 on a pre-existing benign mismatch**, so adopt it
knowing the baseline: `sub_0801E338`, header `int (..., int)` against
`src/decomp/c_0801E338.c`'s `int (..., volatile int)`. `norm_type` does not
strip `volatile`. The header line is byte-identical to HEAD and the definition
file is unmodified, so this predates wave 56 — it is not a wave regression, and
it is why nobody has been running `--all`. Stripping `volatile` in `norm_type`
would make `--all` usable as a gate.

**RULE: the only sweep that catches a caller/header signature conflict is
re-running `trymatch` on every draft that calls the newly declared function.**
Adding a prototype is not done when proto_check is green.

### A 16,000-line diff on a shared header is not necessarily damage (wave 56, W56-A)

`git diff --stat include/` reported 16,392 insertions / 16,209 deletions across
`unknown-functions.h` and `unknown-globals.h` after two agents made a handful of
one-line edits. That is the exact shape of the wave-51 shared-file accident and
it is worth ten seconds to discriminate rather than assume either way. It was
not damage — but **the first version of this section got the check wrong, and
the correction is the useful part** (caught by W56-B).

W56-A ran the check on `unknown-functions.h` only, found all 1,269 missing lines
blank, and wrote it up as though it covered both headers. It did not.
`unknown-globals.h` has **six NON-blank** lines present in HEAD and absent from
the worktree. All six turned out to be legitimate concurrent edits by W56-D, but
"every one is blank" was an overclaim reached by checking one file and reporting
two.

**Use `comm -23` on whitespace-normalised sorted content, not `grep '^<'` on a
raw diff.** A `-` line means removed-or-moved-or-retyped, not lost, and raw
`sort` also mis-counts duplicate blank lines:

```
comm -23 <(git show HEAD:<file> | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' | sort) \
         <(sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' <file> | sort) | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$'
```

**Then resolve every line it prints — do not stop at "non-blank, therefore
damage".** The six here were one global retyped in place
(`extern u8 gUnknown_03002EFC` to `extern volatile u8 ...`, still declared) and
five `filler_NN` members carved into named ones in `struct Unk0200B0B0`.

**For a filler carving the thing to verify is that the SIZE is preserved**,
because narrowing a filler silently shifts every later offset, and that is the
wave-37 accident that regressed two matched functions. These were all clean:
`u8 filler_32[0x02]` became `s8 unk32` + `s8 unk33`; `u8 filler_56[0x04]` became
`s16 unk56` + `u8 filler_58[0x02]`; `u8 filler_08[0x04]` became `s16 unk08` +
`s16 unk0a`. Read the `/* 0xNN */` comments straight down and check each is
contiguous with the previous member's end. A carving that does not add up is the
break, and **neither `trymatch` nor `proto_check` can see it** — `trymatch`
compiles one unit and a shifted offset still compiles.

It is also not a line-ending change — neither version contains CRs. Something
normalises blank lines in these headers on write.

## `proto_check.py --all` IS NOW A USABLE GATE — its baseline exit 1 is fixed (wave 56, orchestrator)

W56-A and W56-B established that `tools/proto_check.py` compiles nothing and
that its DEFAULT mode is diff-scoped, so a green default run on a clean tree is
vacuous. Both findings are correct and verified independently: the tool's only
subprocess is `git diff include/`, the default path keeps only added (`+`)
prototype-shaped lines, and `--all` reads `include/*.h` as files instead
(284 prototypes vs 2,448 in wave 56).

Their conclusion was "use `--all`, but its baseline is exit 1". **That baseline
is now fixed, because a permanently-red acceptance test hides the regression it
exists to catch** — the exact failure wave 21 recorded for
`overlap_screen.py --self-test`.

The single mismatch was `sub_0801E338`, header `int` against definition
`volatile int a6`. **In C a TOP-LEVEL qualifier on a parameter is ignored when
function types are compared** — `f(volatile int)` and `f(int)` are the same type
and both compilers agree — so it was noise, not a conflict.

Fixed in `norm()` (parameters) and `norm_type()` (returns), both guarded the
same way:

    if '*' not in p:
        p = re.sub(r'^(?:volatile|const)\s+', '', p)

**The guard is the load-bearing part.** In `volatile int *` the qualifier is on
the POINTEE and IS significant; stripping it there would hide a real conflict.
Unit-tested both directions, including `volatile int *` / `const char *` which
must NOT collapse.

Note the fix belongs in `norm()`, not `norm_type()` — `norm()` handles parameter
lists and does its own typedef resolution rather than calling `norm_type()`.
Editing only `norm_type()` changes nothing about a parameter mismatch.

`--all` now reports **2,448 prototypes / 0 mismatches / exit 0**. Use it as the
gate and say which mode you ran.

**One latent bug left, deliberately NOT fixed (out of scope, not triggered):**
`TYPEDEFS['unsigned'] = 'unsigned int'`, so `norm('unsigned char')` returns
`'unsigned int char'`. A header spelling `unsigned char x` against a `u8 x`
definition would therefore report a FALSE mismatch. Nothing in the tree spells
it that way today, and it predates wave 56 — verified by re-running the
pre-change tool. Fix it the day it fires.

## A `?:` ON POINTERS FOLDS TO ONE ADDRESS PLUS A CONDITIONAL ADJUST; A `?:` ON VALUES DOES NOT (wave 56, W56-D)

`sub_08005F4C` selects between two adjacent `s8` members with

```
	adds r0, r2, #0
	adds r0, #0x2e
	b _08005FB0
_08005FAC:
	adds r0, r2, #0
	adds r0, #0x2f
_08005FB0:
	movs r1, #0
	ldrsb r1, [r0, r1]
```

-- two address computations, a real branch, and ONE sign-extending load at the
merge. The obvious spelling for that shape is the pointer `?:`:

```c
sub_080078E4(p->unk07, *(p->unk07 == 0 ? &p->unk2e : &p->unk2f));
```

**That spelling is WRONG and it is wrong in an instructive way.** `fold` sees
`COND_EXPR(test, base + 46, base + 47)`, distributes the common addend out, and
emits ONE address plus a conditional correction:

```
	adds r1, r2, #0
	adds r1, #47
	cmp r0, #0
	bne .L
	subs r1, #1
```

The `?:` on the VALUES is what produces the ROM:

```c
sub_080078E4(p->unk07, p->unk07 == 0 ? p->unk2e : p->unk2f);
```

Each arm expands its own `mem:QI` at a constant displacement; `ldrsb` on Thumb
has no immediate form, so each arm legitimizes its address into a register, and
the two identical tails (`movs rI,#0; ldrsb rD,[rB,rI]; adds r0,r3,#0; bl`) are
then merged by cross-jumping. **Both members must have the same type for this**
-- it is what settled `struct Unk0200B0B0::unk2e` as `s8` rather than `u8`.

**READ THE RULE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because the "wrong" half is also a tool.**
`base + K` followed by a conditional `+/- delta` on the SAME register is the
signature of a `?:` (or an if/else) whose two results are constants added to a
common base. `sub_08005F4C` needs exactly that shape for a table subscript:

```
	lsls r3, r0, #3        @ unk07 * 40
	adds r1, r3, #0
	adds r1, #0x1c         @ + 7 * 4
	cmp r0, #0
	bne _080061B4
	adds r1, #8            @ -> + 9 * 4
_080061B4:
	adds r0, r1, r5        @ + &gUnknown_084886F8
	ldr r0, [r0]
```

and gets it from `tbl[unk07][unk07 == 0 ? 9 : 7]`.

## A 2-D ARRAY AND THE EQUIVALENT FLAT `row * N + col` ARE DIFFERENT CODE (wave 56, W56-D)

Same function, measured with `compile_probe`. For `const s32 tbl[][10]`:

- `tbl[row][col]` goes through `get_inner_reference`, which sums `row * 40` and
  `col * 4` as SEPARATE already-scaled terms and adds the symbol register LAST:
  `lsls #2; adds; lsls #3` (= *40), then the column constant, then
  `adds r0, r1, rBASE`. **This is what the ROM does.**
- `tbl_flat[row * 10 + col]` builds ONE index expression and scales it at the
  end: `lsls #2; adds; lsls #1` (= *10), `adds #col`, then `lsls #2`, then the
  base. Two instructions different, and a `?:` in `col` can no longer fold into
  the pre-scaled constant (see the previous section).

So when a ROM row stride shows up folded into the multiply, the original
declared the table 2-D, and the flat declaration cannot reach that code. The
project's older tables were deliberately declared flat (see
`gUnknown_084887AC`'s note) because their two readers scaled them differently;
that is a different situation, not a house style.

## `x -= K; if (x <= C)` ON A GLOBAL: A SECOND `ldrb` IS A `volatile` TELL (wave 56, W56-D)

```
	ldrb r0, [r1]
	subs r0, #8
	strb r0, [r1]
	ldrb r0, [r1]          @ <-- re-load
	cmp r0, #0x77
	bls ...
```

A plain `u8` global cannot produce that. CSE knows the stored value and
zero-extends it in place, `lsls #0x18; lsrs #0x18` -- same instruction count,
different instructions, and `trymatch` reports it as a 2-byte spot. Probed both
spellings side by side; only `volatile u8` re-loads. This retyped
`gUnknown_03002EFC` (all eighteen other users in `src/decomp` are bare stores or
bare reads and were re-verified byte-identical afterwards).

Generalise it: **for a narrow global, "read-modify-write then test the same
global" is a volatile discriminator that costs nothing to check** -- the
non-volatile form NEVER re-loads, so the second `ldrb`/`ldrh` is decisive. This
is a different tell from the aggregate-member one already in this file (a dead
load of the element's own address around a store).

## DEAD-STORE ELIMINATION IS PER-BASIC-BLOCK, AND IT EXPLAINS "ONE LOAD, N OPERATIONS, ONE STORE" (wave 56, W56-D)

```
	ldrb r0, [r1]
	movs r4, #2
	orrs r0, r4
	movs r3, #8
	orrs r0, r3
	movs r2, #0x10
	orrs r0, r2
	strb r0, [r1]
```

Three separate `orr`s with three separate constants, one load, one store. That
is NOT one expression -- `fold` would merge `x | 2 | 8 | 0x10` into a single
`0x1a`. It is THREE separate statements (here three 1-bit bitfield writes to
`gUnknown_030030E0.bits`), and `flow.c`'s `mem_set_list` deleted the first two
`strb`s because a later store to the same address follows **in the same basic
block**. The same mechanism produces `ldrh; ands; ands; strh` from

```c
p->unk00 &= 0xFFDF;
p->unk00 &= 0xFFFC;
```

and `ldr; orrs; ands; str` from `e->unk00 |= 9; e->unk00 &= ~0x30;`.

**The corollary is the useful half: if a branch lands between the two
operations, the elimination cannot fire and you get TWO stores** -- which is
exactly how `sub_08005F4C`'s `e->unk00 &= ~0x40; if (...) e->unk00 |= 8;` reads
out. So one store means one basic block, two stores mean a branch between them;
never spell either one as a single `(x | A) & B` expression.

## READ A NEGATED MASK OFF `movs #N; rsbs` AS `~(N-1)`, NOT `~N` (wave 56, W56-D)

`movs r1, #0x31; rsbs r1, r1, #0; ands r0, r1` is `x &= ~0x30`, not `~0x31`:
the register holds `-0x31 == ~0x30`. Four masks in `sub_08005F4C` were
transcribed one off by this (`~0x30`, `~0x31`, `~0x40`, `~0x70` written as
`~0x31`, `~0x32`, `~0x41`, `~0x71`), which is invisible in the byte score and
obvious in the instruction diff. The rule: **the immediate before `rsbs` is the
complement PLUS ONE.**

## OPEN: agbcc KEPT A PROVABLY DEAD CONDITIONAL ASSIGNMENT AND NOTHING REPRODUCES IT (wave 56, W56-D)

`sub_08005F4C` @ `_08006326` contains

```
	movs r0, #7
	ldrsb r0, [r1, r0]
	cmp r0, #0
	bne _08006344
	movs r2, #0x3a
	ldrsh r0, [r1, r2]
	adds r5, r0, #4
	b _0800634A
	@ pool: gDesignRing, gUnknown_0200B224
_08006344:
	movs r2, #0x3a
	ldrsh r0, [r1, r2]
	adds r5, r0, #3
_0800634A:
	...
```

i.e. `i = p->unk07 == 0 ? p->unk3a + 4 : p->unk3a + 3;` -- **and r5 is never
read again on any path.** Every reachable successor writes r5 before reading it
(verified instruction by instruction from `_0800634A` to the epilogue; the
epilogue only `pop`s it). It is 24 bytes of genuinely dead code that the
original compile kept.

Writing the same statement makes agbcc DELETE it, and the deletion has a
distinctive fingerprint worth recognising: `flow` removes the two `adds` and
then the two `ldrsh` that feed them, both arms become empty, `jump` then removes
the now-pointless conditional branch, and **the condition's own load survives as
three dead instructions** (`ldrb rN,[rB,#7]; lsls #0x18; asrs #0x18`) because no
dead-code pass runs after that jump pass. Confirmed with `compile_probe` on
three reductions, including one where the variable is redefined inside a
jump-table `switch` and one where it is redefined inside a loop -- agbcc deletes
it every time.

Wave 72 found a spelling that does retain the value for zero net instructions:

```c
if (i)
    q = expression;
else
    q = expression;
use(q);
```

In a controlled reduction, `flow` retains the complete conditional producer of
`i`; the later jump pass merges the identical definitions of `q` and removes the
test of `i`, with no dead-code pass rerun afterward.  Final assembly contains
one copy of `expression` and no emitted consumer of `i`.  Applied to
`sub_08005F4C` with `expression = gpKeySt->unk02 | gpKeySt->held`, it restored
the ROM's entire 24-byte block at `_08006326` without the artificial `strh` and
raised the configured draft from 13.7% / +8 bytes to 25.1% / +28 bytes.

This does not yet match the function: the use ends too early, so the candidate
still has a 16-byte frame rather than 20, assigns the retained value to r6
rather than r5, and keeps the downstream 0x28..0x2E allocation residual.  Moving
the same mechanism into case 0x28 by selecting identical recomputations kept the
producer but made the candidate materially larger; it did not recover the
frame.  The remaining question is therefore the original lifetime placement,
not whether agbcc can retain a provably dead producer without emitted use code.

Previously ruled out: storing it
to any `gUnknown_0200B0B0` member (emits a `strh`/`strb` the ROM does not have;
`flow.c`'s dead-store elimination is per-block and the killing store would have
to be in the SAME block, which it is not); reading it later in `case 0x41` or
`case 0x28` instead of recomputing (both of those visibly recompute
`unk3a + 4` / `+ 3` themselves); and reusing any of the function's other locals
as the destination (all of them are defined before use everywhere).

Forcing it live artificially (`p->unk3c = i;`) DOES emit the block
byte-for-byte and costs exactly the one extra `strh`, so the block itself is
understood -- only its liveness is not. Whoever picks this up: the question is
narrow and general, "what use of a local costs zero instructions under agbcc",
and answering it is worth more than this one function.

## THE SWITCH SOURCE-ORDER RULE (wave 45) HELD ON A 22-CASE JUMP TABLE (wave 56, W56-D)

`sub_08005F4C` has six switches on the same `u16`, two of them jump tables
(22 entries, `case 0x46..0x5B`; 9 entries, `case 0x28..0x30`). Reading the case
BODIES in address order gave the source order directly, first time, for all six
-- including the three fall-throughs (`case 0x32` into `case 0x33`, `case 0x3c`
into `case 0x41`, `case 0x2D` into `case 0x2E`), which read out as "the earlier
body has no `b` to the tail". Two cases with IDENTICAL bodies (`0x50` and
`0x5A`) show up as one body plus a `b` into the other's tail; that is
cross-jumping, not a shared source label, and writing the body out twice
reproduces it. **A jump table costs nothing extra to order: gcc fills the gaps
in the case range with the default label, so a 22-entry table for five live
cases is normal output and not a sign of missing cases.**

## sub_08005F4C, 2026-09-24: `-fforce-addr` `.rodata` WORDS ARE gcse PRE INSERTIONS, AND THREE MORE LEVERS

Measured on the 5084-byte design-room state machine, which went from a
3560-byte (-1524) draft to size-exact / +4 at 77-80% in one session.

**Every `-fforce-addr` `.rodata` word in a function is a gcse PRE artifact.**
Compiling the draft with `-fno-gcse` removes ALL of its `.rodata` words,
including the ones the ROM has. With `-da`, `gccdump.gcse` shows why: under
`-fforce-addr` each global address is expanded as
`(set t (symbol_ref .LCn)); (set r (mem t))`, and PRE treats `(symbol_ref .LCn)`
as an ordinary expression that nothing kills. Most PRE copies land in the same
extended block as their use, and CSE2 folds `(mem t)` back into a direct
`ldr r, =sym`. A word survives only where a PRE insertion or a redundant use is
separated from its fold by a join, so the pseudo that holds `&.LCn` lives
across it. `PRE/HOIST: end of bb N ... copying expression K to reg R` in the
gcse dump names the insertion, and `PRE: redundant insn` names the victims.
So an extra or missing word is a question about **which references PRE
considers the same expression**, not about spelling that one access.

- **Two names for one object split the PRE expression.** State 0x2C passes
  `gDesignRing[slot].itemId` to `sub_080077EC` and then runs ring loops over
  `gDesignRing`. With one name, PRE hoisted `&.LC(gDesignRing)` above the
  `frame < 0` test: a stray `.rodata` word, a spilled pointer and a 24-byte
  frame. Spelling that ONE argument through the linker's other name for the
  same address (`gUnknown_0200B0D0`; aw2bhr.lds has
  `gDesignRing = gUnknown_0200B0D0`) removes the word and restores the ROM's
  20-byte frame. Bisecting with `-da` needed all three of: the argument, the
  frame==0 set loops and the mark loops. Removing any one also removed the
  hoist.
- **A reset base kept apart from the walking pointer.**
  `e = &gDesignRing[slot]; ring = gDesignRing;` with `e = ring` as the
  wrap-around reset gives the ROM's `ldr r2,=sym; mov r8,r2` (the base in a
  high callee-saved register). Writing `e = &ring[slot]` (ring used for the
  add) gives `ring` a LO_REGS preference, so global alloc takes caller-save r3
  first and spills it around every call.

**A volatile table read is how the ROM re-loads a `?:` test operand.** See
the note on `gUnknown_084886F8` in include/unknown-globals.h. The ROM loads
`tbl[m][0]` and then reloads `m` for `m == 0 ? x - 0x18 : x - 0x21`. Every
non-volatile spelling either reuses `m` or duplicates the table load into
both arms. agbcc's fold distributes `a - (c ? k1 : k2)` without a SAVE_EXPR
unless `a` has side effects.

**Merge a block-local into the function-wide variable when the ROM's register
says so.** A block-local delta (`int d;`) in states 4 and 0x36 left the draft
at 38%. Using the function-wide `n` that the ROM keeps in r7 elsewhere moved
it to 75.7% in one step, because global allocation is driven by the whole
function's pseudo census.

**RESOLVED (2026-09-25): the function now matches** (`trymatch` exit 0; needs
`"rodata": ["0x0808D7D8", "0x0808D7DC", "0x0808D7E0", "0x0808D7E4"]` at
promotion). The last three residuals, and the mechanism behind each:

- **Ring loops index `gDesignRing[slot]` directly; there is no walking
  pointer.** `slot++; if (slot > visible) slot = 0;` is a biv update to
  loop.c: the set-to-constant is recorded with `mult_val == 0`. So
  `&gDesignRing[slot]` is strength-reduced into the ROM's walking pointer,
  and the reset becomes `mov r4, r8` from a hoisted base. The giv init is
  emitted after the reversed counter's init, which is the only way to get the
  ROM's `movs r6,#9` *before* the pointer init in the call-free loops. Every
  hand-written `e++` / `e = ring` spelling, in any statement order, emits the
  pointer init first, plus an extra `mov r2,r8` in the call-bearing loops (the
  whole +4). Read `ldrh r3,[r2,#4]` against `(itemId & 0x3F) == 1 || == 2`
  the same way: re-read the member, do not cache it in a local.
- **The e/slot/i rotation was the gSinLut preference, and the loop form above
  removes it.** Pass 0 of `find_reg` skips any register preferred by a
  *lower-priority conflicting* allocno. The gSinLut PRE reaching register
  prefers r4 (from `set_preference` on `(set V (mem R))` with V local-allocated
  to r4) and conflicted with the function-wide `e` only through the 0x2C mark
  loops. Once those loops stopped using `e`, `e`/`slot`/`i`/`frame` landed in
  r4/r5/r6/r7. Merging the case-4/0x36 delta and the 0x51/0x5B scale into
  `frame` (all r7 in the ROM) was the other half.
- **`ldrh r0; adds r1,r0,#0; cmp r1,#0x19; beq; movs r1,#63; ands r1,r0; ...
  orrs r1,r0; strh r1`** needed three locals: `int v = itemId; x = (u16)v;`
  (the conversion stops CSE merging x into v, so the copy and the compare on
  it survive), then-arm stores `x`, else `y = v & 0x3F; y |= army;` then
