`gUnknown_03002EE0` and none can be created -- `aw2bhr.lds` already binds that
address, wave 20 invented the name and the SPLIT build caught it as an undefined
reference (the note lives under `gUnknown_03005920` in unknown-globals.h). The
reason it keeps being missed is worth repeating: **there is no direct
`ldr rN,=gpKeySt` anywhere in `asm/`.** Every reader spells it
`ldr rN,=<pool>; ldr rM,[rN]; ldr rM,[rM]`, so the address only ever appears as
pool-word CONTENT and a name-based grep of the disassembly finds nothing.

**So before declaring anything for a decoded pool word, grep `include/` for the
raw ADDRESS as well as for `gUnknown_<addr>`.** Three words of the
0x0816E180-0x0816E1CC run and one of 0x081D93xx hold 0x03002EE0.

## CgbSound: three source-shape readings worth ~50 bytes (wave 56, W56-N)

From `sub_08070FAC` (1100 B, MP2K `CgbSound`; matched in wave 66 with its
historical old_agbcc profile). Each of these was measured by flipping only
that spelling:

- **The envelope-phase dispatch is an if/else-if CHAIN, not a `switch`.** With
  `switch (channels->sf & 3)` over cases 0/1/2/default agbcc balances the tree
  and compares 1, 1, 0, 2. The ROM compares 0, then 1, then 2 in source order.
  Worth ~40 bytes of diff and no size change. **Read the dispatch order out of
  the assembly before choosing between the two spellings** -- a linear 0,1,2,…
  chain is an if/else-if chain and a middle-first order is a `switch`.
- **`p->m = cond ? A : 0;` goes BRANCHLESS and a `if/else` does not.** For
  `channels->n4 = channels->le ? 0x40 : 0;` agbcc emits
  `negs r0,r1; orrs r0,r1; asrs r0,#31; movs r1,#0x40; ands r0,r1` -- six bytes
  and no branch. The if/else form emits `cmp #0; beq; movs r0,#0x40` and reuses
  the register already known to hold 0 in the else arm, which is what the ROM
  has. This does NOT contradict the wave-37 finding that `?:` on a store is real
  code the original wrote; it says the two spellings are DISTINGUISHABLE, so the
  branch tells you which one it was.
- **A `goto`'s target block lands where the LABEL sits in the source.** Moving
  the shared `CgbOscOff(ch); channels->sf = 0;` tail from after the switch to
  inside the branch that first reaches it moved the block to the ROM's address
  and took the function from 46.7% to 69.0% in one edit, because every later
  block then lined up. On a function with six shared entry points, block
  PLACEMENT is worth more than any individual statement.

## CORRECTION: CgbSound IS an old_agbcc positive; fix the source before comparing profiles (wave 66, W66-H)

Wave 56 called `sub_08070FAC` a counter-example because its then-current draft
scored 65.9% under old_agbcc against 69.5% under default. That conclusion was
contextual and wrong: the draft was eight bytes short and still had four wrong
MP2K source spellings. Once those were restored -- the byte-pointer read of
`fr`'s high byte, the masked/narrow NRx4 store, `envelopeGoal * echoVolume`
operand order, and separate signed `ev`/`goal` locals in the decay arm -- the
same source measured:

    sub_08070FAC default       1096/1100, 70.0%
    sub_08070FAC old_agbcc     1100/1100, bytes and relocations exact

The function now carries the evidence-backed `old_agbcc` override. The earlier
text also said its calls did not qualify because the surrounding loop body was
"otherwise pure stores". That was not the wave-38 discriminator: CgbSound's
main four-channel loop contains calls to both `sub_08070F44` and
`sub_08070EF4`, so it is a direct positive for **CALL INSIDE A LOOP BODY**.

**Do not compare compiler profiles while a known structural/size residual is
still present and treat the higher score as a compiler verdict.** Allocation
effects are contextual; fixing source changed old_agbcc from apparently worse
to exact. Temporary profile probes remain cheap and decisive only when they
compile the same semantically settled source.

### THE m4a-REGION `old_agbcc` HEURISTIC: THREE PROBES THIS WAVE, ZERO POSITIVE (wave 56, orchestrator)

`data/compiler-overrides.json` advises: "If you are matching in this region
[0x0806F710-0x080745C0] and land at 90-99% with the size exact, try old_agbcc
BEFORE touching the C -- but do not assume you need it." **The caveat is the
operative half.** Three probes this wave, all run by the orchestrator with a
throwaway override entry restored afterwards via `git checkout --`:

| function | in m4a span | default | under old_agbcc | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_080706B0` (280 B) | **yes** | size-exact, 93.6%, +0x4 | **identical** — 93.6%, +0x4 | no effect |
| `sub_0807E980` (1040 B) | no | size-exact, 99.0%, +0x370 | **worse** — 98.7%, +0x78 | negative |
| `sub_08005F4C` (5084 B) | no | +8, 13.7% | +4, 16.5%, **not** matching | allocation only |

`sub_080706B0` is the one that met the documented trigger exactly — inside the
span, size exact, 93.6% — and old_agbcc produced **byte-identical output**, not
merely a non-match. So the heuristic did not merely fail to close it; the axis
is inert for that function.

**What the wave-38 measurement actually said, and it is narrower than the
region:** the two m4a functions that needed the override were exactly the two
whose **loop body contains a CALL**, which is where the two allocators diverge
over r0 being both the argument register and the only free scratch.
`sub_080706B0` has **zero backward branches and one call** — no loop at all, so
the mechanism cannot apply. **Screen on the mechanism (call inside a loop body),
not on the address range.** The address range was always a proxy for it.

Cost of learning this: three probes, ~5 minutes, no agent slots. **Keep running
them** — they are cheap, they are decisive, and the fourth one may be positive.
But stop treating "it is in the m4a span" as evidence on its own.

## Two zero-initialised locals are ONE cse quantity — the slot you load is decided by LIVE RANGE, not by which variable you name (wave 56, W56-R)

`sub_08081D30` matched at 1956/1956 bytes with **one byte wrong** for three
attempts, and the byte was a stack-slot displacement:

```
    original    mov r3, sp ; ldrh r3, [r3, #4] ; strh r3, [r2]
    candidate   mov r3, sp ; ldrh r3, [r3, #0] ; strh r3, [r2]
```

The source is two `int` locals both set to 0 at entry — a saved timer and a
flag — both spilled to the frame at sp+0 and sp+4, and the statement is
`p->unk4e = <one of them>`.

**Naming the other variable does not change the output.** `= a` and `= b`
compile to byte-identical code. A full sweep of all eight
declaration-order x initialisation-order x operand permutations moved the two
stack slots around (1, 3, 4 and 6 bytes differing) but **never moved this
load off slot 0**. So did rewriting either local as a one-element array, and
`volatile` on either one blew the frame apart (-32 and -40 bytes) by dropping
a pseudo and letting the two spilled address constants keep registers.

**Why:** two pseudos that are both equal to `(const_int 0)` are merged by cse
into one quantity, and `canon_reg` rewrites the operand to that quantity's
canonical register *before* reload assigns a slot. The source-level choice of
variable is erased. Which register is canonical is decided in
`make_regs_eqv`, and it is **the register with the later `REGNO_LAST_UID` —
the one that lives longest** — not the first declared, not the first assigned,
not the one you wrote.

In the tail

```c
    if (b != 0)
        p->unk4c = 0x22 - a;
```

the flag's last mention is the compare and the value's is the subtract two
insns later, so the value wins the quantity and every spelling loads the
value's slot.

**The lever is to extend the flag's live range past the value's**, and the
cheapest way is a store that is dead:

```c
    if (b != 0)
    {
        p->unk4c = 0x22 - a;
        b = 0;           /* consumed */
    }
```

`reg_scan` runs **before** cse, so cse sees that store and flips the canonical
register; `flow` then deletes it as dead and it costs zero bytes. Byte-exact,
and it was the only change from the 99.9% draft. A trailing `b = 0;` as the
function's last statement matches identically, so the placement is a
readability choice and carries no evidence.

**Read it backwards as a diagnostic.** If your candidate is size-exact and the
only difference is the *displacement* of an `ldr`/`ldrh`/`str` on the frame —
one byte, in an instruction that is otherwise right — stop looking for a
different expression. You have the right statement and the wrong canonical
register, and the fix is a liveness change in a *later* statement, not a
rewrite of the one the diff points at. This is the stack-slot analogue of the
already-recorded rule that of two address constants used equally, the pseudo
created FIRST wins the callee-saved register: same allocator, different
tie-break, and here the tie-break is live range rather than allocno number.

Corollary worth stating on its own: **`compile_probe` cannot see this class of
error and neither can reading the C.** Two spellings that a probe reports as
identical are identical *because cse erased the difference*, which is exactly
the wave-15 blind-spot rule — but here the erased thing is a variable
identity, not a width.

## THE CLEAN SMALL BAND IS 14 BIOS SVC WRAPPERS, NOT WORK (wave 56, orchestrator)

With the ≥256 B seam exhausted, the clean (`asm`, no `work/` dir) band below 256
bytes reads as **103 functions / 1,184 bytes**, which looks like a fresh seam and
is not. It splits three ways:

| group | count | bytes | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| contains `svc` | **14** | 88 | BIOS wrappers — **agbcc cannot emit `svc`** |
| no `svc`, ≥48 B | 7 | 768 | genuine matchable work (given to W56-S) |
| no `svc`, <48 B | 82 | 328 | stubs/thunks, unexamined |

The 14 are decisively hand-written and belong in `data/asm-resident.json`:

```
sub_080707C8 svc #0x2a   BgAffineSet  svc #0xe    CpuFastSet svc #0xc
CpuSet       svc #0xb    Div          svc #6      DivRem     svc #6
HuffUnComp   svc #0x13   LZ77UnCompVram svc #0x12 LZ77UnCompWram svc #0x11
MultiBoot    svc #0x25   RLUnCompVram svc #0x15   RLUnCompWram svc #0x14
SoftReset    svc #1      VBlankIntrWait svc #5
```

`SoftReset` is doubly decisive — it also writes the stack pointer directly
(`mov sp, r1`) before the `svc`. **An `svc` instruction is the strongest
asm-resident evidence available**, on a par with the recorded "reads the PC as a
value" case for `sub_08063614`: there is no C spelling, in any configuration.

**DELIBERATELY NOT ENTERED IN WAVE 56.** Moving 14 functions from `asm` to
`asm-resident` changes the index metric's denominator, and the commit title
quotes that metric — doing it inside a wave would make this wave's progress
figure non-comparable with the previous one for reasons that have nothing to do
with matching. **Enter them as a standalone commit between waves**, then re-run
`index_functions.py` and note the denominator change explicitly.

### AND `data/asm-resident.json` HAS TWO DUPLICATE KEYS — do not `json.dump` it

`sub_0807004C` and `sub_080702C0` each appear **twice**, with DIFFERENT reason
text, both from wave 47 (once from W47-A, once from the orchestrator). Python's
`json.load` keeps the LAST value, so:

- the earlier write-up of each is **invisible to every tool** that reads the file;
- **any round-trip through `json.dump` deletes it permanently and silently** —
  the file is 194 lines and dumps back as 192.

This is the evidence base every later hand-written-assembly judgement is made
from, so losing half of two entries matters. Found by round-trip-checking the
file before editing it, which is the same discipline the `parked.json` note
already demands and the reason nothing was lost here.

**Fix it deliberately** — merge each pair by hand, keeping both write-ups —
rather than as a side effect of some other edit. Until then, **edit that file by
TEXT insertion, never by re-dumping it.**

## Switch and if/else LAYOUT is the whole cost of a decision-tree function (wave 56, W56-P)

`sub_0800B61C` (1152 B, a 19-arm dispatch on a table lookup) matched, and every
one of the four attempts it took was spent on LAYOUT, not on semantics. The
statements were right from the first draft. Four rules came out of it, and they
should transfer to every `switch`-shaped function left in the corpus.

**1. Case BODIES are laid out in SOURCE order; the dispatch tree compares in
VALUE order.** So the body order has to be read off the ROM's block addresses
and copied into the source; it is not the case-label order and it is not
ascending. `sub_0800B61C`'s is 0x400, 0x200, 0x800, 0x4a00, 0x4c00, 0x5200,
0x5400, 0x2c00, 0x3400, 0x2a00, 0x3200, 0x4800, 0x5000, 0x2400, 0x2200, 0xc00,
0xa00, 0x1400, 0x1200. Writing the cases in ascending value order instead scored
27.0% at −44 bytes; fixing only the order took it to 35.2% with no other change.
(This confirms W56-D's 22-case reading from the same wave on a much sparser
table.)

**2. A `switch` BALANCES its decision tree from THREE cases up, so a LINEAR run
of `cmp`s in ascending value order is an if/else-if chain, not a small switch.**
`balance_case_nodes` splits whenever the node count exceeds 2, so a 3-case
switch on {2, 8, 0xa} opens with `cmp #8`. The ROM opened with `cmp #2` and then
tested 8 and 0xa in sequence — an if/else-if chain. This is a clean, cheap
discriminator and it runs the other way too: **a linear ladder in the ROM means
you must NOT write a switch, however switch-shaped the code reads.**

Beware the trap that cost an attempt here: the chain's BODIES were laid out
2, 0xa, 8 — out of source order — which looks exactly like switch behaviour and
is not. It is cross-jumping, and it only resolves once the function is the right
overall length. Do not chase apparent body reordering inside an if/else chain
until the size is closed.

**3. `if (guard && call()) r = THEN; else r = ELSE;` and
`u = call(); r = ELSE; if (u) r = THEN;` are DIFFERENT CODE, and the tell is
which constant sits between the call and the compare.** The first puts THEN
there, and because the `movs` is then adjacent to the block's terminating jump,
`thread_jumps` can fold the function's common `if (r > 0)` epilogue test away on
that path. The second puts ELSE there, the `movs` is no longer adjacent to the
jump, threading fails, and the path keeps the runtime test. So:

- `movs rD, K` immediately before `cmp r0, #0` ⇒ the source bound the call
  result to a temp and assigned the ELSE value as its own statement.
- an arm that reaches the epilogue's `cmp` rather than jumping past it ⇒ same
  thing, read from the other end.

Eleven arms of `sub_0800B61C` needed the temp form. Also note the corollary that
settles the variable's storage: the ROM re-materialises the ELSE constant in the
guard's own `else` block instead of pre-setting it, which is what proves the
result variable is never live across a call and is therefore in a CALLER-saved
register. A `r = ELSE;` before the guard would force a callee-saved one.

**4. A TEMP SHARED BETWEEN UNRELATED SWITCH ARMS IS A REGISTER-ALLOCATION
COUPLING, and nothing in the diff points at the declaration.** Using one `int t`
for both the eleven `u = sub_0800B4F0(...)` arms and the four
`t = sub_0800B5C0(...) & mask` arms gives the pseudo one allocation for the
whole function: it lands in r1 (which the masked arms need) and costs an
`adds r1, r0, #0` in each of the other eleven — +28 bytes, 40.1%. Splitting it
into two locals let the two-way temp coalesce onto r0 and took the same body
straight to 82.1%, then to MATCHED. **If a diff shows a uniform one-instruction
copy after a call in many otherwise-correct arms, suspect a shared local before
suspecting the allocator.**

### Two smaller readings from the same batch

**A `movs #k; lsls #1` pair building a return constant is a LITERAL, not a
shift.** `sub_0800FD44` builds 0x142, 0x160, 0x140 and 0x122 that way. Reading
them as `x << 1` invents an expression that is not in the source.

**`gUnknown_0808D85C` is a `-fforce-addr` word holding 0x08499590 — the MAP
POINTER, which is itself `extern u8 *`.** So `MAP->width` through it is THREE
loads (pool word -> &gUnknown_08499590 -> the u8 * -> `ldrh`), and the promotion
carries `"rodata": ["0x0808D85C"]`. The very next function over,
`sub_0800FD44`, reaches the same global with the ordinary two-load spelling and
needs no pool word at all — **so the number of indirections is a property of the
CALL SITE's pool, not of the global, and neither spelling is a defect.**

## Locals: `<<16` in a stack slot with `asrs` at every use (wave 56, W56-Q)

`sub_0802AA78` (2,356 B, 30 data refs) came down from 22.8% to 87.9% almost
entirely on local TYPE choices, and the five facts below are the whole of it.
None of them is visible in a `compile_probe` of an isolated statement — they
only appear once the function has enough live values to spill.

**The shape to recognise.** A stack slot holding `value << 16`, read back with
`asrs #16` at every use and never read raw, is a value whose SIGN-EXTENSION is
the live quantity. A slot holding the raw value with `lsls #16` applied at each
use is the opposite. Both appear in this one function and they are different
declarations:

- **`s16 local`** — agbcc PROMOTE_MODEs it to a sign-extended SImode pseudo, so
  every `int` use is FREE (no shifts) and the raw value is the pseudo itself.
- **`u16 local` + `(s16)x` at the uses** — the `x << 16` is CSEd into one slot
  and each use pays `asrs #16`. THIS is the `<<16`-slot shape.
- **`int local` + `(u16)x` at the uses** — same slot, `lsrs #16` (or `lsrs #15`
  when the use is `* 2`) instead of `asrs`.

**AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT THE SHIFT, IT IS WHETHER THE RAW VALUE EVER
APPEARS.** `sub_0802AA78`'s `cx` was written `u16 cx` + `(s16)cx` and cost
~20 wrong instructions: under a `u16`-truncating context (a `u16` parameter,
or `& 0x1ff`) `force_to_mode` STRIPS the sign extension and substitutes the raw
`cx` pseudo — so agbcc spills raw `cx`, keeps it live across the whole
function, and reaches it with `ldr rN,[sp,#k]` where the ROM has one `add
r0, r9`. Declaring `s16 cx` and deleting every `(s16)` cast fixed all of them
at once and was worth 12 bytes and ~60 differing bytes. **If the ROM holds a
value in a hi/callee-saved register across statements where your candidate
reloads a raw copy from the frame, the local is `s16`, not `u16` with casts.**

**THE MIRROR CASE, and it is the one that is counter-intuitive: `cy` had to be
`int`, not `u16`.** Same function, same slot shape. `cy` is used raw in a
dozen `gUnknown_0849A284[N] + cy` sums. With `u16 cy` every one of those came
out as `adds rD, rCY, rA284` and the ROM has `adds rD, rA284, rCY` — the
operand order of a commutative `adds` is decided by *tree complexity*, and
`(int)cy` on a `u16` is a CONVERT_EXPR that outranks the `gUnknown_0849A284[N]`
ARRAY_REF, so fold puts it first. **Writing the source in the other order does
NOT change it — that was probed both ways at two sites and the output was
byte-identical.** Making `cy` an `int` (with the one `(u16)` truncation the ROM
shows written explicitly, `cy = (u16)(cy - n)`) removes the conversion, the
ARRAY_REF wins, and all twelve sites flip at once.

**Two locals in the ROM are BINDING LOCALS whose only job is to force a
narrowing that agbcc would otherwise prove away.** The ROM materialises
`lsls #16; asrs #16` on a value it then only tests against 0 and passes to an
`int` parameter. Writing `(s16)v` at those two uses emits NOTHING, because
agbcc proves the value fits (it is a merge of 0 and two `ldrb`s). Writing

```c
int acc; s16 accv;   /* ... */   accv = acc; if (accv != 0) { ... accv ... }
```

emits the pair, because the conversion is now an assignment to a declared
`s16` object rather than a cast inside a context that can absorb it. That one
change took the function from 85.4% to 87.4%. **`(s16)x` at a use and `s16 t =
x;` are NOT interchangeable in agbcc even though C says they are.**

**Frame slot order = DECLARATION order.** The four spilled named locals landed
at sp+16/20/24/28 in exactly the order they were declared. The ROM's order was
`cy, v, acc, army`; reordering the declaration list to match moved every
`ldr rN,[sp,#k]` immediate in the function into place in one edit (~40 bytes).
**This is a free, mechanical lever and it should be tried before anything
clever: read the ROM's slot numbers, sort your declarations to match.**

### Two smaller findings from the same function

**A `(s16)` cast on a VOLATILE global is folded away where the same cast on a
non-volatile one is not.** `(s16)gUnknown_03002F90 == 1` compiles to
`ldrh; cmp #1` — `simplify_comparison` drops a sign extension that cannot
affect an equality against a small positive constant. `*(s16 *)&gUnknown_03002F90 == 1`
compiles to `movs r1,#0; ldrsh r0,[r0,r1]; cmp #1`, the ROM's shape, because the
MEM itself is HImode-signed and there is no extension to drop. Adding
`volatile` back to the cast (`*(volatile s16 *)&...`) folds it away AGAIN. So:
**to reproduce an `ldrsh` of a `u16` global under an equality test, cast the
POINTER and drop the `volatile`.** (Probed all four spellings; only the
non-volatile pointer cast works.)

**Reading one `int` struct member at two different widths needs two POINTER
casts, not two value casts.** The ROM reads `gUnknown_03003130.unk0c` (an `int`
member) as `ldrh [r4,#12]` and then again as `ldrsh [r4,r3]`. Writing
`(u16)g.unk0c` and `(s16)g.unk0c` produces ONE `ldr` plus a shared `lsls #16`,
because CSE unifies the SImode load and then the two extensions share their
first shift. Writing `*(u16 *)&g.unk0c` and `*(s16 *)&g.unk0c` produces the two
narrow loads: `zero_extend(mem:HI)` and `sign_extend(mem:HI)` are different
expressions, so CSE leaves them alone.

### The three-per-row ROM table: struct member, NOT a 2-D cast

`gUnknown_0849A2A6` is three `s16` per row indexed `[sel][0..2]`, and the
obvious spelling `((const s16 (*)[3])gUnknown_0849A2A6)[sel][1]` is WRONG here:
agbcc folds the row offset into the RELOCATION (`.word gUnknown_0849A2A6+2`)
and then needs a `-fforce-addr` word for it, where the ROM loads the plain
symbol and does `adds rB, #2`. Reaching the array through a struct MEMBER at
+2/+4 (c_0802AA14.c's `struct Tbl49A2A6` trick, extended with a second member)
is what reproduces the ROM, and it also leaves `sel * 6` as one shared
subexpression the ROM CSEs into a stack slot. **The 2-D cast is still right for
a table you own the declaration of** — `gUnknown_0849A2B2[sel][v]` had to be
declared `const u16 [][3]` to make agbcc distribute the scale into
`v * 2 + sel * 6` and share the `v * 2` with `gUnknown_0849A2A0[v]`; the flat
`gUnknown_0849A2B2[v + sel * 3]` computes `(v + sel * 3) * 2` and shares
nothing.

### `permute.py` still strands header-expanded output in `work/<fn>/<fn>.c`

The wave-17 hazard is NOT fixed. `python tools/permute.py sub_0802AA78` printed
`no candidate matched at the byte level; work\sub_0802AA78\sub_0802AA78.c
restored unchanged` — and then `sub_0802AA78.c` was 7,295 lines of
`typedef signed char int8_t;` etc., i.e. the raw permuter source with every
header expanded. `best.c` is left in the same state whenever the permuter beats
the hand draft. **Diff the first line of `work/<fn>/<fn>.c` against `#include`
after every permuter run**; a promoted file built from that output would carry
the whole header set into `src/decomp/`.

## Wave 56 (W56-S): 0/1 flags, pool-load hoisting, and the ARM block at 0x08000234

### THUMB `MUL` IS PRINTED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS AND THEY ARE THE SAME INSTRUCTION

Read this before diffing any function containing a multiply. `asm/` prints
THUMB MUL as `muls rD, rS, rD`; agbcc's own output prints the SAME ENCODING as
`mul rD, rD, rS`. There is only one THUMB multiply (`MUL Rd, Rm`, `Rd = Rd*Rm`)
and both listings are rendering it. A wave-56 attempt was spent "fixing" an
operand-order difference that does not exist. If you think you have found a
commuted multiply between the two listings, you have not.

### A 0/1 FLAG: agbcc PRESETS THE **ELSE** ARM AND BRANCHES ON `!cond`

Measured over four consecutive attempts on `Decompress`, which is 100 bytes and
whose size matched throughout while the score sat at 76%. The ROM emits

```
movs r2, #1 / cmp r1, r0 / bhi L / movs r2, #0 / L:
```

Both the POSITION of the preset and its POLARITY have to be earned, and the
obvious spellings get exactly one of the two:

| source form | preset | branch | position of preset |
|---|---|---|---|
| `f = (a > K);` as an rvalue | 0 | `bls` | correct (after operands) |
| `f = (a <= K) ? 0 : 1;` | 0 | `bls` | correct -- folds to the row above |
| `f = 1; if (a <= K) f = 0;` | 1 | `bhi` | WRONG -- hoisted to the top of the function |
| `if (a > K) f = 1; else f = 0;` | 0 | `bls` | correct |
| `if (a <= K) f = 0; else f = 1;` | **1** | **`bhi`** | **correct** |

**The rule: an if/else assigning two constants presets the ELSE arm's value and
branches on `!cond` to skip the THEN arm's store.** So to obtain a given
`preset P / b<cc> / store Q` you must write the else arm as P, the then arm as
Q, and choose the comparison whose NEGATION is the `<cc>` in the ROM. Writing
the test in its "natural" polarity produces the exact mirror image.

A plain assignment before the `if` gets the polarity right for the wrong reason
and puts the store at the top of the function, because it is a statement in its
own right rather than part of the comparison's expansion. Only the if/else
defers it until the condition's operands are materialised.

### A SUBSCRIPT WRITTEN INLINE HOISTS THE ARRAY BASE'S POOL `ldr`

`Decompress`'s last defect, and worth 12 bytes on a size-exact candidate. With
the index written inline --

```c
func = gTable[flag + ((src[0] & 0xF0) >> 3)];
```

-- agbcc emits the base's pool `ldr` at the TOP of the basic block that the
preceding if/else merges into, ahead of the `ldrb` that begins the index
computation. Binding the index first --

```c
idx  = flag + ((src[0] & 0xF0) >> 3);
func = gTable[idx];
```

-- moves the entire address computation (pool `ldr`, `lsls #2`, add, load) down
to the assignment statement, which is where the ROM has it. This is the same
family as the note in `include/unknown-globals.h` about a binding's `ldr` being
emitted with its binding statement, read in the opposite direction: there the
binding moved a pool word too EARLY, here it is what moves it late enough.
**If a pool `ldr` sits at the top of a merge block in your candidate and later
in the ROM, split the statement.**

### `(x >> 8) << 4` IS NOT FOLDED INTO `(x & 0xFFFFFF00) >> 4`

agbcc 2.9 leaves two shifts where the ROM has one pool-loaded mask plus one
shift. They are arithmetically identical and gcc folds this in later versions;
this one does not. Write whichever the ROM shows. In `Decompress` the source is
genuinely the mask form, because it is deleting a nibble out of the middle of a
header word: the count is `(src[0] & 0xF) | ((header & 0xFFFFFF00) >> 4)`, the
28-bit byte size with the 4-bit type field at bits 4-7 removed and the two
remaining pieces closed up.

Related, and confirming the existing rule rather than amending it: the `lsls #9
/ lsrs #11` pair that follows is `(x >> 2) & 0x1FFFFF` -- CpuFastSet's 21-bit
count field -- reached by combine from a mask plus a shift. It is NOT a bitfield
read, though it has exactly the shape of one (width 21 at offset 2). Count the
pair as `(u32)x << 9 >> 11` and simplify, per the standing rule.

### ONE LOCAL PER CALL ARGUMENT IS VISIBLE IN THE REGISTER ASSIGNMENT

`Interpolate` (200 B, six-case easing switch) went from 31.0% to 91.5% on this
one change and nothing else. The ROM funnels EVERY case's numerator through r2
and every denominator through r1, then copies r2 to r0 at a merge point shared
by four of the cases. Written with the expressions inline as call arguments,
agbcc allocates per case and computes each numerator straight into r0 -- which
is cheaper, hence the candidate was SIXTEEN BYTES SHORT. Assigning `num` and
`den` as locals in each case makes them one pseudo apiece with a live range
spanning the whole switch, and the consistent r2/r1 assignment plus the merge
copy fall out.

**Read a shared register across the arms of a switch as evidence of a local.**
A value that is computed differently in every arm but always arrives in the same
register was a variable in the source, not an argument expression. The
diagnostic is the CANDIDATE BEING SHORTER than the ROM with no missing
statements: the extra instructions in the ROM are copies into and out of that
variable's register.

Two smaller results from the same function, both measured:
- The power is the left operand. The ROM computes `t*t` first and multiplies the
  difference in last, so the source is `t * t * (to - from)`, not
  `(to - from) * t * t`. Left-associativity puts the accumulator on the power.
- Where a case's second Div argument is a bare variable rather than an
  expression (`Div(num, tmax)`), do NOT also spell it through `den`. With both
  arguments plain register copies they emit together in argument order, and that
  is what stops that case cross-jumping into the tail the other cases share.

`Interpolate` is parked at 91.5%, +4, with a ONE-INSTRUCTION residual: the two
reverse cases end `adds r4, r6, r4 / subs r0, r4, r0` where the candidate emits
`subs r4, r4, r0 / adds r0, r4, #0`, i.e. agbcc coalesces the result into the
dying CSE pseudo's register and copies to r0 instead of subtracting straight
into the return register. Instruction order is otherwise exact. The trailing
`.short 0x0000` is not a second defect -- 202 bytes of body padded to 204.

### THE ARM BLOCK AT 0x08000234 HAS SIX FUNCTIONS STILL UNCLASSIFIED

`data/asm-resident.json` records five ARM functions in this block
(`sub_08000234`, `sub_080003E0`, `sub_08000494`, `sub_08000540`,
`sub_08000554`). `grep arm_func_start asm/code.s` returns ELEVEN. The other six
are still status `asm` and sit in the never-attempted queue, where wave 56
drew four of them as targets:

```
sub_08000304   92 B    sub_08000360   72 B    sub_080003A8   56 B
sub_0800043C   88 B    sub_08000550    4 B    sub_08000568    4 B
```

They are ARM by the same argument as their five neighbours, and the bodies put
it beyond doubt -- these are instructions THUMB cannot encode at all:
`sub r0, r0, r3, lsl #1` and `sub r4, r4, r2, lsl #1` (barrel-shifted register
operand), `mov r0, #0x10000` (rotated immediate; THUMB `movs` is 8-bit),
`push {r4,r5,r6,r7}` paired with `bx lr` and no `lr` in the push. agbcc in this
tree emits `.code 16` / `.thumb_func` unconditionally -- every `compile_probe`
header reads "Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf" -- so no C in
this repo can produce any of them. Two of the four are already named INSIDE
`asm-resident.json`'s existing entries as the ARM targets of the linker
interworking veneers `sub_080718E8` (to `sub_08000304`) and `sub_080718F8`
(to `sub_0800043C`); the veneer chain was documented at both ends and the
middle left open, exactly as the `sub_08000234` entry describes.

**`fe_matches` is a reliable DETECTOR for this block and a trap if read as a
work queue.** It shape-matches five of the eleven ARM functions here
(`Checksum32`, `TmFillRect`, `TmCopyRect`, `TmApplyTsa`, `PutOamHi`) and the
bodies confirm all of them: `sub_08000360` sums u16s into one accumulator while
XOR-ing into another and returns `(sum & 0xFFFF) + (xor << 16)`, which is
Checksum32 exactly; `sub_080003A8` fills a w*h rect of halfwords on a 0x40-byte
row stride; `sub_0800043C` reads a 2-byte (w,h) header then copies halfwords
with a base added. The names are RIGHT and the C is still unreachable, because
Fire Emblem also has these as ARM. Two of its five hits here
(`sub_080003E0`, `sub_08000494`) were ALREADY `asm-resident` when it reported
them. **A full-strength `fe_matches` hit is not evidence a function is
matchable; check `mode` first.** Screening `fe_matches` output against
`mode == "ARM"` would have kept four functions out of this wave's batch.

More generally: **`get_function`'s `mode` field is worth reading during batch
selection.** Nothing else in the screen surfaces it, and an ARM function looks
like ordinary clean never-attempted work in every other column -- status `asm`,
no `work/` directory, small, zero backward branches on the index's count.

Conversely, `fe_matches` returned NOTHING for either of wave 56's two NAMED
THUMB targets, `Interpolate` and `Decompress`, which were the two the tool was
expected to help with. Both were matched or near-matched by ordinary reading of
the assembly instead. The tool's 61 hits are concentrated in the m4a sound
driver and this ARM library block; do not expect it to cover named game code.

## SCOPE A RETYPE SWEEP FROM `git status src/decomp/`, NOT FROM CHANGED HEADER PROTOTYPES (wave 56, orchestrator)

The standing rule is "scope a retype sweep by UNIT, not by caller". True, and
insufficient — **it does not tell you how to find the units**, and the obvious
method misses some.

I derived wave 56's sweep scope from `git diff include/unknown-functions.h`,
taking every prototype whose line was CHANGED (a `-` line, not a `+` line). That
found `sub_0801D348` and `sub_08047190`, whose units gave three promoted
functions. All three swept clean.

**It missed three more promoted files entirely.** W56-H had retyped four
functions' parameters `u16` -> `s16` by editing `src/decomp/c_0801E22C.c`,
`c_0801E27C.c` and `c_0801E294.c` **directly**, and those four are *defined* in
promoted units rather than *declared* in the shared header — so no header line
changed and the header-diff scope could never see them. Found only by reading
`git status --short` before committing.

Swept afterwards (5 functions across the three units, after `sync_work.py`):
**5 of 5 OK**, so nothing regressed and the agent's byte-neutrality claim held.
But the miss was luck, not method.

**THE CORRECT SCOPE, and it is strictly larger:**

```
git status --short src/decomp/     # every MODIFIED promoted file
git diff include/                  # plus every CHANGED prototype's unit
```

then expand each file to **all** its member functions and `sync_work.py` each
before `trymatch` — a promoted function's `trymatch` compiles `work/<fn>/<fn>.c`,
not `src/decomp/`, so an unsynced draft measures the stale copy and answers a
different question (the wave-25 six-function regression).

Cheap generalisation: **the set of promoted functions a wave put at risk is the
set of promoted FILES the wave modified.** Read it off git, not off your own
memory of what the agents said they did.

## An `||` LADDER OF `==` CONSTANTS FOLDS EXACTLY ONE RANGE TEST, THEN STOPS (wave 56, W56-J)

`sub_08010664` tests one map tile against **fourteen** constants, twice over.
Emitted, that is ONE range test followed by TWELVE individual `cmp`s:

```
adds r0, r1, #-0x142 ; lsls #16 ; lsrs #16 ; cmp r0,#1 ; bls hit   <- 0x142,0x143
movs r0,#0xa0 ; lsls r0,#1 ; cmp r1,r0 ; beq hit                   <- 0x140
adds r0,#1 ; cmp r1,r0 ; beq hit                                   <- 0x141
adds r0,#0x1f ; ...  0x160,0x161,0x162,0x163,0x122,0x123,0x121,0x120,0x103,0x102
```

**0x140 and 0x141 are adjacent and did NOT merge, and neither did 0x160-0x163
or 0x120-0x123.** That looks like evidence the source is not a plain `||`
chain. It is not. The chain is left-associated, so after the first pair folds,
the tree is `LE_EXPR || ==`; that pair fails to merge (the ranges are not
contiguous), and from then on **the lhs is a `TRUTH_ORIF_EXPR`, which
`fold_truthop` rejects outright — it requires both operands to be comparison
class.** Every later merge is blocked no matter how adjacent the constants are.

So: **write the constants in the ROM's emitted order and let exactly one merge
happen.** The naive reading — "adjacent constants merge, so the source order
must have interleaved them" — is wrong and would cost the function. Verified
byte-exact on both fourteen-way copies.

Corollary for reading a diff: a lone `lsls #16 ; lsrs #16 ; cmp #N` at the head
of a comparison ladder is the FIRST TWO source terms, not a hand-written mask.

## THREE SPELLINGS OF `symbol + CONSTANT` AS AN ARRAY BASE, ALL DIFFERENT CODE (wave 56, W56-J)

`sub_0800CB30` reads row 1 of four 0x20-byte ROM tables. The ROM does this four
times, with only the pool word changing:

```
ldr r0, =gUnknown_084888A0
adds r0, #0x10
adds r0, r7, r0          @ r7 is the index
```

Measured on this function, all three spellings, all three distinct:

| source | code |
|---|---|
| `base[k + 0x10]` | hoists `k + 0x10` into ONE pseudo that CSE shares across all four bases; the `adds #0x10` vanishes and the index add reverses to `adds r0, r2, r0` |
| `(base + 0x10)[k]` | folds the whole thing into ONE pool word holding `base+0x10`; **the `adds #0x10` disappears entirely** (-8 bytes over 4 sites) |
| `((struct Rows *)base)->row1[k]` | `ldr =base ; adds #0x10 ; adds k, base` — the ROM |

**This CORRECTS an unverified claim in `include/unknown-globals.h`.** W50-I
wrote there that "agbcc splits a `symbol + constant` address constant into a
pool load plus an `adds` on Thumb rather than putting the addend in the pool
word", and concluded the honest spelling was `gUnknown_08488900[i + 0x10]`.
That was inferred from unmatched assembly and **neither half survives a probe**:
agbcc DOES put the addend in the pool word when you write the pointer sum, and
the subscript form produces different code again. Only a **COMPONENT_REF pins
`base + K` as its own value** — the same mechanism W34-F documented for the
gUnknown_08499590 map planes, which is where the worked example lives. The
header note has been corrected in place.

## A `u16` LOCAL AND THE SAME MEMORY READ INLINE ARE DIFFERENT COMPARISONS (wave 56, W56-J)

Wave 15 recorded that a straight-line probe cannot separate `u16 v` from an
`int` with casts. Here is a real function where they are **two bytes and one
match apart**, and it is a clean read-out of `PROMOTE_MODE`.

`sub_0800F77C` compares one map tile against 0x163 in one arm and 0x162 in the
other. The ROM:

```
arm A:  ldr r0, =0x163 ; cmp r1, r0                                   @ SImode
arm B:  lsls r1, r1, #16 ; movs r0, #0xb1 ; lsls r0, #17 ; cmp r1, r0 @ HImode
```

- Bound to a **`u16` local**, the value is a PROMOTE_MODE'd **SImode** pseudo,
  so BOTH arms compare in SImode and arm B comes out `movs #0xb1 ; lsls #1 ;
  cmp` — two bytes short, and that was the entire residual on an otherwise
  size-exact 344-byte function.
- Written **inline as the array read**, the operand is a `mem:HI`, both
  comparisons are HImode trees, and agbcc then picks the encoding **per
  constant**: `0x162 << 16 == 0xB1 << 17` is synthesizable so it takes the shift
  form; `0x163 << 16` is not, so it falls back to comparing the
  already-zero-extended value against a pooled `0x163`. **One source spelling,
  two encodings — do not read the asymmetry as two different source shapes.**

The range test is unaffected either way: `(u16)(v - K)` is a truncation and
emits `lsls #16 ; lsrs #16` from both spellings. **The range test is NOT the
discriminator; the equality comparisons are.**

## NESTING A CALL IN ANOTHER CALL'S ARGUMENT LIST KEEPS THE SHARED ARGUMENTS LIVE (wave 56, W56-J)

Worth **44 bytes over six sites** in `sub_08010664`, and the two spellings look
equivalent:

```c
sub_08001158(A, B, sub_0800FD44(A, B, 0));     /* WRONG: A and B evaluated ONCE */

t = sub_0800FD44(A, B, 0);                     /* RIGHT: A and B recomputed */
sub_08001158(A, B, t);
```

Nested, agbcc evaluates the outer call's `A` and `B` into pseudos and keeps them
live across the inner `bl`. As two statements the intervening call kills the CSE
on the ROM tables inside `A` and `B`, and both operands are rebuilt — which is
what the ROM does. **The tell is a pair of callee-saved registers holding
argument values across a `bl` where the ROM re-derives them from a base
pointer.**

Related, same function: `rowOffset[..] + x + dx` and `rowOffset[..] + (x + dx)`
are different code. Left-associated, `x` folds in first and `x + dx` never
exists as a value; parenthesised, it becomes a CSE the following call reuses
(`adds r0, r3, #0` instead of rebuilding it). +4 bytes.

## `const` ON A ROM TABLE: A STORE DOES NOT FORCE A RELOAD, A CALL DOES (wave 56, W56-J)

A three-function controlled probe, run both ways with nothing else changed:

| reader | what sits between the two reads | `const` | non-`const` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_0800CB30` | a `strb` into the map's +0x1432 plane | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| `sub_0800F77C` | `bl sub_0800F564` | **exit 1** | exit 0 |
| `sub_08010664` | `bl sub_0800FD44` | **exit 1** | exit 0 |

`const` sets `RTX_UNCHANGING_P`, and CSE then keeps the value **across a call**,
deleting the second load and the reload of the `-fforce-addr` base word feeding
it. Across an aliasing **store** it makes no difference — the reload happens for
other reasons and both declarations are byte-identical.

**So `const` on a ROM table is neither a free accuracy improvement nor always a
defect. Decide it from what separates the two reads.** I got this backwards
first and wrote the wrong justification into `include/unknown-globals.h`; it is
corrected there now. The practical consequence: a table whose only reader has a
call between its reads must be declared non-`const` even though it demonstrably
lives in ROM.

## A LOOP COUNTER SHARED WITH A LATER LOOP OUTRANKS A FRESH ONE (wave 56, W56-J)

`sub_08003C48` opens with a row-offset loop and then a nested x/y sweep. A
**dedicated** counter for the first loop:

```c
for (i = 0; i < MAP->height; i++) MAP->rowOffset[i] = i * MAP->width;
```

is size-exact at 96.3% — the first loop's counter and its scratch swap r3/r4,
14 bytes, and nothing else in 380 bytes differs. Reusing the variable that is
also the inner counter of the following nest:

```c
for (x = 0; x < MAP->height; x++) MAP->rowOffset[x] = x * MAP->width;
```

**matches.** The wider live range lifts the counter's allocation priority past
the scratch it had been losing to. The same function reads the lever from the
other end too: splitting the row-offset loop off the sweep's `y` is what freed
the register the inner loop's `y * 2` giv had been spilling to the stack. Both
directions mattered in one function.

**Declaration order is NOT the lever, and that is worth saying because it is the
obvious thing to try.** Three orders were tested here and four on
`sub_08010664`; all byte-identical. Priority is live range and reference count,
not `expand_decl` order.

Where none of that reaches: `sub_08010664`'s last 48 bytes were a pure
`r6`<->`r7` / `r8`<->`sl` permutation at size-exact 95.8%, and decomp-permuter
closed it in ~1,960 iterations. Its lever was a **dead store inside a condition**
(`&& (v = y + tab[i] >= 0)`) in the second of three identical sweeps. That is
byte-correct and is flagged in the draft as NOT the original source — something
in the real source made one more value live across that sweep, and the permuter
reproduced the effect without recovering the cause.

### Two confirmations of other agents' wave-56 findings

**Case bodies emit in SOURCE order** (W56-P rule 1, W56-D's 22-case table),
independently re-measured on `sub_08003C48`: a 4-case tree on {1,3,4,7} lays its
bodies out 7, 1, 3, 4, and writing them in ascending order costs the match.
Cross-jumping then merges the identical tails of cases 4 and 7, keeping the
LATER copy and branching the earlier one forward into it.

**W56-P's `movs #k; lsls #1` reading is right and the constants recur.**
`sub_0800FD44` builds 0x142 / 0x160 / 0x140 / 0x122 that way; `sub_08010664`
compares against that same family, which is corroboration from a second
function that they are literals and not shifts.

### `start_function`'s stub sometimes carries a whole body — read it before writing one (wave 56, W56-J)

The brief and the tool's own docstring both describe the `start_function` stub
as a signature guess that "is often wrong". For `sub_08009F10` (392 B, 14
callees, never drafted) the `stub` field came back with a **complete candidate
body** — control flow, the `goto fail` shared return, the `(a & 0xfe00)` arms
and the map read — and it **matched byte-for-byte on the first `try_match`**,
with the only edit being the struct tag renamed from `MapScreen` to the
`Unk3F44Map` its promoted neighbours use. Cost: one probe.

Not a general claim that the stub is trustworthy — it is one function. But it is
free to read, and nobody in twenty waves seems to have looked at it for anything
but the signature. **Read the whole stub field before deriving a body from
scratch.** (Rename any `struct MapScreen` it hands you: wave 37 found that tag
defined 17 different ways across drafts.)

## An inherited draft's residual is almost always ONE REGISTER — the score measures WHERE it diverges, not HOW MUCH is left (wave 57, W57-D)

Wave 57 gave one agent five functions that all carried drafts, deliberately
spanning the score range, to answer why inherited drafts convert at ~9% against
~83% for never-attempted ones. Two explanations were on the table: the draft
**poisons** the attempt (anchoring), or the drafted pool is a **selection
effect** and the draft is a symptom. The instruction was "delete the body and
rewrite from the exemplar".

**It is the selection effect, and the selection is on the residual's KIND, not
on difficulty.** Two of the five closed. Neither closed because of the rewrite.

### The five residuals, measured before touching anything

| function | size | draft | first diff | what the residual actually is | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_080723DC` | 120 | 88.3% | +0x26 | one constant materialised 5 insns early; **same instruction count** | parked |
| `sub_08073A00` | 232 | 72.4% | +0x0 | one constant defined at a loop exit instead of at its first use → one extra live register → `push {r4,r5,lr}` | **MATCHED** |
| `sub_080726E8` | 216 | 18.5% | +0xa | `loop.c` reduces two givs the ROM does not; +12 B | parked |
| `sub_08071B9C` | 232 | 15.1% | +0xc | `proc`/`data` swapped between r7 and sl; +8 B | parked |
| `sub_08076E20` | 244 | 93.4% | +0x4 | one constant's slot, plus copy-vs-recompute in a max | **MATCHED** |

Every one of the five is **register allocation or constant placement**. Not one
was a wrong shape, a wrong type, a missing statement or a misread idiom. In four
of five the instruction *stream* was already correct end to end.

**Correct a number before reusing this table.** The wave brief listed
`sub_080726E8` at 56.9%. Its draft measures **18.5%**; 56.9% is what
`work/sub_080726E8/best.c` scores. The brief's own rule — ignore `best.json`,
it tracks `best.c` and not the draft `trymatch` compiles — had already been
violated by the table built from it. When a score is quoted to you, ask which
file it came from.

### The one mechanism, and it covers both failure bands

A byte-identity percentage is positional. A one-register difference shifts every
later byte, so the score records **where in the function the allocation
diverges**, not how much is wrong:

- diverges LATE (a constant misplaced near the tail — `sub_080723DC`) → **88.3%**
- diverges EARLY (one extra live value, so the prologue's push mask gains r5 —
  `sub_08073A00`) → **72.4%, first difference at +0x0**
- diverges at the top of a range that spans the function (`sub_08071B9C`'s r7/sl
  swap) → **15.1%**

So wave 34's 0-of-4 at 92–99.6% and W57-B's 0-of-5 at 13–31% are **the same
population sampled at two ends of one artefact**, and they need no separate
explanations. A high score means the register divergence happens late; a low
score means it happens early. Neither says anything about how much work remains,
because in both cases the remaining work is the same size: one allocation
decision. **The pool of drafted functions is the residue of everything whose
last difference was not expressible as a shape.**

This has a sharp corollary for reading a diff. `sub_08073A00` diverged at
**+0x0** — the very first instruction, a push mask — and the brief concluded
from that "the frame is wrong, so start from the frame". The frame was a
*consequence* of a constant defined 100 bytes later. **A difference in the
prologue is the last symptom to appear and the first one you see; never treat
`first difference at +0x0` as evidence about the frame.**

### Why "rewrite from the exemplar" is the wrong instruction here

An exemplar fixes vocabulary, types and shape. If the residual is not a shape,
rewriting from the exemplar reproduces the same allocation and lands on the same
diff. That is the whole of the ~9%.

- Three of the five named exemplars were trivial neighbours — `c_080723C0.c` is
  four lines, `c_08071B98.c` is one — that fix a type model already present in
  the draft. They cannot address an allocation residual, and no amount of
  reading them would have.
- What actually moved the two that fell was a **diff-directed micro-lever**: a
  parameter type, a ternary, an absolute loop bound. None of the three is
  visible in any exemplar.
- Deleting the body also throws away the ruled-out axes, which are the most
  valuable part of an inherited draft. `sub_080726E8`'s note saved four probes
  this wave by naming spellings already measured.

**So: for a drafted function, do not rewrite from the exemplar and do not read
the score.** Read the diff, classify the residual as shape / type /
allocation-or-constant-placement, and if it is the third, spend the entire
budget on spellings that move ONE constant or ONE register. Keep the draft's C
and its measurements; change one thing the diff points at.

Two of five at ~476 bytes per attempt is above the band table's prediction for
this size, so the drafted pool is not hopeless — **the 9% is a property of the
method that was applied to drafts, not of the drafts.**

### Mechanisms tested and REFUTED for the constant hoist (do not re-spend these)

`sub_080723DC` still emits `gPal[0] = 0;`'s constant one statement early. Both
natural explanations are wrong, by controlled probe:

- **Not cse sharing the zero with the earlier `= 0` stores.** Change the two
  earlier stores to `= 1` so no zero exists anywhere before it: agbcc still
  hoists, in fact one insn further.
- **Not the instruction scheduler.** `__asm__ __volatile__ ("")` between the
  preceding store and the gPal store — a full scheduling barrier — does not move
  it at all. The placement is decided by an RTL pass upstream of sched.

`src/decomp/c_08072344.c` matches with the identical `gPal[0] = 0;`, but there
the preceding statement is a **call**, which is a hard barrier, so the hoist has
nowhere to go and never shows. That file is therefore not evidence that the
spelling is wrong.

## W57-D replicated on six more drafts: "not a wrong shape" holds at 6/6, "one register or one constant" does NOT — there are at least two more residual kinds (wave 57, W57-E)

W57-E ran W57-D's method unchanged on a second, independent batch: six drafted
functions in blocks 0x08035–0x08039, every one measured with `try_match` on the
**existing** draft before anything was read or deleted. The half of W57-D's
finding that generalises is the important half, and the half that does not is
worth knowing before you spend a budget on the wrong lever.

| function | size | draft | first diff | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_080363F8` | 132 | 22.7% (+4) | +0x2 | **allocation** — one extra live value across `__umodsi3` |
| `sub_08035170` | 128 | 50.8% (exact) | +0xc | **allocation** — one callee-saved register holds a different thing |
| `sub_08035080` | 100 | 23.0% (−4) | +0x2 | **constant placement** — `+3` on base vs index, dragging the pool |
| `sub_08039588` | 172 | 43.0% (−8) | +0x20 | **constant placement** — two literals merged into one pool word |
| `sub_080373F0` | 88 | 73.9% (exact) | +0xc | **basic-block layout** — which of three identical `return 0` blocks survives cross-jumping |
| `sub_08039188` | 220 | 31.8% (+4) | +0xc | **cross-TU prototype conflict**, plus a register-pressure `ldrsb` fold |

**Confirmed, 6 of 6, and this is the load-bearing part:** not one residual was a
wrong shape, a wrong type in the ordinary sense, a missing statement or a misread
idiom. The exemplars named in the brief would not have addressed any of them, so
"do not rewrite a drafted function from the exemplar" is now measured on eleven
functions across two agents. Two of the six are also **size-exact**, and one of
those scores 50.8% — more evidence that the score is positional and says nothing
about how much is left.

**Refuted as a universal:** "the residual is one register or one constant, and
the whole budget should go on spellings that move one of them." That is 4 of 6
here (67%), not 5 of 5. The two exceptions are not near-misses of the same kind —
they are different kinds, and neither is reachable by a micro-lever:

- **Basic-block layout.** `sub_080373F0` is size-exact with an exact instruction
  *multiset*. Three source-level `return 0`s compile to three identical
  `movs r0,#0; b <epilogue>` blocks, cross-jumping keeps exactly one and
  redirects the others, and the residual is entirely *which one it keeps*. The
  ROM keeps the MIDDLE copy. Nine wave-43 spellings put it last, one wave-51
  spelling put it first; the surviving copy is the one entered by FALL-THROUGH
  while the others are branch-only and therefore deletable outright, and no
  spelling has yet made the middle site the fall-through-entered one. Register
  allocation and pool contents are already correct, so there is nothing for a
  one-register lever to move.
- **A conflict between two translation units.** `sub_08039188` needs its callee
  declared one way at the call site and another at the definition. No spelling of
  the caller can reach it; see below.

**So the classification step is worth more than the taxonomy it was given.** Read
the diff and classify, but allow more than three buckets — and when the residual
is layout or a cross-TU contract, stop rather than spending the allocation
budget on it.

### Two negative results that close open axes

- **The permuter does not rescue block layout.** `sub_080373F0` was the ideal
  case on paper — size-exact, instruction multiset exact, and its note recorded
  the permuter as never tried. 300 s, 19,619 iterations from the 73.9% draft:
  ceiling 73.9%, no byte match, best three candidates 73.9 / 40.9 / 61.4. Wave
  37's "order-wrong and slot-wrong are precisely its cases" means *instruction*
  order within a block, not which block survives cross-jumping.
- **`volatile` splits value CSE, not address CSE — re-confirmed, and the obvious
  theory about why is wrong.** On `sub_08035170` the ROM reloads a global's
  address through its `-fforce-addr` `.rodata` word after a call while the
  candidate keeps the finished `base + 0x2f` in a callee-saved register. The
  tempting explanation is that the `.rodata` word is ordinary (not
  constant-pool) memory, so a `bl` invalidates it and forces the reload. True of
  the ROM, but useless: gcc never needs the base again once the *address* pseudo
  is live, and a probe with plain non-volatile reads at both sites caches it
  exactly the same way. The reload only appears if the address expression itself
  is unavailable.

### An unnarrowed argument at a call site: COUNT THEM BY COMPILING, not by reading the ROM

This corrects a wave-43 conclusion in `include/unknown-functions.h` and is the
most transferable thing in the batch. The rule everyone uses — "an argument the
caller does not narrow is evidence about the declaration visible to the caller" —
is right. The wave-43 refinement built on it was that ONE unnarrowed argument is
ambiguous but TWO, of different signedness, in one call can only mean *no
declaration in scope*, i.e. C89 default argument promotion.

**The second of `sub_08039188`'s two was never unnarrowed by the caller's
choice.** Compiled against the existing `u8 sub_08039140(u16, s16, u8, u8)`, the
`s16` argument already emits a bare `lsls r2,r1,#4` and nothing else, because the
value is `s8 * 16` and combine deletes a sign-extension it can prove redundant
(`num_sign_bit_copies` ≥ 17). Only the `u16` argument costs a shift pair. So the
count was ONE, which is the case the refinement itself calls ambiguous.

**A narrowing that combine can prove redundant is invisible at the call site.**
Any argument narrow enough for its declared type — an `s8`-derived value into an
`s16`, a masked value into a `u16` — looks like a promoted argument in the
listing while its declaration is perfectly ordinary. Count by compiling.

### The unprototyped-declaration escape hatch does not exist in agbcc (probed)

Where a caller genuinely does need default argument promotion and the callee
genuinely does need narrow parameters, the one thing a single shared header might
have expressed is a K&R declaration — `u8 f();` — leaving the definition's
prototype to narrow on arrival. **agbcc rejects it, as a hard error and not a
`-Werror` warning:**

    conflicting types for `probe_fn'
    An argument type that has a default promotion
    can't match an empty parameter name list declaration.

That is the C89 6.5.4.3 constraint. So a function whose ROM caller has no
declaration in scope and whose definition takes sub-word parameters cannot be
expressed in this tree at all, however few callers it has (`sub_08039140` has
exactly one). Park it and say so; there is no spelling.

### `ldrsb` vs `ldrb; lsls #24; asrs #24` is REGISTER PRESSURE, not an idiom

Long-standing open question on `struct Unk0849D5F8`, and the answer is not the
address form. Probed on one `s8` member array, a **single** read folds to
`movs rN,#0; ldrsb` under every spelling tried — bound to an `int` local, reached
through a bound `s8 *`, indexed by an `int` instead of the `s8`, or multiplied
inline. Reading **both** parallel `s8` tables off the same base in one statement
group emits `ldrb; lsls #24; asrs #24` for *both*, with a byte-identical address
computation to the single-read case.

agbcc's THUMB `extendqisi2` needs a spare low register to materialise the zero
index (`ldrsb` has no immediate-offset form), and with the second table's index
and the first table's result both live it takes the shift path instead.
**Consequence: the shift-pair twin is not evidence that a member is `u8` or that
there is a cast in the source** — do not retype a shared struct on the strength
of seeing it, and expect the fold to reappear on its own if some other fix frees
a register.

## A sub-word PARAMETER's prologue conversion is its own insn group, and the first statement's constant lands AFTER it — `u16 p` and `int p` with a `(u16)` cast are different code (wave 57, W57-D)

This is the wave-15 blind spot on the parameter side, and it was worth two bytes
and a whole function (`sub_08076E20`).

    u16 p;  k = 4;  n = (p >> 4) & 0xf;     ->  lsls r0,#0x10 / movs r3,#4 / lsrs r2,r0,#0x14
    int p;  k = 4;  n = ((u16)p >> 4) & 0xf ->  movs r3,#4 / lsls r0,#0x10 / lsrs r2,r0,#0x14

`PROMOTE_MODE` emits the sub-word parameter's zero-extension as the prologue's
own group, before any statement, so the **first statement's constant is emitted
between the conversion and the first use of the converted value**. With the cast
there is no prologue group and the constant has nowhere to sit but in front.
`combine` folds the conversion's `lsrs #0x10` into the statement's `>> 4` to
produce the single `lsrs #0x14` in both cases, so **the merged shift is not
evidence against a `u16` parameter** — `include/unknown-functions.h` had carried
a comment arguing exactly that, and it was backwards.

Retyping a parameter is a contract change: re-run `try_match` on every promoted
caller. Here `src/decomp/c_0807703C.c` already passed a `u16` and stayed
byte-identical.

## ABSOLUTE and RELATIVE bounds for a second loop over one array emit the SAME loop but define the next shared constant in different places (wave 57, W57-D)

`sub_08073A00` clears two halves of one array, then does eight `strb`s of a
shared `0`. These two spellings emit an identical loop — same base, same count,
same `check_dbra_loop` `subs; cmp #0; bne`:

    for (i = 0; i < N; i++)      a[N + i] = 0;    /* relative */
    for (i = N; i < 2 * N; i++)  a[i]     = 0;    /* absolute -- the ROM */

but only the **absolute** form leaves the following `0` to be materialised at
its first use. The relative form defines it at the loop's **exit** instead, and
that one def cost four things in sequence: the early zero takes r3, so `proc`
cannot have r3 and moves to r4, the `-fforce-addr` base moves r4 → r5, and the
prologue becomes `push {r4, r5, lr}`. 64 of 232 bytes differed and every one was
that cascade.

Separate loop variables (`i` and `j`) also remove the early zero, but then pin
the second loop's exhausted down-counter — strictly worse. The axis that matters
is the subscript's origin, not the variable.

## `m = a > b ? a : b` copies BEFORE the compare; `m = b; if (b < a) m = a;` copies after (wave 57, W57-D)

Both keep the result in its own pseudo, and the doc's existing note that a max
"needs its own result variable" is right — but the two spellings are not the
same code, and it was 14 bytes in `sub_08076E20`.

    m = a > b ? a : b;          ->  adds r2,r0,#0 / lsls r0,r0,#0x10 / lsls r1,r3,#0x10
                                    cmp r0,r1 / bge / adds r2,r3,#0
    m = b; if (b < a) m = a;    ->  lsls r0,r0,#0x10 / lsrs r2,r0,#0x10 / lsls r1,r1,#0x10
                                    cmp r0,r1 / bge / lsrs r2,r1,#0x10

The ternary emits the `m = b` **plain copy** before the compare's `lsls #0x10`,
so `a` and `b` survive in their own registers and the taken arm is a second
plain copy. The `if` form computes `b << 16` for the compare first and then
derives `m` from it, letting the shift destroy `a`'s register, so both arms have
to shift back. Swapping the compare to `if (a > b)` changes only the `cmp`
operand order — it is not the lever. For `s16` operands the probe reproduced the
ROM's register numbers as well as its instructions.

## A duplicated `return k;` merges at the LAST site in the FIRST arm, and the TRAILING statement's value is the one that falls into the epilogue (wave 57, W57-F)

This closed `sub_0800AEAC` (120 B) in one attempt after wave 52 parked it
size-exact at 50.8% with a one-instruction residual and the diagnosis "a jump.c
block-placement tie, so run the permuter". The diagnosis was wrong: it is a
source shape, and it is fully determined by two things.

For a function whose returns are drawn from a small set of constants:

- **The value returned by the LAST statement gets the block that falls into the
  epilogue** and costs no jump. Every other value's block ends `movs rD,#k; b
  <epi>`.
- **Every other value's block is placed at the LAST site of that value inside
  the FIRST if/else arm**, and sites in later arms reach it by a BACKWARD
  conditional branch.

So the ROM's layout tells you the shape directly. `sub_0800AEAC` has
`movs r0,#1; b _0800AF1C` sitting mid-function at the fall-through of the mask
chain, and `movs r0,#0` falling into the epilogue, therefore:

- `return 0;` is the trailing statement, and
- every `return 1;` is a *conditional* return inside an arm, the last of them
  closing the first arm.

    /* wave 52's draft -- one extra `b`, 50.8% */      /* matches */
    if (v != 0) {                                     if (v != 0) {
        w = ...;                                          w = ...;
        if (w != 0) {                                     if (w == 0) return 1;
            if (w <= 0) return 0;                         if (w > 0) {
            if (mask-fails)  return 0;                        if (a == X) return 1;
        }                                                     if (a == Y) return 1;
        return 1;          /* <- plain */                     if (a == 0) return 1;
    }                                                     }
    ...tail...                                        } else {
    if (v > 0) return 1;                                  ...tail...
    return 0;                                             if (v > 0) return 1;
                                                      }
                                                      return 0;

A plain `return 1;` closing the first arm makes agbcc keep the merged block at
the TAIL instead, which forces a `b` at the first arm's fall-through. The two
shapes are otherwise the same instruction stream; the difference is 2 bytes and
it is the whole residual.

**Probe that identified the rule** (`compile_probe`, three variants in one
file). The mirror image -- conditional `return 0;`s in the arms with a single
trailing `return 1;` -- emits the ROM's instruction COUNT with the two blocks
swapped:

    aeac_g:  ... beq .L20 / .L27: mov r0,#0 ; b .L25 / <tail> / ble .L27
                 .L20: mov r0,#1 / .L25: pop        = 5 insns, ROM has 5
    aeac_h:  ... bne .L40 ; b .L34 / <tail> / bgt .L34
                 .L40: mov r0,#0 ; b .L39 / .L34: mov r0,#1 = 6 insns

`aeac_g` proving the mechanism in mirror is what said the ROM was the same
construct with the roles of 0 and 1 exchanged. **Read the ROM's two constant
blocks first: whichever one falls into the epilogue is your last statement.**

Corollary for the permuter: this is NOT one of its cases. The residual was one
extra instruction, and per the existing note the permuter cannot express that.

## The `((x - 1) * A + C1) * C2 + base` address fold is blocked by a BASIC BLOCK BOUNDARY and by nothing else (wave 57, W57-F)

`sub_080029F4` needs

    subs r1,r6,#1 / lsls r1,r1,#3 / movs r2,#0xa3 / lsls r2,r2,#2
    adds r1,r1,r2 / lsls r1,r1,#5 / ldr r2,=0x06010000 / adds r1,r1,r2

where agbcc emits three instructions and one pool word. Wave 52 ruled out four
spellings; this wave adds the two that matter and identifies the mechanism.

**Measured (`compile_probe`, four variants):**

| spelling | result |
|---|---|
| one expression | `lsl r3,#8` + `.word 0x6015080` -- fully folded |
| `idx = (x-1)*A + C1;` then `idx*C2 + base`, same block | fully folded |
| `idx = x-1; idx = idx*A; idx = idx+C1;` then `idx*C2 + base`, same block | fully folded |
| `idx = (x-1)*A + C1;` **before an if/else**, `idx*C2 + base` **after the join** | **NOT folded** -- `lsl #3 / mov #0xa1 / lsl #2 / add` then `lsl #5 / ldr / add` |

So **a statement boundary is not a fold barrier here** -- contrast the wave-46
chapter, which is about evaluation order and LICM, not about this fold. Both
`cse` and `combine` reset their value tables at a label (`reg_last_set_label`
vs `label_tick`), so the *only* thing that stops the chain is a real basic block
boundary between the parts.

Note the partial fold in the last row: `(x-1)*A + C1` still collapses to
`x*A + (C1 - A)` **within its own block** (`0xa3<<2` becomes `0xa1<<2`). The ROM
keeps `subs #1` AND `0xa3`, i.e. it is unfolded at BOTH joints, which would need
two separate block boundaries. `sub_080029F4` has all eight instructions in one
merge block, so no arrangement of the C reaches it. **That is why the function
is still parked, and it is a fold residual, not an allocation one.**

## `volatile` on a member read does NOT reproduce a ROM-side dead computation -- it keeps the LOAD and the branch only (wave 57, W57-F)

`sub_080079B8` and `sub_080077EC` both contain a genuinely dead
`(s8)p->unk36 + d` whose register is overwritten by the next instruction. Wave
52 established that a plain dead local is deleted outright (flow removes the
assignments, then jump.c removes the emptied if/else and the frame with it) and
listed `volatile` among the untried vehicles. It is now tried and it is not it.

**Probe:** `j = *(volatile s8 *)((u8 *)p + 0x36) + 4;` with `j` never read, and
the same as a `(void)`-cast expression statement. Both give:

    cmp r3,#0 / bne .L12 / add r0,r0,#0x36 / b .L14
    .L12: add r0,r0,#0x38
    .L14: ldrb r0,[r0]            <- ONE shared ldrb, cross-jumped

versus the ROM's five instructions **per arm**:

    add r0,#0x36 / ldrb r0,[r0] / lsl r0,#0x18 / asr r0,#0x18 / add r0,#4

`volatile` keeps exactly the MEM reference: the branch survives, the two address
adds survive, and one `ldrb` survives in the merge block. The sign extension and
the addition are separate RTL insns with a dead destination and flow deletes
both, and cross-jumping then shares the single load. **So `volatile` buys the
load and the control flow and nothing downstream of it.**

Two things the probe settled for free:

- The volatile form DOES reproduce `movs r3,#7; ldrsb r3,[r0,r3]` for `unk07`,
  where the plain form gives `ldrb r0,[r0,#7]; lsl; asr`. That is only because
  the second `if` gives `unk07` a second use, so it stays in a register and gets
  the register-offset `ldrsb`. It confirms the ROM tests `unk07` twice and is a
  clean instance of the wave-49 "`ldrsb` is about the ADDRESS" rule.
- A dead local is deleted whether or not the `p->unk3a` load is bound first, so
  wave 52's residual 1 and residual 2 really are independent.

Still untried for this construct: a dead store to memory that survives as a
computation. Nothing in agbcc's flow.c does memory dead-store elimination, so
the store itself would appear in the ROM -- which it does not. **Treat this as a
SHAPE residual with no known C construct, not as an allocation residual.**

## Replication of "an inherited draft's residual is almost always ONE REGISTER": 2 of 6, not 5 of 5 (wave 57, W57-F)

W57-D measured five drafted functions and found all five residuals were register
allocation or constant placement. Running the same method on six drafted
functions in `asm/code.s` blocks 0x08002-0x0800A, the ratio comes out
**2 of 6**, and the one function that closed closed on a SHAPE change:

| function | size | residual | class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_0800AEAC` | 120 | duplicated-return block placement, fixed by restructuring the returns | **shape** -- MATCHED |
| `sub_0800401C` | 172 | `h` vs `y + 1` for the third callee-saved register | allocation |
| `sub_080035C8` | 120 | one preheader insn's position among the LICM movables | placement |
| `sub_080079B8` | 84 | a whole dead if/else missing, 24 B and the frame | shape |
| `sub_080029F4` | 188 | an address expression folded that the ROM leaves unfolded, 5 insns | shape |
| `sub_080077EC` | 232 | first loop strength-reduced and reversed where the ROM's is neither; plus 079B8's dead chain | shape |

The two findings are compatible and the difference is probably **which drafts
the pool holds in a given block**, not a disagreement about drafts in general.
But the operational instruction that follows from 5-of-5 -- "if the residual is
not a shape, spend the entire budget on spellings that move ONE constant or ONE
register" -- has a load-bearing precondition, and **classifying the residual
before choosing the budget is the part that transfers; the 5-of-5 ratio is
not.** Here, four of six needed shape work and the only match came from it.

What did transfer verbatim, and is worth keeping:

- **Read the diff, not the score.** `sub_0800401C` reads 19.8% and its
  instruction stream is correct end to end.
- **Do not delete the body.** Every park note in this batch named spellings
  already measured, and three of them saved a probe each.
- Two of the six were mis-diagnosed by their own park notes (`sub_0800AEAC`
  said "permuter"; `sub_080035C8` said "the scheduler"). **The ruled-out axes in
  a park note are reliable; the note's proposed NEXT STEP is not.**

## An induction variable whose init PRECEDES the counter's init is SOURCE, not a giv — the preheader rule is decidable in reverse (wave 58, W58-B)

The preheader rule ("the preheader is written by three passes in a fixed order:
your source, then LICM hoists, then `strength_reduce`'s biv/giv inits, so
anything after a hoisted invariant was written by the loop optimiser and must
NOT be authored") has been read for several waves as a one-way prohibition:
*never* spell a second induction variable. That reading cost `sub_080200EC`
seventeen waves. It is wrong, and the rule has a cheap decision procedure in the
other direction.

**gcc emits a `strength_reduce` giv initialisation with
`emit_insn_before (..., loop_start)`.** `loop_start` is the `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG`,
which sits *after* the source's own loop-variable initialisation. So:

- an induction variable whose init lands **after** the counter's init may be a
  giv — do not author it;
- an induction variable whose init lands **before** the counter's init **cannot**
  be a giv. There is no pass that moves a compiler-invented init above source
  code that was already there. It is a second source variable, and you must
  write it.

`sub_080200EC` (Manhattan-diamond map fill, 244 B) is the worked example and it
matched on the first attempt once this was applied. Its ROM preheader is

    lsls r5, r2, #0x10        ; r << 16
    asrs r2, r5, #0x10        ; (s16)r
    rsbs r0, r5, #0
    lsrs r6, r0, #0x10        ; r6 = (u16)(-r)      <-- d init
    lsrs r0, r1, #0x10
    str  r0, [sp]
    asrs r1, r1, #0x10        ; (s16)cy
    subs r0, r1, r2           ; cy - r
    lsls r0, r0, #0x10
    lsrs r4, r0, #0x10        ; r4 = (u16)(cy - r)  <-- y init

`d` is initialised two instructions before `y`, so `d` is source. The wave-41
draft had read the same preheader, concluded from the headline of the rule that
`-r` "cannot legitimately be spelled as a second loop variable", and spent three
spellings trying to make `strength_reduce` invent `d` out of `y - cy` recomputed
in the body. The match is

    d = -r;
    for (y = cy - r; y <= cy + r; y++, d++)

**Two corollaries that came out of the same read and both matter for placing the
increment:**

- `d++` is in the **for-increment**, not at the end of the body. The row-bounds
  `continue` branches to the block that carries both increments, so a `d++`
  written at the end of the body would be skipped by it. Where a `continue` can
  reach the increment block, every counter stepped in that block is in the
  for-increment.
- The **emission order of the two increments fixes the comma order.** The ROM
  steps `y` then `d`, so it is `y++, d++`.

### Do not generalise this to "the ROM hoisted it, so author it"

The reverse case is in the same wave's batch and it is the opposite error.
`sub_0800CAA0` has a `strength_reduce` pointer giv that the **candidate** has and
the **ROM does not** — the draft's plain subscript `sym[i + 0x10]` gets a giv
with a preheader init and a loop-bottom increment, where the ROM rematerialises
`ldr =sym; adds r0,#0x10; adds r0,r2,r0` inside the loop every iteration. Both
functions are +12 bytes and both residuals are induction variables, in opposite
directions. Read the ORDER; do not read the direction off the byte count.

## Scoping an address base to the innermost conditional BLOCK suppresses `strength_reduce`'s pointer giv (wave 58, W58-B)

Measured on `sub_0800CAA0` (144 B, four parallel byte tables searched in a
16-iteration loop): +12 -> +8, and the giv and its loop-bottom increment both
disappear.

Of four address givs of the identical form `base_k + i`, agbcc reduced exactly
one — the only one whose `add_val` is a `CONST` expression (`sym + 0x10`) rather
than a bare invariant. The other three have their symbol force-addr'd into a
hoisted pseudo, so their address is `reg + reg` and reduction buys nothing.
The one reduced giv costs six instructions, and only ONE of them is the giv
itself:

    +3  preheader   ldr rX,=sym / adds / adds  -> giv init
    +1  loop bottom giv increment
    -3  loop body   address arithmetic removed
    +2  prologue/epilogue: the giv is a 9th live value, so a third hi register
        is saved and restored
    +1  loop body   the value pushed out of a LOW register now needs a `mov`

**So five of the six extra instructions are downstream of one extra live value,
not of the giv's own code.** This is the general shape of a giv residual on a
register-tight loop and it is why the byte count over-reads the cause.

Binding the base to a **block-scoped** local inside the innermost conditional
removes the giv. The two spellings are not equivalent and differ in the pool:

- `p = sym + 0x10;` then `p[i]` folds the addend **into the pool word**
  (`R_ARM_ABS32 sym` with addend `0x10`), which the ROM does not do;
- `p = sym;` then `p[i + 0x10]` keeps the pool word at **addend 0**, which the
  ROM does, and moves the `+0x10` into the `ldrb` displacement.

Prefer the second. Neither reaches the ROM here: both still HOLD the base in a
register for the whole loop, where the ROM holds nothing for it and reloads the
pool word every iteration. That remaining step has not been reached from any
caller-side spelling in three waves.

## The recurring residual in the drafted pool is a HOLD/REMATERIALISE inversion, not a shape error (wave 58, W58-B)

Three of six functions in one wave-58 batch have the same residual, at three
different byte deltas, which is why counting bytes hides it:

| function | delta | the draft HOLDS | the ROM REMATERIALISES |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_0800CAA0` | +12 | the 4th table's base, for the whole loop | `ldr =sym` + `adds #0x10` each iteration |
| `sub_08026290` | +8 | `gUnknown_03003FC0`'s force-addr word, whole function | a **plain** pool word, loaded at each of two in-loop sites |
| `sub_08028D28` | +4 | `&gUnknown_03003340`, hoisted to the function preheader | the pool word, reloaded once per OUTER iteration |

`sub_08026290`'s is the sharpest readout because it is visible in the
relocations rather than in the register allocation. The ROM's literal pool
carries **two words for one object**: a `.rodata` force-addr word that is
dereferenced and used exactly ONCE (the pre-loop `unk02` read), and a plain
`R_ARM_ABS32 gUnknown_03003FC0` word loaded fresh at each of the two in-loop
sites. The candidate emits only the force-addr word and reaches the struct as
`ldr r2,[r7]` at every site. `try_match`'s relocation list is the cheapest place
to see this — a candidate with FEWER pool words than the ROM for the same symbol
is holding something the ROM rematerialises.

The lever is not a spelling of the access. In every one of the three the
competition is between loop-invariant candidates for a callee-saved slot, and
what has to change is how many invariants are live at the hoist, not how the
winner is written. Do not spend a budget rewriting the access expression.
