## TWINS: TRANSPLANT THE MATCHED REGION VERBATIM BEFORE DIAGNOSING -- and when the ROM lands two values in one register in different blocks, suspect ONE variable (wave 80, W80-B)

`sub_0804EB78` was parked as "frame 48 against 44, one extra simultaneously
live value spilled; deleting the `volatile unsigned int new_var2` local is
WRONG (80.1% -> 60.6%)". Its twin `sub_0804F3C8` has the same first region and
that region was already byte-exact in the twin's draft. Diffing the two SOURCES
rather than either against the ROM: the twin spells the source entry inline in
each statement (`src->x + table[c * 10 + f * 2]`, entry first), binds the
group stride to a u16 local, has no do/while(0) round e1 and no cached copy of
`gUnknown_08552148[c]` -- the ROM keeps that address in r5 and RE-READS the
global for dst->y. Moving the twin's block across verbatim: 82.6% -> 98.4%,
frame 44, in one attempt. Wave 73's deletion had been right about the slot
and wrong about the rest of the statement, which is why it read as a
refutation.

`sub_0804F3C8`'s own residual ("k in r6 where the ROM has r4, n in ip where
the ROM has r6, and the unk0c value in r0 where the ROM has r6") was three
pseudos where the original has one variable: the first region's `f`, the
`n = k * 5 + unk1e[k]` sum, and the `unk0c[k]` test value are ALL `f` in the
ROM -- r6 three times, in three blocks. Writing `f = ...unk1e[k] + k * 5;`
and `f = ...unk0c[k]; if (f != 0xff)` with `k` its own global pseudo passed
to sub_080505A4 matched. The wave-77 `(f = k) * 5` permuter win had found the
same register by making f global through a copy the ROM does not have, and
every addend swap after it kept the copy (the 78.2% of W77-H and W80-B both).
**Same register, different block, no copy between them: one variable
reassigned.**

One more measured trade, agreeing with W80-C's do/while(0) chapter: on
`sub_0804EB78` the `do { e1 = ...; } while (0)` moves `c * 180` into ip (the
ROM) but re-allocates the gUnknown_02029B94 temporaries r3/r2/r0 -> r0/r3/r4;
without it the temporaries are right and `c * 180` goes to r9. Neither is the
source; the `int v` read above gives both.

## SWITCH LEAF POLARITY IS DECIDED BY CASE-BODY SOURCE ORDER; `case 0: default:` ON AN `int` SUBJECT BUYS THE `cmp/ble` LOW-BOUND TEST; AN ENUM SUBJECT ONLY MAKES THE COMPARES UNSIGNED (wave 80, W80-A) -- `sub_080242B0` MATCHED, `sub_0803BFBC` 65.7% -> 89.2% by hand -> 94.8% by permuter

Both wave-80 pre-registered hypotheses were tested by `compile_probe` on the
functions that motivated them. Hypothesis 1 is CONFIRMED and closed a
function parked for 45 waves; hypothesis 2 is REFUTED as stated, with a
measured side effect worth knowing.

### Hypothesis 1 (confirmed): the block after the decision tree is the FIRST case body in SOURCE order, and jump.c inverts a leaf only when its target is that block

`sub_080242B0`'s residual was one branch pair, the right leaf {14} of the
{6, [10,11], 14} tree: ROM `cmp r2,#0xe / bne _default / b _true`, candidate
`cmp r2,#0xe / beq _true / b _default`. Everything W35-C, W39-C and W77-I
tried reordered the case LABELS inside a group, defaulted, padded the node
list or moved the leaf out of the switch; nobody moved the BODIES.

The mechanism: `expand_end_case` emits the tree and `reorder_insns` it to the
start of the switch, so what follows the tree's last test is whichever case
body was written FIRST. jump.c turns `beq L; b default; L:` into `bne default`
only when `L` is the very next block. So:

- draft (`case 6:` body first, `case 10: case 11: case 14: return TRUE;`
  second): the tree's last leaf is followed by the case-6 body, the leaf
  keeps `beq true / b default` -- 3 bytes off, 97.7%.
- probe (a), the `return TRUE` group written FIRST: the leaf is followed by
  `movs r0,#1; b end`, inverts to `bne default`, and cross-jumping folds that
  body into case 6's identical tail, leaving `bne default; b <tail>` -- the
  ROM, byte-exact. MATCHED on the first `try_match`.
- probe (b), same with `default: return FALSE;` inside the switch: identical
  to (a).
- probe (c), TRUE as fall-OUT of the switch (`break` arms, `return TRUE;`
  after it): the whole tail layout inverts (`movs #0` block first); wrong.

Rule: **when a leaf's polarity is the only residual, reorder the case BODIES,
not the labels.** Label order within a group is bit-identical (W39-C); body
order is the lever. `sub_0803BFBC` confirmed it a second time the same wave:
its ROM has the `default` body directly after the tree, then case 1 falling
into the join -- and only `default:` written FIRST reproduces that.

### Hypothesis 2 (refuted as stated): an `enum` subject does not move a leaf; it makes the range compares UNSIGNED

`enum { T6 = 6, T10 = 10, T11 = 11, T14 = 14 } lo;` as `sub_080242B0`'s
subject left the leaf polarity exactly where it was and changed the root
range test from `bgt / bge` to `bhi / bcs`: agbcc's enum with non-negative
enumerators is an unsigned type. That is a usable tell in the other
direction -- a switch whose range tests are `bhi/bls/bcs` on a value loaded
by `ldrb` may be an enum subject -- but it is not a lever on leaf shape. For
the `{1, 2}` tree in `sub_0803BFBC` an enum `{0, 1, 2}` bounds BOTH children
(TYPE_MIN = 0, TYPE_MAX = 2) and emits `bgt case2 / b case0`, further from
the ROM.

### The `cmp #1 / beq; cmp #1 / ble default; cmp #2 / beq` tree is `case 0: default:` on an `int` subject -- and the same tree on a `u8` subject is the +8-byte W73-F result

`sub_0803BFBC`'s ROM tests `1`, then `<= 1 -> default`, then `2`. Read that
`ble #1` as combine's canonical form of `LT 2` (`simplify_comparison` rewrites
`x < C` as `x <= C-1` for C > 0). The only `emit_case_nodes` path that emits
`LT <right child's low>` for a first-tested node 1 is the NEITHER-CHILD-BOUNDED
branch: root 1 with a left child {0} and a right child {2} emits
`beq L1; bgt test; <left: cmp #0; beq L0>; b default; test: cmp #2; beq L2`,
and when `L0` IS the default label jump.c deletes the `cmp #0; beq` (a
conditional jump to the same place as the following `b`) and then inverts
`bgt test; b default; test:` into `ble default`. Two conditions, both
measured:

- the subject must be `int`-typed (or otherwise have TYPE_MIN < 0). On a `u8`
  subject the left child {0} is bounded at TYPE_MIN = 0, `node_is_bounded
  (left)` fires first, and gcc emits `cmp #1; blt case0` plus a different
  body layout -- that is the `+8 bytes, 8.0%` W73-F measured for `case 0:
  default:` and wrongly closed as "a third case node is refuted". It refuted
  the u8 spelling, not the node. `c_expand_start_case` keeps the member's own
  type, so the subject has to be an `int` local assigned from the member.
- `case 0:` must share the default body (`case 0: default: v = 1;`).

Two more facts from the same probes:

- A two-leaf tree CANNOT carry the low-bound test on any index type: the
  right-child-only path takes the `do_jump_if_equal` shortcut whenever the
  right child is a single leaf, before it looks at bounds. So "a switch
  subject whose type defeats node_has_low_bound" (the wave-73 lead) is dead
  by code reading; a third node is required and it must be UNBOUNDED.
- An if-chain is NOT an alternative spelling of this tree. `if (v == 1) v =
  3; else if (v < 2) v = 1; else if (v == 2) v = 2; else v = 1;` (and the
  `>= 2 &&` form) compile to a PRESET form -- `movs r1,#3; cmp; beq join;
  movs r1,#1; cmp; bls join; ...` -- with no per-case `movs` blocks. Per-case
  constant blocks reached by the tree mean a real `switch`.

### `case N: break;` on the value variable itself is an EMPTY leaf that jumps straight to the store

`sub_0803BFBC`'s case-2 leaf branches to the `strb` with r0 still holding
the loaded 2, and no `movs r0,#2` exists anywhere. `case 2: v = 2;` always
emits the `movs` (cse knows r0 == 2 on that edge but a constant of equal cost
beats the register in `cse_insn`'s tie order). The source is
`v = unk2f; switch (v) { ... case 2: break; }` -- the switch subject and the
stored variable are the same object.

### `?:` with a constant arm vs two stores under if/else

`d->m = c ? 1 : g.n;` emits `bne <movs #1 arm>` with the load arm falling
through. `if (c) d->m = 1; else d->m = g.n;` emits `beq <load arm>; movs
r0,#1; b join` and cross-jumps the two `strb`s. Same bytes, opposite arm
order; `sub_0803BFBC`'s ROM is the if/else form. (The wave-37 rule that `?:`
on a store is real code still stands -- pick by the branch polarity.)

## AN UNROLLED BYTE COPY IS EXPLICIT SOURCE, AND A MODIFIED PARAMETER IS COPIED OUT OF ITS REGISTER AT ENTRY (wave 80, W80-A) -- `sub_08061A40` MATCHED

W44-H proved neither of agbcc's block-move paths can emit `sub_08061A40`'s
sixteen unrolled `ldrb/strb` pairs and 24-trip 12-byte loop, and closed the
struct-assignment, `movstrqi`, `memcpy`/`move_by_pieces` and flag axes. Its
own `next` line -- "the source wrote the byte moves explicitly" -- is the
answer: sixteen `d[k] = s[k];` statements and a `for (i = 0; i < 24; i++)`
loop of twelve more with `dd += 12; ss += 12;` match byte-for-byte. Nothing
in gcc 2.95 merges adjacent byte stores, so the spelling survives `-O2`
verbatim; `check_dbra_loop` turns the ascending counter into the ROM's
`movs r3,#0x17 / subs / cmp #0 / bge`.

The one register fact, measured three ways: **a parameter that is MODIFIED
anywhere in the function is copied to a fresh pseudo at entry**, and that
copy is the first instruction. `d += 0x10` gave `adds r2,r0,#0` at +0x0 with
r0 becoming the byte scratch; with `d` untouched and `s += 0x10` it was `s`
that got copied (`adds r2,r1,#0`). The ROM addresses both parameters in
place through the head with r2 as scratch, so the loop pointers are two NEW
locals: `dd = d + 0x10` is `adds r2,r0,#0 / adds r2,#0x10`, and `ss = s +
0x10` lands in r1 (s is dead by then) as the in-place-looking `adds r1,#0x10`.
Read backwards: an `adds rX, r0, #0` at entry that is not a callee-saved copy
means the source modified the parameter; parameters used only in place mean
it did not.

## A DEAD `int` LOCAL RECEIVING THE RELOADED MEMBER DEFEATS STORED-VALUE FORWARDING (wave 80, W80-A) -- `sub_08048F4C` MATCHED after four parks

The residual (W35-L .. W59-D): after `p->unk01e--` the ROM re-reads the
member (`strh r0,[r2,#0x1e] / ldrh r0,[r2,#0x1e]`) before comparing it with
`unk020`, where agbcc forwards the stored pseudo and pays `lsls/lsrs` to
re-narrow it (+4 bytes). Aliasing, volatility, width, pointer provenance,
operand order and a dummy store were all measured and excluded.

The matched twin `sub_08047F70` (promoted in wave 30, same shape on a
parameter pointer) had the spelling all along:

```c
p->unk01e--;
if (((v = p->unk01e) == p->unk020) && (p->unk01e != 0))
    p->unk020 = p->unk01e - 1;
```

with `int v` declared and never read. Binding the load to a named local
stops cse substituting the just-stored pseudo into the comparison; the
member is reloaded, and `p->unk01e - 1` then compiles to the ROM's
`subs r0,#1` off the reloaded register (cse knows the reload is in r0), where
W35-L's `unk020 = unk01e - 1` had produced `sub r0,r1,#2` because the
forwarding was still active. The RIGHT arm of the same function needs no
help: its stored value (`unk01e + 1`) is computed BEFORE the guard branch, in
a different basic block from the reload, and is never forwarded. So the rule
is about the store and the reload sharing a block, and the lever is on the
LOAD side, not the store side the parked entry named. Three waves of
"comparison shape is exhausted" measurements were right; the answer was in
`src/decomp/` under the twin's name (the wave-77 grep rule, again).

## THE `ok` / KEPT-COORDINATE "TIE" IN `sub_08009538` IS NOT A TIE: THE ROM HAS A COPY AFTER EACH FIRST CALL (wave 80, W80-A, still parked)

The wave-37 record called the residual a bare r7/r8 allocno tie with the
instruction order correct. Reading the ROM against the draft by instruction:
every case's first check is `subs r4,rY,#1 / adds r0,.. / adds r1,r4,#0 /
bl / mov r8,r4 / cmp r0,#0 / beq / movs r7,#1` -- there is an EXTRA `mov
r8,r4` after the call that no allocation of one pseudo produces. The kept
coordinate is two pseudos: a per-case scratch that is the call argument, and
a second variable assigned from it AFTER the call and before the result is
tested (`n = y - 1; r = f(x, n); keep = n; if (r) ok = 1;` reproduces the
copy exactly). With one per-case pseudo instead, `ok` loses r7 and the
symmetric cases cross-jump wholesale (448 bytes against 488). One
function-scope `keep` shared by the four cases gets keep = r7, ok = r8;
function-scope `nx`/`ny` put the kept value in r5 ahead of x and y. The ROM
needs `ok` to outrank `keep` on `allocno_compare`'s priority
(`refs * log2(refs) / live_length`), and no measured spelling does that
without adding instructions. The permuter (300 s from the valid draft; the
recorded `best.c` was an INVALID 46.5% variant, `ok = tile; switch (ok)`)
found nothing. Parked with that evidence; do not re-run the permuter from its
+56-byte "best".

## THE DEAD-STATEMENT LEVER DOES NOT TRANSFER TO A BARE TIE -- BUT "SAME REGISTER, DIFFERENT BLOCK = ONE VARIABLE" CLOSED TWO OF FIVE (wave 80, W80-F) -- `sub_080872D0`, `sub_08000CCC` MATCHED

Controlled transfer test. Five parked functions whose residual was recorded as
a bare register tie with nothing behind it (sub_08000CCC 5 B, sub_08056638
6 B, sub_0805A0EC 2 B, sub_08059E3C 4 B, sub_080872D0 2 B; all size-exact,
all seven compiler profiles already swept by the orchestrator with zero
matches) were each given the W80-B dead-statement lever, the W80-A dead-int
load form, and the W80-C ref-count reading, by `compile_probe` first and
`try_match` only for a verdict. Result: **2 of 5**, and neither match came
from a dead statement.

| function | dead statement / dead int (W80-B, W80-A) | what closed it |
|---|---|---|
| sub_080872D0 | the parked draft's dead `i = 0x608F` was the lever half-applied | the ROM's four DivRem loops count in r4, i's register, with no copy between: `j` IS `i`. Reusing `i` gives one pseudo the refs of six loops, it wins r4 on priority, and the final PutSprite constant is no longer routed through r4. MATCH, no dead code. |
| sub_08000CCC | dead `v = a1;` after the store, and `((v = a1) & 0xC0) \| ((w = b) & 0x3F)`: byte-identical to the draft | `b = (a1 & 0xC0) \| (b & 0x3F); unk24 = b;` -- the OR assigned back into `b`. Both AND results become constant-tied local temporaries (`movs r1,#192; ands r1,r4; movs r0,#63; ands r0,r2`). MATCH. |
| sub_08056638 | dead address locals for either symbol at either point: byte-identical | not closed. A dead gUnknown_0202980A reference created BEFORE the first gUnknown_02029822 use (lower pseudo number) changes nothing, so the residual is not the allocno-number tie-break. A `do{}while(0)` region around the gUnknown_02029822 loads puts 22 in sb (ROM) but spills the outer counter -- a region weights every ref inside it. |
| sub_0805A0EC | dead `z = 0;` before the p binding: identical to the plain literal; W80-A `(v = props[off])`: worse | not closed. Residual refined: the permuter's long-lived `new_var3` zero OCCUPIES r3, which is why reload takes r2 for the `mov r2,ip` copy; a literal frees r3 and reload sorts it first. The ROM has the zero in r0 and something else live in r3. |
| sub_08059E3C | dead row-pointer local, W80-A `(s8)(v = ...)`, compute-then-copy `t2 = t`: all byte-identical | not closed. Two reload scratch picks; nothing a dead statement reaches. |

What bounds the lever, measured six times in this batch: **flow deletes a dead
set before it counts a single reference, so a dead statement only does
anything when cse has already substituted its pseudo into a later identical
expression** (W80-B's `k = b * 2` case). Three things cse never substitutes
that way, so the dead form of each is a no-op: a dead COPY (`v = a1;`,
`t2 = t;` -- cse canonicalises to the older register and the copy dies), a
dead CONSTANT (`z = 0;` -- a register is never cheaper than the literal's own
register, and `(set (mem) (const_int))` is not a Thumb insn so cse keeps the
literal's pseudo), and a dead ADDRESS the code already forms (`p = &g[side][j]`
-- renaming the address pseudo adds no ref). The W80-A dead-int form is
specific to a stored-then-reloaded member; on a value that is not forwarded
from a store it either does nothing or rewrites the block.

What did transfer was W80-B's OTHER finding, twice: **when the ROM lands two
values in one register in different blocks with no copy between them, the
source has ONE variable there.** On sub_080872D0 that was the loop counters;
on sub_08000CCC it was the OR result written back into `b`. Both parked
entries had measured every spelling of the temporaries and the constants and
never the variable count. Read that tell before believing a register
residual is a bare tie: it is the cheapest check in this file, and the
wave-37 rule that "reuse an existing local" inverts with the exit test does
not apply -- neither of these is in a loop exit.

Two mechanism notes from the misses. On sub_08056638 the tie between the two
row symbols is NOT the allocno-number tie-break (lowering one symbol's pseudo
number below the other's is byte-identical), so their `allocno_compare`
priorities differ and the `do{}while(0)` is the visible source of the
difference: a region raises the loop-depth weight of every reference inside
it, and one around the gUnknown_02029822 loads flips the held symbol to the
ROM's sb at the cost of the counters. On sub_0805A0EC the r2/r3 copy scratch
is not a use-count tie: r3 is simply occupied by the permuter's long-lived
zero pseudo, and the ROM has the zero in r0 with r3 held by something this
draft does not contain.

## RAW POINTER SUMS ALWAYS PUT THE CONSTANT LAST; ONLY A COMPONENT_REF FORMS `(ptr + c)` FIRST, AND THEN THE CONSTANT IS A MOVABLE (wave 80, W80-D) -- `sub_0803D558` stays parked

`sub_0803D558`'s residual (ROM `(ptr + 0x417A) + y*2` with the constant
loaded inside the loop; draft `(y*2 + ptr) + 0x417A`) was worked with eleven
`compile_probe`s. Three facts, all general:

1. **`expand_expr` reassociates every SImode sum it expands in address
   context.** The PLUS_EXPR case under `EXPAND_SUM` does "make sure any term
   that's a sum with a constant comes last" and "if adding to a sum including a
   constant, associate it to put the constant outside". So `(p + c) + i2`,
   `p + (i2 + c)`, `(int)p + c + i2`, `i2 + (c + (int)p)`,
   `(u16 *)((u8 *)p + c) + y`, and a pre-bound `t = y*2` added to
   `((u8 *)p + c)` ALL emit `(p + i2) + c`. Same-mode casts (`(int)`, `(u8 *)`)
   pass the modifier through and change nothing. The W80-C fold rule
   (`associate:`) decides which operand a constant is grouped with at the TREE
   level; this rule then flattens the constant to the outside at RTL level, so
   for pointer arithmetic the fold rule cannot be used to put `(p + c)` first.
2. **`(*(T (*)[N])(p + c))[i]` is not an ARRAY_REF.** `c-typeck.c`'s
   `build_array_ref` builds a real ARRAY_REF only when the array operand is
   not an INDIRECT_REF; a subscript on a dereferenced pointer-to-array becomes
   `*(ptr + i)` and reassociates like any raw sum. Do not spend a probe on it.
3. **The COMPONENT_REF path is the only one that forms `(p + c)` first** --
   `normal_inner_ref` applies the member's bitpos with `plus_constant` and
   forces THAT into a register before adding the variable offset -- and it
   reproduces the ROM's grouping for both the row (`(p + 0x417A) + y2`) and
   the cell (`(p + 0x1432) + idx`). But the constant then arrives as its own
   `(set u 0x417A)` insn (the thumb `addsi3` expander forces non-encodable
   constants into registers), i.e. a LICM movable. Whether it is hoisted is a
   `move_movables` decision that depends on the loop's composition and not on
   the value or the load's mode: with the two constants' VALUES swapped the row
   constant still hoists; with both arrays `u8` it hoists; with the CELL array
   `u16` (one extra `lsl` in the body) the inner loop hoists nothing at all;
   alone in a tiny loop each constant hoists. In the real function the struct
   spelling hoists 0x417A (+4) and the ROM does not. The mechanism is
   consistent with `move_movables`' `threshold * savings * lifetime >=
   insn_count` test (a lifetime-1, savings-1 constant fails it in a big enough
   loop), but that is inferred, not read from source; agbcc's loop.c is not in
   the tree. **Read-out rule: an in-loop `ldr rN, =bigconst` next to a
   `(p + c)` add in the ROM is a movable the loop optimiser declined, and the
   lever is something that changes the loop's insn count or the constant's
   lifetime at loop time, not the spelling of the sum.**

## THE SECOND `?:` OF A PAIR THAT EMITS `bne L; movs #K; b; L: subs` IS AN if/else STATEMENT (wave 80, W80-D)

On `sub_0804A760` both `x == 0 ? K : x - 1` and `x != 0 ? x - 1 : K` emit
`beq L; subs; b; L: movs #K` (the then-arm falls into the shared store). The
ROM's `bne L; movs #K; b; L: subs` is what `if (x == 0) x = K; else x = x - 1;`
emits -- two stores that cross-jump at the `strh`. The FIRST of each pair
(`x > N ? 0 : x + 1`, ROM `bgt L; adds; b; L: movs #0; b`) is a genuine `?:`;
written as four `if/else` stores it comes out `ble L; movs #0; b; L: adds`. So
the original mixes a conditional expression for the wrap-increment with an
if/else for the wrap-decrement, in both the unk1e and the unk20 pair.
**Read-out: which arm falls into the shared store tells `?:` from `if/else`;
the polarity of the compare alone does not.**

## `((x + 1) & 0xff) | 0x80` KEEPS ITS MASK ONLY THROUGH A MULTI-SET LOCAL (wave 80, W80-D)

For a `u8` member store, `((x + 1) & 0xff) | 0x80` inline, a `u8` local, and a
`(u8)` cast all let nonzero_bits prove the mask redundant and re-canonicalise
`| 0x80` as `| -0x80` (`movs r3,#0x80; negs r3,r3; adds r2,r3,#0; orrs`). The
ROM's `movs r1,#0xff; ands; movs r1,#0x80; orrs` needs `c = x + 1; c &= 0xff;
c |= 0x80; x = c;` -- the wave-57 rule (nonzero_bits is tracked only for a
single-set pseudo) applied to a mask. Measured on `sub_0804A760`'s `unk66`.

## A `register int v asm("rN")` PIN DEFEATS local-alloc's DESTINATION TYING -- AND UNPINNING A DRAFT THAT SCORES ON PINS COSTS 47 POINTS (wave 80, W80-D)

`sub_0804A760`'s draft pins flag/t/u/c to r8/r6/r4/r3. In the `case 1` default
arm the ROM writes `adds r0,r6,r0` (the table sum into the dying table-address
pseudo's register), the pinned draft `adds r6,r6,r0`: local-alloc ties an add's
destination to a dying PSEUDO input, and a hard-register variable is never a
pseudo, so the pin hands the destination the hard reg. That proves `t` was an
ordinary pseudo in the original. Removing all four pins, with every other fix
in place, is 12.4% against 59.3% -- flag lands in r7 and the three
`unk63 = flag` arms cross-jump into one store. **A pin in a draft is a costume
for an allocation construct nobody has found; note it as such and do not
promote it.**

## THE W80-C FOLD RULE READ BACKWARDS CLOSED `sub_0804A760`'s CLASSIFIED HUNK WITHOUT A STATEMENT SPLIT (wave 80, W80-D)

`gUnknown_084C36E4[t] + 1 + gUnknown_030044E0->unk65` is `(VAR + CON) + ARG1`
and folds to `table[t] + (unk65 + 1)`: the table address is expanded first and
the member load deferred -- the wave-77 hunk. `gUnknown_030044E0->unk65 + 1 +
gUnknown_084C36E4[t]` folds to `unk65 + (table[t] + 1)`, whose expansion forms
the unk65 ADDRESS, then the table load plus one, then the deferred unk65 load
and the add: the ROM, instruction for instruction. The wave-77 header said "the
operand order of the sum cannot move it, since the ROM loads the table byte
first" -- it read the emitted order back into the source. **When the ROM loads
the constant-grouped member SECOND, the source wrote that member FIRST.** The
W43-I "give the pointer global its own statement" axis was the wrong tool.

## AN IN-LOOP POINTER LOCAL IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE ARRAY FORM; THE ROW-ANCHOR ORDER ON `sub_08055940` IS A HOIST-ORDER TIE (wave 80, W80-D)

Every row-1-named spelling of `sub_08055940`'s loop is now measured:
`gUnknown_020296E4[i - 20]` puts `subs #0x14` in the body; `(&E4)[-1][i]`,
`*(E4 - 20 + i)` and `*(u16 *)((u8 *)E4 - 0x28 + i * 2)` fold to one pool word
`E4-0x28` and derive row 1 with `adds #0x28` -- the draft up to the reloc
name. A pointer local DECLARED IN THE LOOP BODY (`u16 *row0 = E4 - 20;`) and an
in-loop `int base` are also byte-identical to the array form, so wave 77's
"any pointer local costs 12 bytes" was about locals defined OUTSIDE the loop.
Mechanism: the two row reads are in different extended basic blocks, so cse1
cannot relate their constants; LICM hoists the loop's four invariants in body
order, and cse2 then derives whichever row constant sits SECOND in the
preheader from the first. A row-0-first body always yields
[row0][&c0][row1][&c1]; the ROM's [&c0][E4][&c1][E4-0x28] has the row-0
constant hoisted LAST, which is a deferred hoist that no body spelling reaches.
Bare tie; stopped at two attempts.

## THE W80-C REF-COUNT LEVER NEEDS A WRITTEN-OUT TAIL THAT REFERENCES THE TIED PSEUDO (wave 80, W80-D) -- `sub_08049944` stays parked

Six no-split spellings of `sub_08049944` (duplicated `sub_08013AFC(); return;`
tail, the tail under both `if (a4)` polarities, a `goto` past the second call,
`0` for the sixth argument in the a1 == 0 arm -- one ref fewer for a1, cse still
storing the known-zero register -- and `a1 - a1`) all keep a1 in r5 and a4 in
r6. None of this function's shared tails mentions a1 or a4, so there is no
count to inflate. The lever transfers only when the arm tails contain the
pseudo whose priority is wrong.

## AN EMPTY-ASM BARRIER THAT "FIXES" A GIV CAN BE MASKING A CORRECT LAYOUT -- delete it and read the FRAME before spending spellings (wave 80, W80-E)

`sub_0805D888` carried an `asm("" : "+r"(sx), "+r"(sy))` barrier for four
waves because without it two strength-reduced givs (`x<<16`, `y<<16`) cost +36
bytes. Wave 80 deleted the barrier in a `compile_probe` and found that the
barrier-free build reproduces the ROM's ENTIRE remaining structure at once:
the frame slot order (bestX spilled to sp+4, bestY sp+8, flag sp+12, e
sp+16 -- reload allocates slots in descending pseudo order, so slot order
reads out DECLARATION order), the hoisted-mask allocation, and even the ROM's
odd loop-entry guard. The barrier was buying 36 bytes and PAYING for it with
the wrong frame, the wrong guard operand and a blocked permuter. Two
transferable readouts:

- **The ROM's y-guard `ldr r3, [sp, #8]; cmp r3, r0` compares BESTY'S SPILL
  SLOT against the bound.** That is not a variable read: at `y = 0` cse knows
  y == 0 and replaces it in the compare with the 0-class's representative
  register, which is a pseudo (bestY) initialised to 0 at the top. **A guard
  that compares an apparently unrelated zero-initialised variable is cse
  constant-class substitution, not source** -- do not chase it with a
  spelling; reproduce the zero-init ORDER instead.
- **A `mov ip, <giv reg>` copy right after a call, whose target is only read
  in a post-loop block, is loop.c's NOT-REPLACEABLE move** -- proof the giv's
  value is live outside the loop, i.e. cse merged a post-loop use with the
  in-loop expression. On sub_0805D888 the merged use is the `found:` exit
  block's `(s16)x` / `(s16)y`. Every spelling probed still merges (int fx/fy
  at the label, fx/fy copies at the goto site, the exit call inline in the
  loop, `s16` copies at the body call -- the last because thumb `extendhisi2`
  expands to two shift insns, so `(ashift biv 16)` exists and is reduced in
  every cast spelling). The remaining open construct for that function is
  whatever keeps the exit conversion out of cse's reach in the original.

## AFTER AN INTERIOR LOOP, cse's TABLE IS EMPTY: a post-call re-derive on one path and a kept register on the other means A LOOP SITS BETWEEN (wave 80, W80-E)

`sub_0802FACC`'s 0x1a/0x86 arm reads `&gUnknown_0849B018` (an unchanging
`.rodata` pool word, NOT invalidated by calls) at the arm head and again
after calls on both branches. The ROM keeps the head's register (r5) across
`sub_08030838` on the 0xAF path but RE-DERIVES from the pool-word address
after the calls on the 0xAD path. The difference is not volatile, not a
barrier, and not source: the 0xAD body contains the 13-byte copy LOOP, and
the loop-top CODE_LABEL ends cse's extended basic block, so everything after
the loop starts with a fresh table and must re-load. The loop-free 0xAF path
stays in the head's extended block and keeps the register. Read backwards:
**re-derive after a loop, keep across a call, in the same function, is ONE
mechanism, not two source spellings.**

## `if (x != K) { A } else { B }` places B OUT OF LINE -- and the ROM can show the same statement at the top of BOTH branches (wave 80, W80-E)

`sub_0802FACC`'s ROM tests `cmp #0xAD; beq _0802FC6C` with the 0xAD body
after the 0xAF part: source order `if (pkt->unk00 != 0xAD) { <0xAF part> }
else { <0xAD body> }`. Both branches open with their own `next = i + 1`
(+0x166 and +0x226 -- a genuine duplicated source statement; cse cannot
delete the second because the arm label has two uses and starts a fresh
block). Writing the arm this way took the draft from -12 to -4 bytes. The
CAUTION: transcribing the ROM's five FURTHER scattered `next = i + 1` sites
(inside the case-4 arms) as source statements regresses to +52 and costs the
pool-address cache its register -- the ROM's remaining increments are not all
plain per-arm statements, and their origin is still open.

## A PIN CAN REPORT SIZE-EXACT WITH WRONG CODE: check the .s for writes to the pinned register inside the variable's live range (wave 80, W80-E)

`register int i asm("r7")` on sub_0802FACC (the ROM's register for i, per
W79-A lever 1) reports size-exact 1388/1388 -- and the emitted 0xAD copy loop
uses r7 as the reload scratch for the `gUnknown_020257E4` base WHILE i IS
LIVE, then stores the clobbered r7 as the packet's slot id. gcc 2.95 does not
guarantee an explicit-register local stays put outside asm statements, and
`trymatch`'s byte comparison cannot catch a wrong-code candidate that
happens to fit. First measured pin failure after W79-A's three successes:
after any pin, grep the .s for writes to the pinned register before
believing the score.

## Toolchain profile sweep survey, wave 81 (W81-E) -- complete measurement of the open drafted pool
**What ran.** Every function in the open drafted pool -- all 138 `data/parked.json` entries
(every one has a draft) plus the 17 drafted unmatched non-parked functions, 155 total,
superseding preflight's "148" -- was compiled under **all six non-configured profiles plus
`configured`, 1,085 `tools/trymatch.py` shell runs** (exit code and `% identical` recorded;
single-run cost ~0.7 s). The match detector was validated before trusting its negatives:
the wave-79 closures reproduce as exit 0 under their mechanisms (`sub_0808AC7C` under
`o1-no-force`, `sub_08070D98` under `old-agbcc`), so a hit would have been caught.

**Outcome counts (measured, not recorded):**

- Outcome (a), exit 0 under ANY non-default profile: **0 of 155** (0 of 930 pairs).
  No open drafted function is matchable off the default toolchain.
- Outcome (b), best off-default score >15 points above configured ("JUMP"): **7**.
  Between 4 and 15 points ("move"): **15**. Within 4 points either way ("flat"): **133**.
- Direction asymmetry: 22 of 155 improve >4 points somewhere; **120 of 155 DEGRADE >4
  points somewhere**. The default configuration is already at or near each draft's
  maximum; a low configured score is normally *not* the pool hiding behind a wrong
  profile. Where it is, see the mechanisms below.

**The seven jumps, attributed flag by flag** (all numbers today's drafts, measured):

| fn | size | cfg | mechanism | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sub_08018100 | 92 | 22.8 | removing `-fforce-addr` at -O2 ALONE | no-force 82.6, old-agbcc-no-force 82.6 identical; old-agbcc alone 25.0 |
| sub_08058A2C | 392 | 24.5 | `-O1` ALONE | o1 = o1-no-force = 77.6; force-addr inert here |
| sub_0805D438 | 436 | 17.9 | plain `-fforce-addr` removal at -O2 | no-force 65.6 beats o1/o1-no-force 41.7 and old-agbcc-no-force 56.2 |
| sub_0804F658 | 612 | 31.4 | old compiler WITH `-fforce-addr` kept | old-agbcc 52.6, old-agbcc-no-force 15.8, no-force 18.0 |
| sub_0801DCD4 | 516 | 12.0 | needs BOTH -O1 and no-force | o1-no-force 33.3 vs o1 15.3, no-force 9.9, cfg 12.0 |
| sub_080077EC | 232 | 25.9 | `-O1` | o1 = o1-no-force = 43.1 |
| sub_08028D28 | 240 | 27.1 | `-O1`, partially cancelled by force-addr removal | o1 43.3 vs o1-no-force 27.5 |

Winner-profile census over movers+jumps (22): o1-no-force 9, old-agbcc-no-force 5,
old-agbcc 4, o1 3, no-force 1, default 0. Three different single-flag mechanisms operate
(`-O1` vs `-O2`, `-fforce-addr` on/off, cc1 version) and two functions need a specific
*combination* -- confirming W79's "o1 and o1-no-force are DIFFERENT" as a general rule,
not a flash-block special case.

**Clustering answer: there is none.** The nearest override entry to any of the seven jumps
is +0x13174 away (+0x17b80, +0x20f54, +0x47884, +0x528d8, +0x584ac, +0x68dc0 for the rest)
-- every one far outside both known override blocks and unreachable by wave-79's "within
0x600 of an overridden function" screen. Profile sensitivity is a PER-FUNCTION property,
which matches W38's original finding (the discriminator was a call inside a loop body, not
an address range) and refutes any hope of localising it by address. Wave 79 closed three
latent partial-sweep cases; this survey certifies that **no further latent ones remain**: every parked toolchain claim testable against these runs agreed within 3 points, including
sub_08012B70 (87.5/8.0/85.2), sub_08070F44 (56.7/19.2/68.3), sub_080620FC (old-agbcc 42.7),
sub_080029F4 and sub_08068A00 (old_agbcc byte-neutral, unchanged), sub_0808AAF4 (-O1 worse:
34.2 vs 59.9), and the flat verdicts on sub_08074AD0, sub_0803D558, sub_0804A760,
sub_0804F18C, sub_08073228, sub_08073480 whose notes assert toolchain negativity. The four
apparent numeric mismatches are all explained inside their own entries or by draft drift:
sub_080620FC "configured 72.7" is the divergent permuter best.c the entry itself disowns;
sub_0808AAF4 "no-force 28.3" was marked STALE by W79-D (today 59.9); sub_0808A3DC "-O1
60.0" (W60) vs 55.6 today and sub_08049944's superseded figures reflect drafts that moved
after recording -- exactly the wave-60 stale-score warning operating. **No parked.json edit
was needed:** the wave-46 "TOOLCHAIN AXIS RULED OUT ... do not re-run it" text on
sub_0808A3DC was already corrected by that same entry's wave-60 note, and nothing else in
parked.json contradicts measurement.

**Practical consequence.** The sweep is now cheap enough to be routine: ~0.7 s per pair,
the whole pool inside a few minutes. Before spending a wave's probes on any source
residual, re-run the six profiles mechanically instead of reasoning from an older note.
A better off-default score is diagnostic about where allocation diverges and is worth a
coordinator override ONLY with a byte-exact match under that configuration -- outcome (a)
above says no such case exists today. And remember the direction asymmetry: most profile
changes make a draft worse, so a failed profile probe does not mean the axis never fires.

**Harness note.** Parallel sweeping across FUNCTIONS collides: trymatch.py writes fixed
shared comparison artefacts `build/unitcheck/_target.bin` / `_cand.bin`, so eight workers
produced five exit-code-2 failures with empty output among 930 pairs. Re-run sequentially;
they then all parse cleanly. Per-function `--profile` artefacts (_cand.<prof>.bin/.o/.s)
are collision-free by construction.

## The `sub_08004D90` row above is STALE: the survey ran against a pre-fix draft; the real residual is a `X - (-Y)` vs `X + Y` add-destination tie, reachable WITHOUT a toolchain override

The wave-81 table lists `sub_08004D90` at 19.1/19.1/19.1/20.6/20.6/19.1/19.1
("flat") because the survey ran against whatever draft existed at the time --
one that had not yet bound `dst = &gUnknown_08499578` (now `gBG0TilemapBuffer`)
inside each `if`/`else` arm. **A stale row in this survey is scoped to the
draft it measured, not to the function**; re-run `trymatch.py --profile` on any
row before trusting it once the draft has moved.

Re-measured on the current draft (`offset`/`dst` bound as above): `configured`
(the canonical toolchain) gives 85.3%, 10 differing bytes, a whole-function
`r0`/`r1` swap from the first branch onward. `o1`/`o1-no-force` jump to 98.5%,
1 differing byte -- but so does `configured` itself, with **no profile change
at all**, once the final statement is spelled as a subtraction of a negation
instead of a plain sum:

```c
sub_0801F2AC(9, *dst + offset);        /* configured: 85.3%, whole-fn r0/r1 swap */
sub_0801F2AC(9, (*dst) - (-offset));   /* configured: 98.5%, size-exact, 1 byte   */
```

Both spell the identical value. The second removes the ENTIRE register swap
under the real toolchain -- not just the final add -- landing on exactly the
same one-byte residual `o1` reaches by changing optimisation level instead.
Confirms a second, independent mechanism reaches the same wall, and this one
needs no `data/compiler-overrides.json` entry to use.

**The exact spelling matters, and it is not just "subtraction instead of
addition".** `-(-offset) + (*dst)` -- mathematically and by C's `+`/unary-`-`
precedence identical to `(*dst) - (-offset)` -- compiles back to the 85.3%
swapped form. Only `pointer_expr - (-int_expr)`, pointer side first as the
minuend, negated int side second, gets the fix; simplifying the double
negation early (by writing the `+` form, however the double-negative is
arranged around it) loses it. This was found already sitting in
`work/sub_08004D90/best.c` from an earlier permuter run (`prefer_best`
default), predating the `gBG0TilemapBuffer` rename -- **always diff a
function's own `best.c` against its current draft before writing off a
residual**; a tied or higher score there can carry a lever the live draft
never tried.

The one byte still open after the subtraction trick (`configured`, size-exact,
first diff at +0x24) is the same one `o1` alone reaches:

```
ROM   adds r1, r0, r1      @ result = (loaded *dst) + offset
cand  adds r1, r1, r0      @ same operands, destination tied to the OTHER one
```

**This last byte resisted every lever tried, including two independent real
permuter runs (~29,500 iterations against the o1-compiled target, ~30,000
against the `(*dst) - (-offset)` configured-toolchain target, 240s x 8 threads
each, `--better-only --stop-on-zero`, zero candidates beat either base score),
plus a from-scratch TILEMAP_LOCATED/TILEMAP_INDEX-macro rewrite permuted for
240s more (53 candidates tried, best only 47.1% -- the macro folds the `+3`/
`*0x20` constants into the shift/add pair at the SOURCE level, discarding the
structure a mutator would need to reconstruct; not a useful starting point for
this residual).** Also ruled out directly on the subtraction-form base:
reordering the C operands both ways (`*dst + offset` and `offset + *dst`
compile byte-identical -- combine's commutative canonicalisation erases the
source order once both operands are already loaded into bare `REG`s), a
zero-trip `do { } while (0)` wrapped around the branch, around the `offset`
arithmetic alone, around the call alone, and around the subtraction-form call
specifically (no effect in any position -- consistent with the wave-38/60 rule
that the zero-trip lever moves `allocno_compare` PRIORITY across a whole
variable's live range, not a single instruction's dead-operand reload tie),
binding `*dst` to a local either before the `offset` arithmetic (regresses to
79.4%, extra live range) or as the call argument (no change), and a self-tying
`offset = offset + (int)*dst` cast (loses the implicit `u16` pointer-arithmetic
`lsls #1` scale entirely -- regresses further). Both operands are dead after
this one instruction, so reload's usual "tie to whichever operand is dead"
rule does not discriminate -- this reads as the same class of case as the
`orrs` destination chapter above ("no source form found controls it"), except
now on the LAST byte only, with the swap itself solved.

## WHICH SIDE OF THE try_match DIFF IS WHICH: `-` lines are the ROM (TARGET), `+` lines are your CANDIDATE (wave 81, W81-B)

`-` lines carry absolute labels (`_08086xxx`); `+` lines carry `<fn+off>` labels.
Misreading this direction inverts every measurement you take from the diff --
it cost W81-B two attempts on sub_0807E980 before being caught. Read one known
line and check which side it is on before reasoning about any hunk.

## SNAPSHOT BEFORE *EVERY* try_match CALL, NOT ONLY BEFORE RISKY ONES (waves 63/81, re-confirmed twice)

try_match persists whatever C it was handed into work/<fn>/<fn>.c even when
compilation fails outright -- W81-A hit this twice with a stub body, W81-D once
with a guessed draft before reading the file. A "confirmation" run of the
source you THINK is active can silently replace it with something else. Copy
the draft to work/<fn>/wNN-snapshot.c first, every time.

## THE WAVE-58 REVERSE RULE GENERALISES: what must be authored is a second local whose DEFINITIONS DISAGREE BY VALUE (wave 81, W81-C)

The measured statement "an IV initialising before the counter cannot be a giv"
is the special case. The general mechanism: if the source has a second local
that reaches a use via definitions of DIFFERENT VALUES on different paths
(e.g. `(j = idx) >= 0` else `j = -1`), copy-prop coalescing cannot remove it,
so the guard/subscript read a reload-materialised copy and the ROM shows an
extra `adds rN,rM,#0`. Every prior spelling of sub_08024720 had j provably
equal to idx and therefore missed; the disagreeing-value spelling produced the
copy on the first attempt (42.4% -> 90.2%, size-exact). When a loop pool looks
like it needs an instruction nobody authored, ask what second value flows to
that use.

## THE do_store_flag PRESET: its polarity follows the SOURCE SHAPE, and the preset lands wherever the value's production does (wave 85, W85 + orchestrator)

For `f = (call() == 0)` into a local, every FOLDED spelling -- the plain comparison, `(x == 0) ? 1 : 0`,
and `(x != 0) ? 0 : 1` -- emits the SAME preset-0 / bne-over-true-store shape. The wave-54 claim that
"agbcc presets the ELSE arm" was measured wrong: the ?: folds before the polarity is chosen. The ROM's
reversed shape -- preset-1 AFTER the call, then cmp / beq-over-false-store -- comes from the STATEMENT
form with the call result bound to a local first:

    u8 c = sub_0803CB24(q[a + i]);
    f = 1;
    if (c != 0)
        f = 0;

Two independent facts, both measured on sub_08086A58 (13.9 -> 97.6 over the wave): (1) the preset store
is scheduled ABOVE the call unless something pins the call first -- `f = 1; if ((u8)call(...) != 0)` puts
`movs r5,#1` before the `bl` and loses; the local `c` is the pin. (2) `f = 1`-then-`if` keeps the
do_store_flag expansion with the true value preset. When a comparison's preset appears on the wrong side
of a call in your diff, look for a missing local binding the call, not for a different comparison.

## HOISTING A POINTER INIT BEFORE A LOOP TO FIX THE PREHEADER ORDER FLIPS THE GIV REGISTER ASSIGNMENT (wave 85, sub_08086A58)

The ROM preheader read `ldr =pool; movs r1,#0; mov r8,r1; adds r0,#4` -- pointer load before the counter
init. Hoisting `q = base; q += 4;` above the for DOES reproduce that order -- and simultaneously flips the
k-giv from r8 to r7 and displaces n, because the extra pre-loop pseudos shift allocno numbering for
everything strength_reduce creates later. Measured twice with two different f-spellings (41.6% at worst;
the unhoisted draft was 95.2%). The two orders trade against each other: matching the preheader byte order
and keeping the loop-body register assignment were not reachable together from this spelling set. When a
preheader ORDER residual sits next to a correct loop body, expect this trade before believing a spelling
fixes both.

## A DESCENDING SOURCE COUNTER WITH ASCENDING ADDRESSES IS NOT REACHABLE BY REINDEXING (wave 85, sub_0807E980)

The ROM's tail loop keeps `movs r6,#7` (a source descending counter, init before every giv init) while
both address givs step POSITIVE (dst +0x100 before src +0x400 in the latch). Three spellings measured:
`for (j = 7; j >= 0; j--)` with j-indexed addresses fixes the counter position but folds +7*0x100 into
the inits and steps negative via pool words (+8); `(7 - j)` indexing breaks the pre-loop region; explicit
body-stepped pointer locals cost the frame (+12, first diff moves to the prologue). The implied original
shape is the pointer-variable form without the pseudo cost -- if you attempt it, the open question is
where the pointers live without adding allocnos.

## THE W83 LIVE-RANGE-SPLIT LEVER TRANSFERS TO 0 OF 5 BARE ALLOCNO TIES -- the discriminator is whether the ORIGINAL PSEUDO DIES AT THE COPY, and the tie-break is NOT the allocno number (wave 86, W86-B)

Wave 83 closed `sub_08040EF4` with a narrow copy local (`short new_var; ... new_var = y;`)
bound between two `Div` calls and used at every later y-site: it re-ranked a tied allocno
pair (y->r8, s->r9) without rotating the other three values. `src/decomp/c_08040EF4.c` is
the promoted proof. Wave 86 ran it as a controlled transfer test against five bare
allocno ties, with the mechanism pre-registered. **It transferred to none of them.**
With W84-C's earlier negative on `sub_0805A0EC` the lever now stands at 0 for 6 as a
transfer, positive only in the function it was found in.

| function | tie | placements tried | best result | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_0803F990` | force-addr base vs `(s16)i*4` | 3 | 40/664 differ, 94.0%, size-exact | 3/664, 99.5% |
| `sub_0805B6A0` | two -fforce-addr address constants | 1 | 118/160, 25.6% -- **byte-identical to baseline** | 118/160, 25.6% |
| `sub_08062C94` | r3/r4 and an r5-r7-r6 rotation | 2 | 129/348, 62.9%, size-exact | 22/348, 93.7% |
| `sub_08066874` | `cnt` vs a LICM-hoisted `2` | 1 (declaration order) | 26/428, 93.9% -- **byte-identical to baseline** | 26/428, 93.9% |
| `sub_0804DA40` | -- | n/a | **MATCHED by a TYPE change; it was never a tie** | 208/212, 21.2% |

### The mechanism in the wave-86 brief was wrong in its second half

The brief stated it as: "splitting one long-lived pseudo into two shorter ones changes
each half's priority (refs / live length) in global-alloc, **and the new pseudo's allocno
NUMBER (creation order) becomes the tie-break**", predicting that the split must be placed
so the new pseudo is created before or after the competitor's, depending on which side
must win.

The first half is right. **The second half does not reach any of these ties, and two
independent measurements say so:**

- **Declaration order of locals is byte-neutral** (`sub_08066874`). agbcc's `expand_decl`
  gives every non-addressable scalar local its pseudo at block entry, in DECLARATION
  order, before any statement is expanded. So for a source local, statement position
  cannot change its allocno number at all -- only its live range -- and declaration
  position is the only thing that can. Moving `int cnt;` ahead of `struct Unk08580934
  *state;`, nothing else changed, is byte-identical in every figure: 26 of 428, 93.9%,
  first difference +0x7.
- **Promoting a compiler temp to a source local is byte-neutral** (`sub_0805B6A0`). This
  is the strongest available form of the number lever: a local declared at block top is
  numbered ahead of EVERY temp in the function, both -fforce-addr address pseudos
  included. Binding `*a1 * 0x20` to `int n;` and using it at both index sites gives 160
  bytes, 118 differing, 25.6%, first difference +0xe -- identical to the baseline in
  every figure. The two address constants did not budge.

So `allocno_compare`'s `return v1 - v2;` tie-break is real, but by the time these ties are
decided the competitors are not separated by it. Do not spend a probe on declaration
order or on temp-to-local promotion expecting a register to move.

### What the lever actually needs: THE ORIGINAL MUST DIE AT THE COPY

Re-read the proof. In `c_08040EF4.c`, `y` is assigned once (`y = proc->unk3e & 0xff;`),
copied once (`new_var = y;`), and **never read again** -- every later site reads
`new_var`. `y` is DEAD from the copy onward, so its live range is genuinely CUT IN TWO:
one short range before the copy, one short range after. Both halves get a shorter
`live_length`, both priorities rise, and the pair re-ranks. Total live values across the
region is UNCHANGED.

In all five wave-86 attempts the copy source was still live afterwards, so nothing was
split -- a pseudo was ADDED:

- `sub_0803F990` (`j = i;`), `sub_08062C94` (`kk = k;`, `ii = i;`): the source is a LOOP
  COUNTER, which the for-increment and the exit test keep live to the bottom of the body.
  The copy cannot shorten it. Register pressure inside the loop goes up by one and
  global-alloc re-runs for the whole region.
- `sub_0805B6A0` (`n = *a1 * 0x20;`): the source is an expression, not a variable, and the
  local occupies exactly the live range the temp already had. Nothing changed at all,
  which is why this one is byte-neutral rather than worse.

**A LOOP COUNTER IS THE ONE VALUE THE SPLIT LEVER CAN NEVER BE APPLIED TO.** So is any
value read after the copy point. Before spending a probe, check that every later read of
the value goes through the copy; if the original is read again anywhere downstream, you
are adding an allocno, not splitting one, and on a loop body that is the same failure
mode as W77-B's `register asm` pin (an extra fixed register inside the loop reran global
allocation for the whole body, 664 bytes at 26.4%).

### Two ties in one function are ONE allocation, not two

`sub_08062C94` was chosen because it carries two independent-looking ties. A narrow copy
placed in the THIRD loop moved the first difference from +0x11 to +0xe -- i.e. it
perturbed the FIRST loop, upstream of the edit. The second placement, in the first loop,
took the function from 93.7% to 9.5%. Both stayed size-exact, so this is pure allocation
churn. **You cannot aim a split at one tie in a multi-tie function; global-alloc reruns
for the whole function and every tie re-rolls.**

### Corollary measured on the way: POOL ORDER AND REGISTER ASSIGNMENT ARE TWO FACTS, NOT ONE

This doc says "of two address constants used the same number of times in the same
statements, the pseudo created FIRST wins the callee-saved register ... so a misplaced
`ldr` and a swapped pair of pool words are ONE fact, not two -- never chase the pool order
directly."

On `sub_0805B6A0` they came apart. Binding `&gUnknown_030033EC` to a pointer local ahead
of the array base **did** swap the pool words into the ROM's order -- the swap that
function has wanted since wave 48 -- while the base stayed in `ip` exactly as before.
Pool order follows reference-creation order; the register follows allocno priority; they
moved independently. The "one fact" claim holds only where the two constants really do
tie on priority. Keep the advice not to chase pool order, but do not read a corrected
pool order as evidence that the register will follow.

(That spelling is otherwise a dead end there: the pointer local lets agbcc CSE
`*zp * 0xc00` and hoist it out of the loop, killing the ROM's per-iteration re-read that
W59-E proved must survive. On that function, "bind the other address first" and "keep the
re-reads" are mutually exclusive, so the axis is CLOSED, not untried.)

### And the wave's one match came from none of this: RE-DERIVE A PARK'S TWIN LIST FROM THE CONSTANTS

`sub_0804DA40` had been parked since wave 34 and was classified in wave 79 as the
canonical hopeless case: "NO SOURCE CONSTRUCT -- three values with identical reference
counts tie on allocno priority, register numbers with nothing behind them; do not give it
another budget without a NEW mechanism." It matched on the first attempt of wave 86, with
no allocation lever at all. The residual was a declared TYPE: `u32 d` had to be `u16 d`.

Two things went wrong in that park, and both are general:

1. **The oracle that pinned the wrong type was inverted.** The park argued that a u16 `d`
   promotes to signed `int` and would emit `__divsi3/__modsi3` against the ROM's
   `__udivsi3/__umodsi3`. It does not. c-typeck's `build_binary_op` sets `shorten` for
   `TRUNC_DIV_EXPR`/`TRUNC_MOD_EXPR` when operand 0 is a `NOP_EXPR` off an unsigned type
   AND operand 1 is an `INTEGER_CST` that is not all-ones -- both hold for `d / 0x38`.
   `shorten_binary_op` then performs the division in the shortened UNSIGNED type, so u16
   emits `__udivsi3` exactly as u32 does. **Both widths emit the same call, which is
   precisely why the wrong width was invisible to that oracle**: it was byte-neutral at
   the call and cost one register in the high bank. A byte-neutral difference at the place
   you are using as an oracle is not evidence about the type.
2. **The park's twin list was a record of what had been looked at, not of what is
   nearest.** It named the two address-adjacent functions and recorded that nothing in
   either transferred. The actual nearest matched relative is `sub_0804CE24`
   (`src/decomp/c_0804CE24.c`): same prototype, same `sub_0801566C` readout, the same
   `0x38` divisor and the same `0x700` stride, differing only in the `gUnknown_02029668`
   column and the VRAM base -- and matched with `u16 d` the whole time. It sits 0xC1C
   bytes away, so no adjacency screen finds it.

**Re-derive a park's twin list from the CONSTANTS -- divisor, stride, destination base,
callee -- not from the address neighbourhood, and not from the list the park wrote down.**
This is the wave-77 grep-the-tree rule with a sharper handle on it: the older the park,
the more likely the answer arrived in a promoted file after the twin list was written.

## The W56-F insn-count lever: only SAME-DIRECTION shift-of-shift survives to gcse, and the reachable set is tiny (wave 86, W86-A)

W56-F established that spill-slot ORDER is set by gcse PRE's expression hash
table, whose size is `max_cuid / 4`, so **the lever is the pre-allocation insn
count** and `(w >> 2) >> 1` works by adding one insn that `combine` folds back.
Wave 86 ran that lever to exhaustion on `sub_080627F4` -- 38 spellings, three
sweeps -- and the result is two rules, one enabling and one limiting.

**Which fold-backs actually reach gcse.** `cse_main` finishes with
`delete_trivially_dead_insns`, and `fold` collapses most reassociation at parse
time, so nearly every "add one insn" trick is gone before `max_cuid` is taken.
Measured on one function, all byte-identical to the control:

- `(a << 1) >> 1` and `((a << 1) >> 1 >> 1) >> 1` -- **fold before gcse**
- `(t * 0x20) << 1`, `(t << 5) << 1` -- MULT/LSHIFT reassociation, folded
- `t * 0x40 + 0x20 + 0x20`, `0x40 + t * 0x40`, `t * 0x40 + 0x3f + 1` -- folded
- `((g >> t) & 3) & 1` -- mask merging, folded
- every address-scaling respelling of `&g[u]` (`g + u`, `&g[0] + u`,
  `(T *)((u8 *)g + u * sizeof (T))`) -- folded
- a DEAD statement of any form -- deleted by `delete_trivially_dead_insns`,
  which is why wave 74's six dead-assignment variants were all byte-identical

**What survives is a right-shift of a right-shift -- shift-of-shift in the SAME
direction.** `(a >> 1) >> 1` for `a >> 2` is the only reliable +1. W84-B had
guessed the discriminator was signed-vs-unsigned (its `u32 v >> 2` split folded
while the `int` ones did not); it is not. The discriminator is **direction**:
same-direction pairs survive, opposite-direction pairs (`<<` then `>>`) fold.

**The limiting rule, and it is the important one.** The number of foldable
sites bounds the number of insn counts you can reach, and therefore the number
of slot layouts. `sub_080627F4` has exactly TWO `>> 2` sites, giving counts
+0, +1, +2 -- and +0 and +1 produce the same layout, so the whole lever reaches
**two of the six** permutations of its three spilled pseudos. Neither is the
ROM's. So before spending a wave on this lever, **count the same-direction
shift sites in the function**: with fewer than three you cannot sweep the table
size, and a negative result is a property of the source, not of the hypothesis.

**Read the residual as an ORDER, not as a set of swaps.** Slot offsets rise in
allocation order, so `{0x10, 0x14, 0x18}` is a permutation. On `sub_080627F4`
the ROM's order is RTL creation order (loop init, counter, loop test), the
0/1-split candidate is that order exactly REVERSED, and the 2-split candidate
is a transposition of the last two. Three parked notes on this function had
each described the residual as "a pair swap" and two of the three named the
wrong pair; decoding it as a permutation of an ordered list settles it in one
reading.

## Cheap harness: N spellings as N functions in ONE unit, scored off the `.s` (wave 86, W86-A)

`tools/permute.py` normalises `[sp, #N]` immediates away, so a residual made
entirely of stack slots scores 0 and the search never runs (wave 60 found this
on `sub_080627F4`). The same is nearly true of a residual made of two register
numbers. Both are cheap to sweep by hand with this pattern, which wave 86 used
for 53 spellings across three functions at a cost of five compiles and **zero**
`try_match` attempts:

1. Wrap the function body in a `#define BODY(NAME, ...)` macro, or textually
   rename the function N times, so one translation unit holds N variants under
   N different names. gcse and reload run per function, so the variants do not
   interfere.
2. Compile it with `agbenv.flags(<the real function name>)` so the unit gets
   the function's own configured profile and any override.
3. Parse the `.s` per function label and extract the signature that
   discriminates the residual -- for a stack-slot residual the ordered list of
   `[sp, #N]` operands; for a register residual the instruction neighbourhood
   of the differing site; for a pressure residual the frame directive, the
   `mov ip/sl/sb, rN` set and the count of a rematerialised immediate.
4. Compare against the same signature extracted from `work/<fn>/target.s`.

Two practical notes. `compile_probe` writes the same `.s` to
`build/probe/<stem>.s`, so its output can be read from disk instead of being
returned -- what it returns is capped at 400 lines and on a large function
those 400 lines are `.debug_abbrev`, not code. And when calibrating offsets
against `target.s`, do not assume 2 bytes per THUMB instruction: anchor the
listing on a known differing byte instead. Wave 86's first calibration on
`sub_0805A0EC` was 4 bytes out and made `r3` look live where it was dead.

## A constant local pins a register by its live-range START, not by existing (wave 86, W86-A)

On `sub_0805A0EC` the residual is two bytes: the ROM stores the zero from `r0`,
the draft from `r3`. The draft binds `int new_var3 = 0;` before the guards.
Four spellings, one unit, read off the `.s`:

    ROM        : ldr r1,[r0] | movs r0,#0 | strh r0,[r5,#2] | mov r2, ip | ldrh r0,[r2]
    zero local bound BEFORE the guards : mov r3,#0 | strh r3 | mov r2, ip
    literal `0`                        : mov r0,#0 | strh r0 | mov r3, ip
    zero local bound just BEFORE the store : mov r0,#0 | strh r0 | mov r3, ip
    literal + a later-dead extra local     : mov r0,#0 | strh r0 | mov r3, ip

**A zero local assigned immediately before its use compiles byte-identically to
the literal.** Only a live range that starts early enough to span other
computation gets an allocno that holds a hard register. So "literal" and
"late-bound local" are the SAME experiment, not two axes -- several parked
entries in this tree list them separately and thereby double-count one
measurement.

The second half is a warning about reading these residuals. The park had
recorded "the ROM has the zero in r0 AND something live in r3 across the
store". Tracing r3 on the calibrated listing refutes it: r3 holds `props + off`
and dies two guards earlier, and is next *written* 0x24 bytes after the store.
Both r2 and r3 are free in the ROM at that point. The real structure is a
**two-way trade** -- occupying r3 with the zero buys the correct `mov r2, ip`
scratch and loses the zero's register, and freeing r3 buys the zero's register
and loses the scratch. Both spellings are two bytes. **When two spellings of
one construct give equal-sized residuals at different offsets, write it down as
a trade; a park that names only one of the two halves reads like an unfinished
search when the search is actually complete.**

## CONSTANT-DERIVED TWINS SUPPLIED A NEW CONSTRUCT FOR 1 OF 5 PARKS, AND THE ONE THAT LANDED WAS A MIRROR FUNCTION — SCREEN ON INVERSE SHAPE, NOT ON OVERLAP SCORE (wave 86, W86-D)

W86-B proposed an axis mid-wave: **re-derive a park's twin list from the
CONSTANTS and CALLEES, not from the address neighbourhood.** Per the wave-59
rule it was tested in the same wave. The orchestrator ran an IDF-weighted
screen over `asm/*.s` (rare callees + rare immediates + non-address pool
words) and handed five parked functions their top matched relative. Result:

| target | twin | screen basis | verdict | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_08016F38` | `sub_08017208` | 2 callees, imm 0xba/0xbb/0xc4 | YES | **MATCHED, first probe** |
| `sub_0804A760` | `sub_0804A260` | 2 callees, imm 0x5d/0x5f/0x63 | no (already cited) | refuted, +4 -> +10 |
| `sub_08084C14` | `sub_080849C8` | **SIX** callees + imm 0xab | YES | refuted, size-exact -> +32 |
| `sub_0805DCD4` | `sub_0805E87C` | 3 callees, imm 0x79 | YES | refuted, -4 -> -8 |
| `sub_0805D888` | `sub_0805E440` | 3 callees | NO | clean NO, no probe |

**1 of 5. The axis works, but the screen's own score does not rank it.** The
pair with the STRONGEST overlap on the list — six shared callees, a
character-for-character shared `unk01 == 2 ? sub_0802490C(...) :
sub_080248F8()` idiom — produced the worst regression of the batch. The pair
that converted shared only two callees.

### What actually predicted the hit: the twin was the INVERSE function

`sub_08016F38` is the SAVE routine and `sub_08017208` the LOAD routine for one
`struct SaveBlk` / `struct Map`. Same plane loop, same `unk417a[x] + y` index,
same `gUnknown_03003F68 + 2` access, same sentinel `unk0bb8[]` replay, same
three trailing copy loops — with source and destination exchanged. The load
side had been matched in wave 80 by the W77-K offset lever, and the save side
had been parked at 3 bytes since wave 74 with **five separate agents (W74,
W77-M, W81-A, W82-A, W84) classifying the residual as a bare commutation tie
with no source lever.** It had a source lever. It was written down in the
mirror, and the whole transplant was one statement:

    idx = ...unk417a[x] + y;
    off = idx * 2;                                     /* <-- the lever */
    ...unk0a22[idx] != *(u16 *)((u8 *)gUnknown_03003F68 + off + 2)

Binding the byte offset as its own statement creates the index chain's pseudo
BEFORE the pool constant and the base load, so the chain takes r1 and the
constants r0 — the exact r0/r1 exchange that was the residual.

**And the near-miss is the trap.** `sub_08016F38`'s park had explicitly ruled
out `*(u16 *)((u8 *)g + idx*2 + 2)` — the INLINE form — as byte-neutral. That
is precisely the spelling wave 53 measured on the twin and called "not
reachable from the source here" before wave 80 overturned it with the
statement split. **A park that rules out the inline form of a lever has not
tested the lever.** Grep your park's ruled-out list for the inline sibling of
any statement-split construct before believing the axis is closed.

### So: screen on INVERSE / MIRROR shape, not on shared-callee count

Save/load, serialise/deserialise, install/remove, push/pop, encode/decode.
A mirror pair shares the whole statement skeleton, so a lever found on one
side transplants literally. A vocabulary neighbour shares callees and
immediates and nothing else, and the four misses here were all of that kind:
same subsystem, same globals, different shape (352B and 364B single scans
against a 740B two-scan search; a 520B straight-line init against an 816B
jump-table key handler). **Classify the pair before spending the probe** —
"true shape twin / same-vocabulary neighbour / unrelated" is a cheap call and
it was 5-for-5 predictive here.

### Three mechanism results from the refutations, each worth keeping

1. **The `*(T *)&p->m` alias lever is FUNCTION-SCOPE and all-or-nothing.**
   c_0804A260.c documents that a bare pointer-cast MEM is not
   `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P`, aliases the global pointer, and forces a reload where a
   cast through a struct does not. Read backwards on `sub_0804A760` — whose
   ROM reloads where the draft hoists — it is true but unusable: introducing
   the alias in a do-while body killed PRE's hoist for the POST-loop switch as
   well, and those four arms each paid a reload. +4 became +10. **There is no
   way to scope this lever to one loop.** Corrected reading of that park: the
   ROM has no hoist at all, reloading per arm and once more after the loop.

2. **A `register asm` pin is not a neutral experiment when the parameter is
   competing for callee-saved registers.** On `sub_08084C14`, pinning the
   shared constant 1 to r8 (copying c_080849C8.c's `savedParent asm("r9")`,
   which was that function's whole match) forced a `mov rLOW, r8` at EVERY
   store where the ROM spends ONE, and reserving r8 displaced the parameter
   from r7 to r6. Size-exact 816/816 became +32. It also refutes the wave-54
   park's wording: **"the shared constant 1 ... out of r8" does not mean the
   ROM holds 1 in r8 across the arms** — if it did, the pin would have
   reproduced the single `mov`.

3. **Binding a base to a local REDUCES register pressure — stop using it to
   add pressure.** `sub_0805DCD4`'s header asks for "one more value live
   across the second loop so that sl is not free". Binding the 0x376A plane
   base took -4 to -8 and 47.6% to 41.9%, because the bound pointer collapses
   two re-spelled member accesses into one register. Second independent
   measurement of the direction (W66-M got it on the +0x12 base). An extra
   live value has to come from a value genuinely USED twice, never from an
   alias of one used once.

### One process finding

The wave-86 prompts asserted, per function, that the screen's top relative was
"NOT named anywhere in their park entry or draft". **That was false for 1 of
5**: `sub_0804A760`'s active draft cites `c_0804A260.c` by name at its own
struct definition and had already imported that file's view struct. A screen
that reports novelty should diff against the draft text, not only against
`parked.json`.

## TWO EXTENSIONS OF ONE VALUE OFF ONE `lsls` MEANS TWO SOURCE LOCALS, NOT ONE LOCAL WITH AN EXOTIC WIDTH (wave 86, W86-C)

`sub_080193B0` sat parked for 54 waves on this shape, and the whole park was a
search in the wrong space.

The ROM keeps two extensions of a narrow-returning call's result off a
**single** `lsls`:

```
lsls r0, r0, #0x10
lsrs r2, r0, #0x10      <- zero-extended home
asrs r0, r0, #0x10      <- sign-extended home
```

and then re-derives the array subscript by SIGN-extending the zero-extended
copy (`lsls r0,r2,#0x10 ; asrs r0,r0,#0x10`). The `== -1` test reads the
sign-extended home; every subscript reads the other.

**That is two locals:**

```c
s16 r;
u16 idx;
r = sub_08019290(NULL);   /* asrs -- read by the test        */
idx = r;                  /* lsrs -- read by every subscript */
if (r == -1) return NULL;
gUnknown_0200C528[(s16)idx]. ...
```

Both narrowings apply to the SAME SImode call result, so cse shares the one
`x << 16` between them -- which is why there is one `lsls` and two extensions
rather than two shift pairs. `idx = r` is enough on its own: combine folds
`zero_extend (truncate (sign_extend x))` back to `zero_extend (truncate x)`,
so the second `lsls` the naive reading expects never appears.

**Why the one-variable search could never work.** Wave 32 tried `s16 i`, then
`u16 i` with `(s16)i` at both uses, then retyping the callee's return to
defeat gcc's knowledge that the value is already narrow. One variable has
exactly one home, so no spelling of it can produce two, and combine is right
to delete whichever extension is redundant. Nothing had to be defeated: with
two locals the two values are genuinely different and neither is redundant.

**This also refutes a plausible wave-86 hypothesis, so do not re-run it:** the
surviving zero-extension is NOT `nonzero_bits` failing on a multi-set pseudo
(wave 57). `idx` is single-set in the matching source.

**Read it as the general diagnostic.** W80-F gave "same register, different
block = ONE variable". The converse holds too and is worth as much: **two
registers holding differently-extended views of one computed value, live at
the same time, means two source locals.** Before spending a wave on widths and
casts, count the homes.

## AN ARRAY BASE AND A SCALAR-STRUCT BASE PUT A CONSTANT MEMBER OFFSET IN DIFFERENT PLACES (wave 86, W86-C)

Controlled probe, identical address arithmetic in both arms -- a constant 4
plus a variable `m * 2`, feeding a THUMB `ldrsh` (which has no immediate form,
so it needs an index register either way):

```
ARRAY   gUnknown_085643B0[0][1][m]
        ldr r2,=sym / ... / lsl r0,r0,#1 / adds r2,#4 / adds r0,r0,r2 /
        movs r1,#0 / ldrsh r0,[r0,r1]                       (4 insns)

STRUCT  gUnknown_085643A8.unk04[m]
        ldr r3,=sym / ... / lsl r0,r0,#1 / adds r0,r0,r3 /
        movs r1,#4 / ldrsh r0,[r0,r1]                       (3 insns)
```

**Mechanism.** `-fforce-addr` FORCE_REGs an ARRAY's address **bare** at the
subscript, so any constant offset applied afterwards has to be a runtime add
on that register and the `ldrsh` indexes with zero. A scalar struct is never
subscripted, nothing forces its address first, so the address of a member
stays a link-time constant and folds -- into the `ldrsh` index (the plain and
pointer spellings) or into the pool word's relocation (a `const s16 *p =
g.unk04;` local, and a cast of the symbol's address to a pointer-to-array).
Those are the only two places agbcc will put it.

**So `adds rBASE,#k` with a zero `ldrsh` index is a TYPE tell, not an
expression-shape tell.** If the ROM has it and your candidate does not, the
global is declared as a struct and it is an array. `sub_08053520` was parked
at 84.9% for four waves on exactly this: its first half already matched
because that base (`gUnknown_085D6C88`) is an array, and its second half was
one instruction short because that base was modelled as a struct. Retyping
`gUnknown_085643A8` to `const s16 [][2]` and writing `g[1][m]` matched it
byte-for-byte with no other change.

**Two corrections that come with it:**

- The `unknown-globals.h` comment on that symbol asserted the exact opposite
  ("which only a struct member array gives") and three waves of probes were
  run against it. It had generalised from a `const s16 *p = g.unk04;` local --
  a POINTER TO THE MEMBER, a different construct from a 2-D array with a
  constant outer index, and one that really does sink the 4 into the
  relocation. **A type comment that reasons from a pointer-to-member is not
  evidence about an array subscript.**
- Wave 51's note that cse const-propagates a `struct T *q = &g;` local back to
  the symbol is WRONG as stated. Declared at function top, `q` survives cse
  intact: the pool word stays the bare symbol and the pointer lives in a
  callee-saved register across the merge. Two definitions change nothing,
  because there was nothing to defeat. What is true is only the conclusion --
  the member offset still folds into the `ldrsh` index, so a pointer is not
  the lever either.

## A GOTO LOOP REPRODUCES AN UNROTATED SEARCH LOOP, AND ITS STRIDES MUST BE EXPLICIT SOURCE VARIABLES (wave 86, W86-C)

W46-B's chapter says a goto loop is invisible to loop.c. `sub_08073228`'s
inner search is the worked confirmation, and it settles three parked facts at
once.

The park listed three defects and predicted they would move together: the ROM
was UNROTATED (exit test at the top, unconditional `b` at the bottom), it
compared with the searched-for character on the LEFT, and it strength-reduced
`j * 8` to `adds r4,#8`. Wave 46 tried `while (tbl[j].unk00 != c) j++;`, a
`for (;;)` with an `if (...) break;`, and the same `for (;;)` with a leading
`k = j * 8;`. **All three rotate**, because every `for`/`while` emits
`NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG` and jump.c's `duplicate_loop_exit_test` then moves the
test to the bottom.

```c
k = j * 8;
p = (const u8 *)gUnknown_08614024 + k;
_search:
    if (c == *p) goto _found;
    k += 8; p += 8; j++;
    goto _search;
_found:
```

emits the ROM's body instruction for instruction: unrotated, `cmp` with `c`
on the left, three explicit `+8`/`+8`/`+1` steps, `b` at the bottom. **One
construct, three parked facts.**

**The cost, and it is the thing to plan for.** loop.c is not there to invent
the element-pointer giv, so the pointer must be an explicit source local --
one more pseudo than the for-loop version hands the allocator. On
`sub_08073228` that is exactly what the residual became: the first parameter
takes the callee-saved `sl` instead of spilling to `[sp,#0]`, and the frame
comes out 0x1c against the ROM's 0x20. **Expect a goto loop to buy the loop's
shape and spend a register doing it.**

**And the dead copy at the ROM's loop top cannot be authored.** The ROM has a
dead `adds r0,r4,#0` ahead of the exit test, which reads like a source
statement. It is not reachable from C: written as `m = k;` with `m` unused,
flow deletes it (W80-F: a dead copy is a no-op); written as `m = k;` with `m`
used after the loop, `m` coalesces with `k` and the copy is deleted again --
byte-identical output in both cases, measured.

## THE SECOND DELAY LEVER: BIND THE WHOLE INDEX TO ITS OWN LOCAL BEFORE THE REFERENCE (wave 86, W86-C)

W73-H sorted this project's allocno levers by DIRECTION and concluded that
five of six move a reference EARLIER, that only byte-offset-first moves one
LATER, and that that one is welded to an index reassociation. On the strength
of it `sub_0804C5A4` was recorded as CONFIRMED IMMOVABLE with an empty axis
list. **The conclusion was wrong; there is a second delay lever.**

`-fforce-addr` emits the FORCE_REG of an array's address when the ARRAY_REF is
expanded, which is BEFORE its index subtree. That is why a base address
constant can be loaded a dozen instructions ahead of its use. So:

> **Bind the whole index expression to its own local, in the ROM's own term
> order, in a statement BEFORE the reference, then write the access with the
> base added to that local.**

Once the index is a live pseudo from an earlier statement, the only thing left
to expand at the reference is the base load and one add, so the load lands at
the point of use.

```c
off = (g[side].unk1a & 1) * 2 + (h[side][2] - 1) * 4 + h[side][1] * 24;
f(*(const s16 *)((const u8 *)gUnknown_085D6C94 + off));
```

`sub_0804C5A4`: 86.9% -> 99.4%, size-exact, twelve instructions of
displacement gone, the 0x12c/0x130 pool pair now in the ROM's order with no
anchor. W73-E's byte-offset-first spelling had failed at this same function
because it reassociated the index INLINE, costing +8 bytes and a spill;
**doing the identical reassociation as its own STATEMENT costs nothing** --
the `adds r0,#4` / `adds r2,#2` reuse of one base register survives.

**But position and register TRADE, so read this before spending probes on the
remainder.** The same function's last two bytes are one register, and the two
halves of the answer live in different spellings:

- **index local DEAD** (the array spelling kept, the sum written only as a
  dead statement -- W80-B's form): the base load takes the ROM's register
  (r2), but lands ONE instruction early, because the index's final add then
  belongs to the array-ref expansion rather than to the dead statement.
- **index local LIVE**: the final add belongs to the index statement, so the
  load lands in the ROM's position -- but takes r0.

Neither `u32` for the local, nor putting the base as operand 1, nor a comma
assignment binding the base to a pointer first, nor materialising the pointer
in its own statement, nor binding the loaded value to a local before the call,
nor spelling the base as the address of its first element moves the register.
Same family as wave 85's "hoisting a pointer init before a loop FLIPS the giv
register assignment -- the two orders trade, they do not compose."

## A SHAPE TWIN ONLY TRANSPLANTS A LEVER IF IT CONTAINS THE RESIDUAL'S CONSTRUCT, SOLVED — SHARING A SKELETON IS NOT ENOUGH (wave 86, W86-E)

Second half of the twin axis W86-B proposed and W86-D opened (see the previous
chapter). W86-E was handed five more parks screened a different way: **Jaccard
over `data_refs` union non-hub callees**, constrained to comparable size
(0.5–2x) and the same loop count (±2), taking the top-ranked matched relative
that is named nowhere in the park or the draft.

| target | twin | pair class | untried construct? | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_08020EDC` | `sub_08020DBC` | true shape twin | YES — `int rowOff = 0x417a` + `int new_var2 = 0x13` | 90.7% -> **89.4%**, first difference unmoved |
| `sub_0801ECE8` | `sub_0801E8D8` | true shape twin (J=1.00) | YES (weak) — constant-first operand order | refuted, output unchanged (0 `try_match`) |
| `sub_08045FC8` | `sub_080853B0` | same-vocabulary neighbour | NO — killed by the target's own ROM | clean NO, 0 probes |
| `sub_0804F18C` | `sub_0804EEFC` | true shape twin | YES — `<< 3` / `* 0x100` **both inverted** | 34.4% -> 14.0%, -20 -> -12 bytes |
| `sub_0804F658` | `sub_0804EEFC` | true shape twin | YES — same | 31.4% -> **38.2%**, -8 -> +12 bytes |

**0 of 5 converted; 4 of 5 yielded a genuinely untried construct.** Across both
halves of the wave the axis stands at **1 of 10**. The screen is good at
finding untried source constructs and poor at converting parks, which is a
different result from "the screen does not work" and should be read as such.

### The refinement: same-direction twins supply constructs, not levers

W86-D's rule was "screen on INVERSE / MIRROR shape, not on shared-callee
count", from one save/load pair that converted. W86-E's four true shape twins
were all **same-direction** twins — a smaller, simpler sibling doing the same
job in the same direction, not an inverse — and none converted. The mechanism
